By work of Appleby--Flammia--Kopp and Radchenko--Wheeler, ghost SICs, which satisfy the SIC equations with Hermiticity up to parity, exist unconditionally for dge4. We study the passage from ghosts to SICs. We compute all isolated points of the complexified SIC variety for d=4,5,6; exactly half are SICs. We prove that no symmetry of the SIC equations maps a ghost to a SIC, so the step is purely arithmetic, and that a SIC exists in dimension d whenever the ghost overlap units satisfy a place law: each Galois conjugate is real or unimodular according to the infinite place of the real quadratic field F below it. If the unit field is abelian over F, the place law is the Stark relation c₋₌κ; equivalently, a Galois conjugate of an associated near-group fusion category is unitary exactly when it is pseudo-unitary. For d a power of a prime pequiv5±od 6 or of 3, an infinite family, we prove that under the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture c₋₌κ is equivalent to the triviality of κ on the Hilbert-class-field part of the unit field. That condition involves no complex conjugation, and it follows from a sign-free multiplet hypothesis. We state an explicit GL₂ reciprocity law for the squared ghost overlaps that implies c₋₌κ, and we prove it for the computed algebraic overlaps in d=5,7,11,15 by Artin reciprocity and a check in every ray class. Zauner's conjecture remains open: the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture and the multiplet hypothesis are not proved here.
authors: Hassan Khodaiemehr

articles.title: Access Resources and Stability of Error-Correction Capabilities in Continuous Strategic Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous quantum error correction depends on which parts of a measurement record remain available to the controller at recovery. We study this temporal access using continuous strategic codes, formulated as open continuous process tensors contracted with causal instruments and conditional recovery. For monitored stabilizer codes, a common-optimal-correction criterion identifies when records can be merged without loss and yields a factorization for separated CSS inference. Terminal decision labels and causal persistent memory carry different costs: five persistent classical states reach the complete-record optimum in a finite-strength counting model, whereas its two-window diffusive counterpart has nine terminal decision labels and requires unbounded memory for exact causal recovery. Uniform lower and constructive upper bounds establish an optimal fidelity deficit of order m⁻² for m persistent states in the diffusive model. Counting and diffusive stability bounds translate open-process approximation into guarantees for deployed-controller performance and retained access advantages, quantified by explicit quantizers and model-mismatch curves. The same process--instrument framework connects storage with persistent environments and irreversible noise to spacetime interrogation and record-selected paths for a logical T gate. These results specify which record distinctions recovery needs, the memory cost of approximating them, and the logical protection retained under model error.
authors: He Wang

articles.title: Decoherence suppression in quantum dense coding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By harnessing entanglement to transmit information beyond the limits of classical communication, quantum dense coding serves as a key component in various quantum technologies. However, in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, noise-induced decoherence poses inevitable challenges to its practical implementation. By investigating the non-Markovian decoherence dynamics of the two categories of quantum dense coding protocols realized in discrete- and continuous-variable systems, we demonstrate a physical mechanism to suppress the decoherence in quantum dense coding. It is found that the formation of a bound state in the energy spectrum of the entire system consisting of each subsystem and its local environment of the quantum channel restores the quantum advantage of dense coding in the presence of decoherence. Refreshing our understanding on the noisy effect on quantum dense coding, our finding offers a guide toward the practical realization of noise-tolerant quantum dense coding.
authors: Xi Yan, Wen-Jie Zhang, Jun-Hong An

articles.title: Mitigating sloppiness with intermediate controls in sequential multiparameter spin interferometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparameter quantum sensing requires different parameters to produce distinguishable probe responses while allowing their information to be extracted simultaneously. In sequential sensing without intermediate control, two phases encoded through the same generator are locally indistinguishable. Here we show that parameter-independent intermediate controls overcome this limitation in a collective-spin interferometer by separating the corresponding effective generators in the probe covariance geometry. Specifically, a transverse collective rotation provides an analytically tractable realization, and intermediate one-axis twisting (OAT) generates additional nonlinear operator directions and a broad regime of enhanced joint estimation. For fixed total particle number N and matched twisting resource, both marginal precision bounds lie below those of a separated-OAT strategy while measurement incompatibility remains weak. For intermediate OAT, conditional optimization of an upper bound on the Holevo cost yields asymptotic N⁻² scaling. For this protocol, a fixed rotated-Dicke measurement retains simultaneous two-parameter enhancement over a broad phase region. These results show that nonlinear intermediate control can mitigate sloppiness while preserving quantum-enhanced precision with a common readout.
authors: Hai Feng, Xinwei Li, Rong Lu, Li You

articles.title: Tensor Contraction with ZX Calculus, a Graph-Theoretic Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensors are higher dimensional generalisations of vectors and matrices. Tensor networks are a diagrammatic representation of complicated relations between tensors, and tensor contraction is the evaluation of a tensor network analogous to matrix multiplication. Tensor networks and tensor contraction are ubiquitous in computer science, physics, and applied mathematics. Most existing tensor contraction algorithms are focused on finding an optimal contraction order of the tensors' bonds. However, finding the optimal order is an NP-hard problem. It is equivalent to another possibly more straightforward but still NP-hard problem of finding the treewidth of the line graph of the tensor network. While in general finding the optimal bond-by-bond contraction order is hard, in many practical cases there is no need to find an optimal order. This observation leads to the core innovation of this thesis, which is a new tensor contraction paradigm that uses graph theoretic operations to produce an equivalent tensor network whose line graph has lower treewidth than the original tensor network, before applying the bond-by-bond contraction algorithm. We call these graph theoretical operations rewrite preprocessing, and we name the algorithms that apply rewrite preprocessing before regular bond-by-bond contraction Tensor Contraction with Graph Operation. There are many possible ways to perform rewrite preprocessing; in this thesis, we focus on the graph operations of ZX calculus, a diagrammatic language for quantum circuits. Ample numerical simulations have been performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.
authors: Yuhao Han

articles.title: Quantum Path Finder: Navigating Constraint Space via Non-Abelian Gauge Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum algorithms are commonly designed within the circuit paradigm or through adiabatic evolution. Here we introduce emphQuantum Path Finder (QPF), a distinct algorithm-design paradigm based on non-Abelian gauge dynamics in a constraint-protected degenerate manifold. Each Boolean variable is promoted to a qutrit whose additional state represents an unassigned variable. The problem Hamiltonian then defines a connected manifold of feasible partial assignments, and time-dependent local qutrit rotations generate coherent transport on this manifold. Unlike conventional adiabatic quantum computation, QPF does not require the state to follow an instantaneous eigenstate along a prescribed interpolation: adiabaticity with respect to the constraint gap protects the feasible manifold, while adiabatic following within that manifold is optional. The algorithmic task is therefore to design paths and interference in constraint space rather than only to engineer a sequence of gates or a ground-state interpolation. We illustrate the framework with three applications. For unstructured search, a two-level analysis and numerical evolution recover Grover-type scaling under explicitly stated assumptions. For complete 3-XORSAT, the accessible gauge sector has a size-independent gap, in contrast to the exponentially closing gap of a conventional transverse-field adiabatic path. For satisfiable 3-SAT instances, finite-size benchmarks demonstrate high satisfied-clause fractions at short classical comparison budgets, without claiming an equal-cost quantum advantage. We also outline a superconducting-qutrit implementation and discuss the conceptual relationship between QPF and nondeterministic Turing machine.
authors: Chunyin Chen, Biao Wu

articles.title: Classical and Quantum Dynamics in State Space: Projective Hilbert Space, Measurement, and Classical Emergence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric formulation of classical and quantum dynamics in which projective Hilbert space is taken as the primary state space and classical configuration and phase spaces arise as submanifolds of localized quantum states. The Fubini-Study metric induces the Euclidean metric on these submanifolds, while the tangential component of Schrödinger evolution reproduces Hamiltonian and Newtonian dynamics. We then extend the construction to stochastic motion. Brownian dynamics on the localized classical manifold is lifted to a common stochastic unitary evolution in projective Hilbert space; under homogeneity, isotropy, and independence assumptions, the corresponding Hermitian increments have Gaussian Unitary Ensemble statistics. This yields a random-matrix Schrödinger dynamics whose transition probabilities depend only on Fubini-Study distance. Through the embedding of localized states, the classical Gaussian transition law becomes the Born rule in projective state space. Measurement outcomes are identified with first arrival at detector-defined finite-resolution equivalence classes, while each realized state-space evolution remains linear and unitary. The framework is applied to classical emergence, macroscopic stabilization, double-slit experiments, composite systems, and entangled states. A spatially local Caldeira-Leggett-type system-environment model is also shown, under explicit thermal, symmetry, Ohmic, and coarse-graining assumptions, to generate the Brownian family required by the stochastic lift. The remaining open problem is to establish the range and universality of this mechanism for realistic many-body measuring environments.
authors: Alexey A. Kryukov

articles.title: Quantum teleportation using photon-added two-mode squeezed Fock states: A comparison with photon-subtracted counterparts
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum state engineering frequently employs non-Gaussian operations, particularly photon addition and subtraction, to tailor and improve the nonclassical characteristics of quantum states. We investigate how photon addition to a two-mode squeezed Fock state (TMSFS) influences its performance in the Braunstein-Kimble quantum teleportation protocol. We obtain the Wigner characteristic function of the photon-added TMSFS (PA-TMSFS) and evaluate the corresponding teleportation fidelities for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian input states. We further compare the teleportation performance of PA-TMSFS with that of its photon-subtracted counterpart by accessing their fidelity enhancements over the parent TMSFS and considering the probabilistic nature of both the operations. Our results demonstrate that photon subtraction provides superior teleportation performance compared with photon addition, with this advantage becoming more pronounced when the success probabilities of the corresponding non-Gaussian operations are considered. In particular, the symmetric (1,1) photon subtraction yields the optimal trade-off between teleportation fidelity and success probability among the configurations investigated. These findings highlight that photon subtraction retains its advantage even when the underlying entangled resource is already non-Gaussian.
authors: Ankita Panghal, Arpita Chatterjee

articles.title: Single-port homodyne detection achieves optimal multiphase sensing in an n-port ring cavity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating several phases simultaneously is more than estimating them one at a time: the optimal measurements for different parameters may not commute, and in a multiparameter problem the quantum Cramér-Rao bound is not automatically achievable. Ring cavities are a natural setting for this question, since a single coherent input can be made to interact repeatedly with every internal phase before it is read out. We study the simultaneous local estimation of the n internal phases of a lossless n-port ring cavity probed by a fixed-energy multimode coherent state, optimizing over the full coherent-input space and over the operating point of the cavity. We identify a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimum: the input energy should be distributed equally among the ports, and the internal phases and input phases satisfy a simple phase-matching condition for every port. The optimum is unique up to a common optical phase and minimizes both the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) cost and the sloppiness of the model. At this point the quantum Fisher information matrix is full rank and its spectrum is obtained in closed form, the Uhlmann curvature vanishes, and no incompatibility penalty has to be paid. The precision retains the coherent-state scaling and the dependence on the number of phases, but the cavity feedback reduces the prefactor relative to n independent single-pass experiments. Finally, we show that this bound may be achieved in practice: the Fisher information of a balanced homodyne measurement at each output port, with local-oscillator phases locked to the prepared input phases is equal to the optimal quantum Fisher information. Our results establish the ring cavity as a platform for optimal multiphase sensing and provide the ultimate benchmark against which nonclassical probes may be evaluated for further precision enhancement.
authors: Jiayu He, Aviral Kumar Pandey, Krishna Mohan Mishra, Devendra Kumar Mishra, Matteo G. A. Paris

articles.title: Towards Optimal Routing Strategies for qLDPC codes on Silicon Spin Qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One of the major challenges of implementing high-rate quantum error correction codes, like qLDPC codes, is realizing the required long-range interactions. Spin qubit platforms can provide this connectivity by shuttling qubits next to each other whenever they need to interact. When doing this, the performance of the code depends on the shuttling strategy. We study memory experiments of the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle (Gross) code on two shuttling grids for future spin qubit devices: a square grid and a square grid with diagonals. We compare three shuttling strategies, structured and random initial layouts, and a range of shuttling noise models spanning best- and worst-case scenarios. The best strategy minimizes the longest distance travelled rather than the total distance. The initial layout has only a weak effect, whereas adding diagonals to the grid reduces the logical error rate by up to two orders of magnitude which may have implications for future hardware design.
authors: Merlin Incerti-Medici, Minh T. P. Nguyen, Stefano Bosco, James R. Wootton, Daniel Bultrini

articles.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.
authors: Vincent P. Iglesias-Cardinale, Shreekanth S. Yuvarajan, Herbert F. Fotso

articles.title: Belief Propagation-Informed Tesseract Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum error correction, the decoder must estimate the errors from the measurement data accurately and fast enough to avoid a backlog. Search-based decoders such as Tesseract achieve high accuracy by finding a minimum-weight set of error events with an A* search, but their search effort grows rapidly with the physical error rate and the code size. To reduce this search effort while maintaining a logical error rate close to that of Tesseract, we propose a belief propagation (BP)-guided modification of the Tesseract decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Damped sum-product BP is applied to the triggered detectors before the Tesseract search. If the detectors triggered by the BP hard decision match the triggered detectors, this hard decision is accepted directly, and the Tesseract search is skipped. Otherwise, the BP marginal probability estimates, weighted by a trust coefficient, modify the search priority, while the path cost keeps the channel-prior weights so that the decoding objective is unchanged. The framework also supports BP-based initialization, in which selected BP decisions form the starting point of a residual search whose signed-cost objective allows incorrect initial decisions to be removed. A node-exploration limit bounds this residual search; if the limit is reached, the decoder falls back to the BP-guided search on the original triggered detector set. The method is evaluated on the [[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], and [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle codes under circuit-level noise. With BP-based initialization and a global trust coefficient, the number of Tesseract search nodes expanded is reduced by up to more than two orders of magnitude at low physical error rates, while the logical error rate remains close to that of Tesseract.
authors: Sana Javed, Francisco Garcia-Herrero, Bane Vasić, Mark F. Flanagan

articles.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.
authors: Umang Mishra, Teodor Strömberg, Gabriela Valencia-Guzman, Felipe Gómez-Lozada, Marta Marchese, Onur Hosten

articles.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03207v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10⁻⁶, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2²⁰, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
authors: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra

articles.title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mapping a prescribed many-body Hamiltonian to a particular quantum hardware is generally an approximate process, resulting in both intended and unwanted quantum dynamics. We introduce an AI-agent-assisted workflow that uses Lean to establish whether an effective device Hamiltonian retains the intended low-energy subspace of the target many-body Hamiltonian. We demonstrate this approach with topological quantum error correction (QEC), providing, to our knowledge, the first Lean-verified pipeline connecting a code space to low-energy states of a device model. Starting from qubits and parity checks, the pipeline constructs the ideal Hamiltonian whose lowest energy states form the intended code space, and determines the excitation gap that protects that code space. It then tests if the device retains the required number of isolated low-energy states and quantifies how closely their subspace matches the intended code space. We compare three bounds on unwanted energy shifts obtained by: summing the interaction strengths, grouping the anticommuting Pauli interactions, and diagonalizing the Hamiltonian. Pauli grouping yields a bound that is tighter than the conventional sum and closer to the diagonalization result, avoiding overly conservative compensation requirements. The workflow also identifies the strongest unwanted interactions and the qubits they affect, providing specific targets for improving device couplings and controls. We demonstrate our framework using an eight-qubit toric-code array on a superconducting device, where the same driven device generates both the required four-qubit interactions as well as unwanted dynamics. An AI agent identifies viable device parameters within a prescribed leakage budget, and Lean verifies four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space. Our workflow supports predictive hardware engineering for analog implementations of QEC codes.
authors: Arpit Arora, Adam Holmes, Krysta M. Svore, Taylor L. Patti

articles.title: On the Failure Probability of Quantum Leftover Hashing with Bad Seeds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study hashing against quantum adversaries, as used in cryptographic applications, and provide bounds on the probability of failure in practical settings where seeds might be reused and might be non-ideal. Randomness extraction and privacy amplification are key components of quantum cryptographic protocols, such as quantum randomness generation or key distribution, that allow the compression of partially secure raw data into shorter output with high security. To ensure the security of any cryptographic construction that integrates them, it is desirable to establish composable security. This can be done by using methods based on universal hashing and leveraging the general leftover hash lemma, which allows extraction of near-uniform random numbers from an imperfect entropy source by sampling from an almost two-universal family of hash functions using a seed. This approach is taken in many practical implementations, commonly using Toeplitz hashing. The lemma provides an upper bound ǎrepsilon on the distance of the output to uniform randomness, which holds on average over the choice of seeds. It makes no claim that any particular seed yields near-uniform random numbers. This poses a problem for practical applications where a seed is sampled once and reused for many rounds (blockwise hashing). Here, we study the subset of bad seeds yielding far-from-uniform outputs. We show that randomness extraction against quantum side information is guaranteed to produce δ-close-to-uniform random numbers except with failure probability łeft(fracǎrepsilonδi̊ght)². This result is generalised to blockwise hashing providing a guarantee of the security of k rounds except with failure probability big(frac(2k-1)ǎrepsilonδbig)². Moreover, we extend the general leftover hash lemma to blockwise hashing and relax the assumption of almost two-universality.
authors: Asker Friis Bach, Isabel Moreno Babuglia, Jonatan Bohr Brask

articles.title: Unifying entanglement and nonclassicality via the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement and nonclassicality are two fundamental features of quantum mechanics which serve as resources in quantum information processing tasks and are tightly connected by two-mode mixing. In this work, we show that the connection between entanglement and nonclassicality extends well beyond the two-mode mixing setting by considering the case of arbitrary multimode Gaussian evolutions. Using the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as our main technical tool to quantify single-mode phase-space nonclassicality, we derive sufficient conditions for a single-mode state to generate NPT entanglement after a multimode Gaussian unitary evolution, which both tighten and generalize existing criteria. As an application, we obtain simple single-mode protocols for quantitatively testing the entanglement structure of multimode quantum states over arbitrary bipartitions. Our results identify the Narcowich-Wigner spectrum as a powerful tool for investigating fundamental properties of bosonic quantum states.
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Zacharie Van Herstraeten, Hania Herbi, Jack Davis, Nuno C. Dias, João N. Prata, Mattia Walschaers, Ulysse Chabaud

articles.title: Spacetime Emergence in the Memory of a Learning Agent
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the causal structure of spacetime can emerge within the memory of a learning agent performing a quantum information task. We train a model-based reinforcement-learning agent to maximize the quantum mutual information between localized quantum probes interacting with a quantum field in Minkowski spacetime, without directly providing it with information regarding the spacetime metric or causal structure. In learning to accomplish this task, the reinforcement-learning agent constructs an internal predictive model whose planner develops the characteristic null structure of spacetime, allowing us to reconstruct the causal structure of the Minkowski metric with high accuracy. Within this task, spacetime geometry is obtained from an agent's successful predictions and actions, providing a first step toward showing that spacetime concepts emerge from operational quantum experience.
authors: Philip A. LeMaitre, T. Rick Perche

articles.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum channel tomography (also known as quantum process tomography) is a fundamental task in quantum information and quantum computing, aiming to learn the full description of an unknown quantum channel from black-box queries. For channels with input dimension d₁, output dimension d₂, and Kraus rank at most r, [CGO+26] identifies the dilation rate τ=rd₂/d₁≥ 1 as a key parameter governing a Heisenberg-to-classical transition in query complexity. While the optimal bounds in the boundary regime (τ=1) and the away-from-boundary regime (τ≥ 1+Ømega(1)) are now known, the precise behavior in the near-boundary regime (1<τ<1+o(1)) has remained unresolved. In this paper, we close this gap, thereby fully settling the query complexity of quantum channel tomography. Specifically, we show that the query complexity is - Ømega(rd₁d₂/ǎrepsilon²⁾ for diamond norm error ǎrepsilon, matching the upper bound by [MB26, CGO+26], - Θ(d₁²/ǎrepsilon+min(τ-1)d₁²,(τ-1)²d₁²d₂²/ǎrepsilon²⁾ for Choi trace norm error ǎrepsilon. Our results reveal two qualitatively different forms of the Heisenberg-to-classical transition. For diamond norm tomography, the Heisenberg scaling disappears suddenly as soon as τ leaves the boundary regime. In contrast, Choi trace norm tomography exhibits a gradual transition from Heisenberg to classical scaling as τ moves from the boundary regime to the away-from-boundary regime.
authors: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir

articles.title: Neonatal EEG Seizure Prediction with Quantum Inspired Continuous-Variable (Bosonic) Reservoir Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study short-horizon neonatal seizure prediction on Helsinki-style (HUH) preprocessed EEG feature tables using quantum-inspired reservoir computing. Under strict subject-wise cross-validation on imbalanced preictal--interictal windows, we test whether reservoir constructions shaped after (i) gate-based qubit dynamics and (ii) continuous-variable (bosonic/photonic) dynamics provide a practical sequence encoder relative to strong classical baselines. Both reservoirs are executed here purely in classical simulation on a single GPU; accordingly, we do not claim quantum advantage, but rather evaluate whether quantum-shaped dynamics act as useful, low-footprint random feature maps with a trained linear readout. We compare against Random Forests and RBF--SVMs, and report AUROC, AUPRC, per-subject AUPRC, expected calibration error, and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. Across our experiments, the CV/bosonic reservoir is consistently competitive and can improve AUPRC over the baselines, while the gate-style reservoir is more sensitive to hyperparameters. These results suggest that quantum-inspired, photonics-motivated reservoirs can be practical sequence encoders for neonatal EEG feature tables under conservative subject-wise evaluation.
authors: Krishna Bhatia, Chun-Yu Lin

articles.title: Lieb-Robinson Light Cones in Long-Range Bosonic Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lieb-Robinson bounds formulate emergent causality in quantum many-body dynamics. In this Letter, we study interacting bosonic systems with long-range interactions, in which both the standard assumptions of short-range interactions and uniformly bounded local energy scales are absent. We derive upper and lower bounds whose effective light-cone exponents are governed by a nontrivial interplay between the decay exponent α and the bosonic interaction order p. The propagation protocol concentrates bosons within blocks, creating a mediating sublattice with amplified interactions. For pge4 and 2d<αłe2d+1, the resulting exponents coincide, determining the optimal leading light-cone power. The upper bound includes α=2d+1 with arbitrarily small exponent loss, using a fixed-k extension of the bounded-interaction result. Our results reveal that the interplay between long-range couplings and unbounded bosonic degrees of freedom gives rise to a richer light-cone structure than in either long-range bounded systems or short-range bosonic systems alone.
authors: Carla Rubiliani, Cheng Shang, Tomotaka Kuwahara

articles.title: Semi-classical analysis of noise squeezing in Kerr microresonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kerr microresonators are integrated nonlinear devices widely used to generate classical optical frequency combs and nonclassical states of light. In particular, they provide a promising platform for squeezed light sources, which are important elements of emerging quantum sensing, communication, and computing technologies. Designing such sources requires numerical tools that efficiently incorporate realistic device physics and noise processes. Here, we show that established semi-classical frameworks based on the Lugiato-Lefever equation and the Ikeda map, instrumental in the development of classical light sources, can also predict the quadrature-noise properties of squeezed light when vacuum fluctuations are properly included. We consider three canonical configurations producing two-mode quadrature squeezing, single-mode quadrature squeezing, and intensity difference squeezing. In each case, the semi-classical simulations produce quadrature variances and noise spectra in close agreement with the quantum theoretical predictions. These frameworks therefore provide practical tools for designing squeezed light sources, with the capability to incorporate additional noise mechanisms, nonlinear effects, and complex resonator arrangements. More fundamentally, our results show that key experimental signatures of squeezing can be modeled as phase-sensitive amplification of properly normalized vacuum fluctuations within stochastic semi-classical field equations. This observation helps distinguish squeezing properties accessible through semi-classical field evolution from those intrinsically requiring a full quantum description.
authors: Sara Persia, Lev Fandeev, Fuchuan Lei, Bastian Ruhnke, Alexander E. Ulanov, Vaishali Adya, Victor Torres-Company, Tobias Herr

articles.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter α deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding W₀₍α)=±1, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases α where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.
authors: Daksh K. Sambhare, Koustav Roy, Saurabh Basu

articles.title: Graph-Covariant Bottom-Up Scale-Bridging Reconstruction of Ground and Excited States of Extended Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a hierarchical scale-bridging construction for building first principles electronic structure models of extended molecular aggregates with disorder, and its practical realization in exciton systems. The general construction, referred here as to the encapsulation, is based on a recursive operator-valued hierarchy cast in a dual graph-theoretic (discrete) and configuration-space (continuous) structure, in which variables associated with a coarser level parameterize operators governing the degrees of freedom at the next finer level in a graph-covariant, geometry-preserving fashion. In an exemplary application of this scheme, aggregate-level ground- and excited-state operators are constructed through a many-body expansion (MBE), with matrix elements evaluated in a basis comprising the aggregate ground state and local Frenkel excitations. The required monomer and dimer building blocks are obtained from DFT and TDDFT calculations, yielding aggregate-level 1-particle transition density matrices as well as Hamiltonian, dipole moment and other operators that can be evaluated at the level of the building blocks. Starting from structural models obtained from experiment or molecular dynamics, this approach generates aggregate-level operators in a bottom-up fashion without fitting parameters to spectroscopic data or performing calculations on larger system cutouts. A numerical demonstration is given for an excitonic manifold in crystalline quaterthiophene. In particular, through its intrinsic configuration-dependence encoded in the encapsulations, it will provide a bridge between static electronic structure calculations for realistic, structurally disordered aggregates and quantum or quantum-classical simulations of exciton-vibrational dynamics.
authors: Bartosz Błasiak, Irene Burghardt

articles.title: Quantum-enhanced multiphase estimation with spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced two-phase estimation in a spin-1 Bose-Einstein condensate, where spin-exchange collisions generate a spin-nematic squeezed state in the m_F=±1 modes. The resulting pair-correlated state has a rank-one quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for the two mode phases relative to the m_F=0 mode and therefore cannot resolve them independently. Nevertheless, we find that a parameter-independent passive three-mode transformation lifts this rank deficiency and enables joint estimation of both phases. In the undepleted-pump regime, we derive expressions for the QFIM, optimize the equal-weight multiparameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound, and obtain a full-rank probe with squeezing-enhanced sensitivity below the matched fixed-total-number standard quantum limit (SQL). These analytical predictions are confirmed by exact-diagonalization calculations. We further construct a parameter-independent readout that maps the phase combinations onto displacement channels accessible through atomic homodyne or parity measurements. Our results provide a route from spin-mixing-generated quantum correlations to two-phase estimation in spinor condensates.
authors: Jiaheng Jin, Xinwei Li, Dong E. Liu, Li You

articles.title: Achievability of CSS codes performance limits over Pauli channels under separate ML decoding with bounded graphical complexity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Capacity-approaching quantum error correction faces a fundamental tension: the required parity-check matrices need to become increasingly dense, while practical decoding and syndrome extraction favor sparse, bounded-degree structures. Reconciling these competing requirements remains an important open problem in quantum code design. We construct Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code ensembles that approach the CSS rate over memoryless Pauli channels under maximum-likelihood decoding while retaining sparse, bounded-degree graphical representations. The construction separates parity-check density from graphical complexity: although capacity-approaching components may require dense parity-check matrices, they are represented by sparse concatenated factor graphs. We first study a construction combining low-density parity-check (LDPC) and low-density generator-matrix (LDGM) component codes and numerically analyze the average weight distributions of the resulting codes. Motivated by these results, we introduce a second construction based on concatenated LDPC and LDGM codes and generalized irregular repeat-accumulate (GIRA) codes. We derive bounds on the average weight distribution of the resulting sum ensemble and use the Miller-Burshtein framework to prove simultaneous reliability of the two CSS decoding components. Consequently, the proposed ensemble achieves rates arbitrarily close to the CSS hashing bound under separate bit- and phase-error correction, while maintaining bounded graphical complexity, thus providing a foundation for future iterative decoders and indirect syndrome-extraction architectures.
authors: Gulnihal Mercanoglu, Achilleas Anastasopoulos, S. Sandeep Pradhan

articles.title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.
authors: Hoang Anh Nguyen, Ali Tura

articles.title: Many-Body Correlations in Phase-Space Microscopes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03112v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recently proposed "phase-space microscope" (PSM) extends quantum gas microscopes by allowing joint, single-shot measurements of position and momentum. We show that the n-body correlation functions constructed from such phase-space snapshots determine, in principle, all n-body observables of a many-body quantum state. This establishes phase-space imaging as a complete probe of strongly correlated matter, beyond what snapshots of position and momentum can provide---a limitation that goes back to a famous question posed by Pauli. Even without the full reconstruction of the density matrices, the PSM provides valuable insight into the quantum states. We demonstrate this power through several applications: witnessing entanglement hidden from both position and momentum, including between spatially separated collective degrees of freedom; resolving pairing structure across the BEC-BCS crossover, including the phase of the pair wavefunction and the reconstruction of its two-body Wigner function; probing inhomogeneous systems and preformed pairs without long-range order, relevant to the pseudogap phase; extracting the interaction energy in a magnetic field; and measurements of the local Chern marker. Furthermore, we discuss phase imprinting in the matter-wave Fourier plane as an alternative method for probing time-reversal-symmetry-broken phases such as chiral p-wave superconductors. Together, these results establish the PSM as a versatile new tool for exploring fundamental features of quantum many-body phases in strongly correlated quantum matter.
authors: Y. Yang, C. Weitenberg, N. R. Cooper

articles.title: Lossless propagation bounds for long-range fermionic interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove propagation estimates for extensive fermionic many-body interactions with polynomial time growth, no loss of spatial decay, and an optimal threshold for the polynomial spatial exponent. More precisely, we construct local representatives of evolved fermionic many-body interactions on metric spaces with polynomial volume growth of order dᵥₒₗ and suitable cell partitions. For the even Hamiltonian interaction Φᵤ and the even interaction Ψ being evolved, we assume bounds, uniform in the site, on sums of term norms over finite supports X containing a given site, with weights eκ|X|(1+øperatornamediamX)^a and eκ|X|(1+øperatornamediamX)^p, respectively. Here a>dᵥₒₗ, 0łe płe a, κ is sufficiently large, and the Hamiltonian bound is uniform in time. We construct local representatives whose interaction norms with weight e^c(1+|t-s|)⁻b|X|(1+øperatornamediamX)^p grow at most polynomially in |t-s|, for suitable c,b>0. In particular, p=a is allowed: the Hamiltonian need not decay faster than the interaction being evolved. The threshold a>dᵥₒₗ is optimal in general: uniform polynomial time bounds at p=a fail for 0
authors: Stefan Teufel

articles.title: Effects of detuning on PT-symmetric, tridiagonal, tight-binding models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2302.13204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-Hermitian, tight-binding PT-symmetric models are extensively studied in the literature. Here, we investigate two forms of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians to study PT-symmetry breaking and features of surfaces of exceptional points (EPs). They include one-dimensional chains with 2-periodic tunnelling strengths and a pair of balanced gain and loss potentials at parity-symmetric sites. By considering several examples, we demonstrate that algebraic EP curves of a given order generically have cusp-points where the order of the EP increases by one. We count the number of edge states when the gain and loss sites are at the edges of an even chain and show that this number is dictated by the PT and topological phases. When the gain and loss sites are nearest neighbour at the center of an even chain, we construct a positive-definite metric operator for the entire domain of quasi-Hermiticity and show the entire spectrum becomes non-real as the gain is tuned above an EP. Taken together, our results provide a detailed understanding of detuned tight-binding models with a pair of gain-loss potentials.
authors: Jacob L. Barnett, Yogesh N. Joglekar

articles.title: Effective eigenvalue approximation from moments for self-adjoint trace-class operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.04478v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spectral properties of bounded linear operators play a crucial role in several areas of mathematics and physics. For each self-adjoint, trace-class operator O we define a set Łambdaₙsubset R, and we show that it converges to the spectrum of O in the Hausdorff metric under mild conditions. Our set Łambdaₙ only depends on the first n moments of O. We show that it can be effectively calculated for physically relevant operators, and it approximates the spectrum well without diagonalization. We prove that using the above method we can converge to the minimal and maximal eigenvalues with super-exponential speed. We also construct monotone increasing lower bounds qₙ for the minimal eigenvalue (or decreasing upper bounds for the maximal eigenvalue). This sequence only depends on the moments of O and a concrete upper estimate of its 1-norm; we also demonstrate that qₙ can be effectively calculated for a large class of physically relevant operators. This rigorous lower bound qₙ tends to the minimal eigenvalue with super-exponential speed provided that O is not positive semidefinite. As a by-product, we obtain computable upper bounds for the 1-norm of O, too. Numerical examples demonstrate the relevance of our approximation in estimating entropy and negativity, which is useful, among others, in quantum optical and in open quantum system models. The results can be directly applicable to problems in quantum information, statistical mechanics, and quantum thermodynamics, where using traditional techniques based on diagonalization is impractical.
authors: Richárd Balka, Gábor Homa, András Csordás

articles.title: Hardware-Efficient Entanglement Distillation Using Bosonic Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2503.09700v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-fidelity entanglement shared between distant quantum systems is an essential resource for quantum communication and computation. Entanglement distillation addresses this need by converting multiple noisy Bell pairs into fewer higher-fidelity pairs, using only local quantum operations and classical communication. However, this approach typically requires a substantial overhead in the number of qubits. To bypass this hurdle, we propose to leverage the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a single pair of bosonic systems to store a large amount of entanglement, replacing the need for multi-qubit systems. To distill entanglement in such a setup, we devise a new entanglement distillation protocol, tailored for bosonic systems. The protocol converts a highly-entangled noisy state between two bosonic systems into a lower-dimensional but high-fidelity entangled state, using only local bosonic operations. We show that our protocol significantly enhances the fidelity of the entangled state in the presence of naturally occurring loss and dephasing errors. Compared to methods relying on multiple Bell pairs, our scheme offers a more hardware-efficient strategy, providing a practical route toward the realization of entanglement distillation.
authors: Shoham Jacoby, Rotem Arnon-Friedman, Serge Rosenblum

articles.title: Directional Codes for Quantum LDPC Error Correction on Square and Hexagonal Grid Architectures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.19430v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing requires quantum error correction (QEC) to protect quantum information against noise. Currently, superconducting hardware is a promising candidate for achieving fault tolerance due to its fast gate times and feasible scalability. However, it is often restricted to two-dimensional nearest-neighbour connectivity, and therefore the variety of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that can be implemented on it without sacrificing QEC performance is believed to be greatly restricted. In this paper we construct a new family of qLDPC codes, which we call ``directional codes'', that outperforms the rotated toric code (RTC) while satisfying the connectivity requirements of the widely adopted square-grid, and some even the sparser hexagonal-grid, on a torus. The key idea is to utilise the iSWAP gate -- a native gate demonstrated on superconducting qubits -- to construct circuits that measure the stabilisers of these qLDPC codes without the need for additional connections. We numerically evaluate the performance of directional codes, encoding four, six, twelve and eighteen logical qubits, using a common superconducting-inspired circuit-level Pauli noise model. We also compare them to the RTC and to the bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, currently the two most popular quantum LDPC code families. As a concrete example, when evaluated with the Tesseract decoder with short beam setting, the best directional code family investigated achieves the same logical error rate as the RTC at physical error rate p=10⁻³ but requires only a quarter to a third of the number of physical qubits to encode a given number of logical qubits. Our discovery opens a novel direction in QEC code design, suggesting that complex high-connectivity hardware may not be necessary for low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation.
authors: György P. Gehér, David Byfield, Archibald Ruban

articles.title: Hierarchy of entanglement detection criteria for random high-dimensional states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.21787v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement is a cornerstone in quantum information science, yet detecting it efficiently remains a challenging task. Focusing on states with nonpositive partial transpose (NPT), we establish a hierarchy among entropy-based, majorization, realignment, and reduction criteria for Haar uniformly generated random states in finite dimensions, analyzing their performance based on rank and subsystem dimension. We prove lower bounds on the rank of mixed quantum states beyond which the realignment and entropic criteria fail to detect entanglement. We evaluate the relative effectiveness of the considered detection methods using three key indicators -- fraction of detected states, mean detectable entanglement, and minimum required entanglement. Our results provide insights into the entanglement thresholds needed for reliable detection, showing that, beyond a certain level of entanglement, all criteria become equally powerful for low-rank states, while a hierarchy emerges among the various criteria for moderate to high ranks. Intriguingly, the proposed ordering among the considered criteria in qubit-qudit systems is different from that in higher dimensions. Additionally, we establish that the detection efficiency is influenced by the asymmetry in the subsystem dimensions, by illustrating how the realignment criterion behaves more efficiently than other detection methods when the difference between the subsystem dimensions is small.
authors: Akhil Kumar Awasthi, Sudipta Mondal, Rivu Gupta, Aditi Sen De

articles.title: Free mutual information and higher-point OTOCs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.13406v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a quantity called the free mutual information (FMI), adapted from concepts in free probability theory, as a new physical measure of quantum chaos. This quantity captures the spreading of a time-evolved operator in the space of all possible operators on the Hilbert space, which is doubly exponential in the number of degrees of freedom. It thus provides a finer notion of operator spreading than the well-understood phenomenon of operator growth in physical space. We derive two central results which apply in any physical system: first, an explicit "Coulomb gas" formula for the FMI of two observables A(t) and B in terms of the eigenvalues of the product operator A(t)B; and second, a general relation expressing the FMI as a weighted sum of all higher-point out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). This second result provides a precise information-theoretic interpretation for the higher-point OTOCs as collectively quantifying operator ergodicity and the approach to freeness. This physical interpretation is particularly useful in light of recent progress in experimentally measuring higher-point OTOCs. We identify universal behaviours of the FMI and higher-point OTOCs across a variety of chaotic systems, including random unitary circuits and chaotic spin chains, which indicate that spreading in the doubly exponential operator space is a generic feature of quantum many-body chaos. At the same time, the non-generic behavior of the FMI in various non-chaotic systems, including certain unitary designs, shows that there are cases where an operator spreads in physical space but remains localized in operator space. The FMI is thus a sharper diagnostic of chaos than the standard 4-point OTOC.
authors: Shreya Vardhan, Jinzhao Wang

articles.title: Hyperfine spectroscopy and nuclear spin control of dark defects in diamond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.19598v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin defects in diamond serve as powerful building blocks for quantum technologies, especially for quantum sensing and networking. Electron-nuclear defects formed near optically active spins such as the nitrogen-vacancy center provide a resource for multi-qubit quantum registers. However, many remain uncharacterized, limiting their control and integration in quantum devices. Here, we identify the hyperfine components, including their relative sign, and nuclear spin species of two unknown dark spin defects using zero-field double electron-electron resonance spectroscopy and a protocol based on electron-nuclear double resonance. New ab initio calculations assign one defect to a known nitrogen interstitial, while the hydrogen-related defect matches no calculated or previously reported structure. We further use this protocol to demonstrate initialization, unitary control, and long-lived coherence of the hydrogen nuclear spin qubit, with a coherence time of 1.0(3) ms. These characterization and control tools establish a framework for harnessing unknown electron-nuclear defects for quantum registers.
authors: Alexander Ungar, Hao Tang, Andrew Stasiuk, Bo Xing, Boning Li, Ju Li, Alexandre Cooper, Paola Cappellaro

articles.title: Pervasive Vulnerability Analysis and Defense for QKD-based Quantum Private Query
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.01918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum Private Query (QPQ) based on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is among the most practically viable quantum communication protocols, with application value second only to QKD itself. However, prevalent security vulnerabilities in the post-processing stages of most existing QKD-based QPQ protocols have been severely overlooked. This study focuses on hidden information extraction under undetermined signal bits, revealing that most such QPQ protocols face severe security threats even without complex quantum resources. Specifically, direct observation attack causes incremental information leakage, while the minimum error discrimination attack efficiently steals additional database inforamtion. To address these critical flaws, the proposed multi-encryption defense scheme is compatible with existing QPQ protocols. The study demonstrates the necessity of the multi-encryption strategy for the security of databases in QPQ, providing key theoretical and technical support for constructing practical QPQ protocols resistant to real-world attacks.
authors: Xiaoyu Peng, Bin Liu, JiaHao Huang, Nankun Mu, Wei Huang, Bingjie Xu, Fei Gao

articles.title: Spectral Codes: A Geometric Formalism for Quantum Error Correction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.19765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new geometric perspective on quantum error correction based on spectral triples in noncommutative geometry. In this approach, quantum error correcting codes are reformulated as low energy spectral projections of Dirac type operators that separate global logical degrees of freedom from local, correctable errors. Locality, code distance, and the Knill Laflamme condition acquire a unified spectral and geometric interpretation in terms of the induced metric and spectrum of the Dirac operator. Within this framework, a wide range of known error correcting codes including classical linear codes, stabilizer codes, GKP type codes, and topological codes are recovered from a single construction. This demonstrates that classical and quantum codes can be organized within a common geometric language. A central advantage of the spectral triple perspective is that the performance of error correction can be directly related to spectral properties. We show that leakage out of the code space is controlled by the spectral gap of the Dirac operator, and that code preserving internal perturbations can systematically increase this gap without altering the encoded logical subspace. This yields a geometric mechanism for enhancing error correction thresholds, which we illustrate explicitly for a stabilizer code. We further interpret Berezin Toeplitz quantization as a mixed spectral code and briefly discuss implications for holographic quantum error correction. Overall, our results suggest that quantum error correction can be viewed as a universal low energy phenomenon governed by spectral geometry.
authors: Satoshi Kanno, Yoshi-aki Shimada

articles.title: Entanglement in quantum spin chains is strictly finite at any temperature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.13386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entanglement is the hallmark of quantum physics, yet its characterization in interacting many-body systems at thermal equilibrium remains one of the most important challenges in quantum statistical physics. We prove that the Gibbs state of any quantum spin chain can be exactly decomposed into a mixture of matrix product states with a bond dimension that is independent of the system size, at any nonzero temperature. As a consequence, the Schmidt number, arguably the most stringent measure of bipartite entanglement, is strictly finite for thermal states, even in the thermodynamic limit. Our decomposition is explicit and is accompanied by an efficient classical algorithm to sample the resulting matrix product states.
authors: Ainesh Bakshi, Soonwon Choi, Saúl Pilatowsky-Cameo

articles.title: Unified Probe of Quantum Chaos and Ergodicity from Hamiltonian Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.04486v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Developing measures of quantum ergodicity and chaos stands as a foundational task in the study of quantum many-body systems. In this work, we propose metrics for these effects based on Hamiltonian learning that unify multiple advantages of existing metrics. In particular, we show how ergodicity and chaos improve the robustness of Hamiltonian learning to small errors and furthermore demonstrate that this robustness can be used as a metric for such phenomena. We analytically and numerically show that our metrics not only distinguish between integrable and ergodic regimes in various spin chains but also quantify chaos and ergodicity, allowing us to locate regions of parameter space displaying maximal ergodicity and maximal sensitivity to local perturbations. Our approach not only provides conceptual ways to study quantum chaos and ergodicity but also presents viable experimental methods for quantum simulators.
authors: Nik O. Gjonbalaj, Christian Kokail, Susanne F. Yelin, Soonwon Choi

articles.title: Local correlations in long-range dual-unitary kicked Hamiltonian chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.13857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many-body Floquet models with exact space--time duality, such as the kicked Ising chain, provide paradigmatic examples of dual-unitary dynamics. The requirement of exact space--time duality is, however, highly restrictive and, in its standard formulation, permits only nearest-neighbor interactions. We demonstrate that the latter constraint can be avoided, still resulting in exactly solvable models. In particular, we construct a broad class of dual-unitary kicked spin chains with long-range interactions. We show that, for an interaction range r, local two-point connected correlation functions propagate along the edges of the light cone, |n|=r|t|, and can be evaluated analytically for local observables. We illustrate our general statement by analytic calculation of the connected correlation function for a kicked Ising chain with next-to-next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
authors: Vladimir Al. Osipov, Marc Cedric Spyra, Jana Carolina Schumann, Thomas Guhr, Boris Gutkin

articles.title: Quantum linear solvers for quantum chemistry: prospects of exponential quantum advantage
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.08220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum linear solvers (QLSs) offer the potential for quantum advantage in solving quantum chemical problems, but assessing such an advantage hinges on determining condition number (κ) scaling, which itself is computationally challenging. While a recent work applied the HHL algorithm to single-reference linearized coupled cluster (SRLCC), the validity of the framework is restricted to weakly correlated regimes. We thus begin by extending QLS-SRLCC to its multi-reference form, the internally contracted multi-reference LCC (QLS-icMRLCC). We then analyze κ scaling across a diverse range of systems as well as bases in both QLS-SRLCC and QLS-icMRLCC, using three complementary diagnostics that range from explicit computations to use of indirect structural indicators: (i) direct calculations of κ, (ii) scaling of the ratio of maximum to minimum diagonal entries of an A matrix, and (iii) structural analyses of the A matrices based on a recently proposed conjecture that we adapt to the QLS-LCC problem. The three approaches yield broadly consistent predictions, with our numerical results indicating a slow-growing κ scaling in system size for the sampled systems. For icMRLCC, however, the observed behaviour depends on the reference active space, leaving the broader prospects of quantum advantage with it less certain. This finding, when combined with our arguments on sub-linear scaling of sparsity (when excitation rank>2), supports the prospects of exponential advantage for QLS-LCC. However, the prospects of a QLS-level advantage do not necessarily translate to a speed-up in an end-to-end workflow. Finally, up to 28-qubit HHL-icMRLCCSD numerical calculations on potential energy curves of model systems containing up to four atoms recover the ground state energies with about 0.012% errors relative to benchmark classical methods.
authors: Peniel Bertrand Tsemo, Kenji Sugisaki, Ishita Bhattacharjee, V. S. Prasannaa

articles.title: Quantum error-correcting codes from aperiodic monotiles: the Hat and the Spectre
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.15326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Li and Boyle showed that the Penrose tiling defines a quantum error-correcting code: superpositions of tilings over isometry orbits protect quantum information against erasure of any bounded region. We extend the construction to the aperiodic monotiles discovered by Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss. For the Hat, we prove strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings, and we prove local recoverability unconditionally for all nonsingular Hat tilings via the torus parametrization of the underlying cut-and-project scheme. The remaining singular case reduces to one sharply posed geometric question -- can a region that is a union of hats be retiled a second way? -- which we verify computationally has no counterexample up to a substantial scale: a certified 2490-tile patch admits precisely one tiling by hats, so all 2²⁴⁹⁰ of its tile-subregions retile uniquely. Unlike the Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and Fibonacci tilings, both monotiles form two local-indistinguishability classes, so their code spaces split into two erasure-correcting sectors carrying a superselected classical label. Whether the label survives depends on which isometries are gauged: the Spectre's classes are exchanged by a 30ⁱ̧rc rotation and merge once all proper isometries are gauged, whereas the Hat's are exchanged only by reflections. Under the physically natural gauge group SE(2), the Hat code therefore stores one robust classical bit -- the handedness of its long-range order, readable in any bounded window with separation Δ = |K|sqrt5/3 -- alongside its protected quantum sectors. It is the reflexible monotile, not the chiral one, that carries the chirality bit. We give the exact Perron-Frobenius data of both codes, including the per-class reflected-Hat frequencies (3mpsqrt5)/6 and the Spectre orientation-class frequencies (5±sqrt15)/10.
authors: Josep Batle, Adam Bednorz

articles.title: Noise-robust discrimination of incoherent point sources with spatial-mode demultiplexing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.01765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate that a reduced spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) measurement using only the two lowest-order Hermite-Gaussian modes exhibits remarkable robustness against background noise in discriminating between a single source and two incoherent point sources. We establish a theoretical framework incorporating uniform background noise and derive an analytical Chernoff exponent expression, showing that SPADE consistently outperforms direct imaging (DI) across all source separations. Experimental results confirm that SPADE-based hypothesis testing approaches the quantum limit even when the background-to-signal photon ratio per pixel is 0.11. This advantage stems from SPADE's ability to concentrate source information into minimal detection modes, reducing the cumulative background noise impact. Our findings provide a practical detection scheme for applications where background noise is inevitable, such as astronomical observations and quantum sensing.
authors: Jian-Qiang Liu, Chao-Ning Hu, Jun Xin, Xiao-Ming Lu

articles.title: Universal Inductive Inference of Quantum States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.36912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solomonoff's universal inductive inference [Inf. Control. 1964] is one of the most general frameworks for learning from sequential data and predicting future observations. It provides prediction guarantees for any computable stochastic source. We ask whether an analogous universal theory of induction can be developed for quantum systems. To this end, we introduce universal quantum inductive inference, a framework for learning and predicting quantum sources that may exhibit arbitrary correlations and entanglement across time. Given the outcomes of past measurements and the corresponding post-measurement quantum systems, the learner produces a joint state that predicts the next measurement outcome and post-measurement system while preserving correlations with the past systems. We model a quantum source as a multipartite quantum state whose description is generated by an unknown s-bit program within a given time bound. The learner is required to produce a state that is ϵ-close in trace distance to the target with probability at least 1-δ. We establish an information-theoretic inference algorithm with round complexity O(sϵ⁻²δ⁻¹). We further prove a matching lower bound in the relevant parameter regime, even for classical sources. As a second result, we construct a non-i.i.d. state tomography algorithm that outputs a classical description of the conditional state of the next system given past measurement outcomes. Our information-theoretic tomography algorithm achieves round complexity O(sn²ϵ⁻⁴δ⁻²), where n is the number of qubits received in each round. Finally, we investigate the computational hardness of universal quantum inductive inference under quantum cryptographic assumptions.
authors: Taiga Hiroka, Min-Hsiu Hsieh, Yuki Shirakawa

articles.title: Elucidating the topological nature of molecular beam epitaxy grown high Curie temperature (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is used to elucidate the band structure of (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x, a new magnetic quantum material grown using molecular beam epitaxy that has a Curie temperature (TC) above 100K, much higher than those reported for other materials of the MnxSb2-xTe4 class. Conflicting and sparse theory and experiments, as well as the complex disordered structure of the materials make it difficult to establish their topological nature. Here we explore this question by performing ARPES studies for two samples with x=0.65 and x=0.92, respectively. Images of the band structures of these two samples were acquired using photon energy dependent studies. The bulk and surface states of this complex material system, and the effects of composition on the band structure were investigated. Evidence of surface state features as well as bulk related ones were obtained, supporting their non-trivial nature. No signature of Fermi-arcs consistent with Weyl semimetals were seen. A shift in the Fermi level of the two samples due to different carrier densities allowed observation of the onset of a Dirac point in the surface states. Temperature dependent ARPES suggests possible band splitting as the materials undergo magnetic transitions, helping to understand the magnetic interactions. Our results point to their likely magnetic topological insulating nature.
authors: Candice R. Forrester, Jisoo Moon, Sina Mohammadi, Asish Kundu, Amy Lopez Navarro, Kaushini Wickramasinghe, Abhay Pasupathy, Anil K. Rajapitamahuni, Maya N. Nair, Elio Vescovo, Lia Krusin-Elbaum, Maria C. Tamargo

articles.title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
articles.title_zh: 幺正费米气体中非平衡动力学的可逆性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. Unlike the equilibrium case, reversibility out of equilibrium imposes a stringent condition: the accumulated dynamical phase must be an integer multiple of 2π, i.e., Δφ = 2ømega₀ s(T) = 2nπ, where ømega₀ is the initial trapping frequency and s(T) is the rescaled time after a total evolution time T. We demonstrate the reversibility of an initial nonequilibrium state in an isotropic unitary Fermi gas by driving the optical trap through a round trip. We find two types of reversible pathways, the space-time scaling-invariant and polynomial shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) protocols. The phase condition restricts the round-trip time T to discrete values, a distinguishing feature of nonequilibrium dynamics. Our work establishes a clear criterion for the quantum control of nonequilibrium many-body systems beyond linear response and provides practical pathways to reversibility.
articles.abstract_zh: 该工作从理论上描述并实验观察了幺正费米气体中非平衡态的可逆性。研究发现，非平衡态的可逆性需要满足严格的条件，即累积的动力学相位必须是2π的整数倍。作者展示了两种可逆路径，并指出该相位条件将往返时间限制在离散值，这是非平衡动力学的一个显著特征。这项工作为超越线性响应的非平衡多体系统量子控制建立了明确标准，并提供了实现可逆性的实用途径。
authors: Xi-Zhi Wu, Xiangchuan Yan, Xin Xie, Dali Sun, Seong-Ho Shinn, Adolfo del Campo, Kaijun Jiang

articles.title: Curvature-Driven Density and Fluctuations in Interacting AOUPs under Confinement
articles.title_zh: 约束条件下相互作用AOUPs中的曲率驱动密度与涨落
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate interacting active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particles (AOUPs) confined in harmonic and double-well potentials, combining mean-field theory, analytical approximations, and numerical simulations. We derive the stationary density, position and velocity correlations, correlation length, dynamical structure factor, and leading-order entropy production. Unlike established harmonic normal-mode descriptions, our framework incorporates steric interactions, persistent forcing, and spatially varying confinement curvature through the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the many-body Hessian. Within a locally homogeneous approximation, the correlation length is controlled by persistence and local curvature, increasing as the effective restoring stiffness decreases and formally diverging at the instability of the linearized description. Entropy production, at leading nontrivial order in persistence, is governed by gradients of the effective curvature. Harmonic confinement provides a constant-curvature reference, whereas double-well confinement creates equilibrium-like regions near the minima and strongly nonequilibrium regions near the barrier. The barrier exhibits enhanced velocity and density fluctuations, soft collective modes, long-lived correlations, and increased entropy production. Persistence amplifies these effects, while steric crowding suppresses collective fluctuations. The dynamical structure factor reveals enhanced low-frequency contributions from soft modes. Our results establish how confinement geometry, active persistence, and interactions jointly regulate collective fluctuations and irreversibility in active matter.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究结合平均场理论、解析近似和数值模拟，探讨了谐振势和双势阱中相互作用的活性奥恩斯坦-乌伦贝克粒子（AOUPs）。研究推导了稳态密度、位置和速度关联、关联长度、动力学结构因子以及领先阶熵产生，并考虑了空间变化的约束曲率。结果表明，关联长度受持久性和局部曲率控制，而熵产生则由有效曲率梯度决定。
authors: Renu Parashar, Sandipan Dutta

articles.title: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons
articles.title_zh: 扶手椅型石墨烯纳米带中体能隙的完全边缘控制
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In solid-state physics, the ability to open and tune an electronic energy gap provides a direct route to controlling charge transport and accessing distinct electronic phases.
