In solids with physical boundaries, a bulk energy gap formed exclusively by extended bulk states is conventionally expected to be governed primarily by the interior bulk region, with only a minor contribution from the boundaries. Here we show that, in stark contrast to this conventional expectation, the bulk gap of armchair graphene nanoribbons in the N_w=3p+2 family with pinZge 0 can be fully controlled through the hoppings solely at the boundaries. This full boundary control originates from an exact cancellation between the gap contributions of long-range hoppings along and across the ribbon in the bulk region. It persists in the presence of Hubbard interactions and holds irrespective of ribbon width in this family. Our findings establish boundary dynamics as an unexpectedly powerful means of manipulating bulk electronic properties, enabling width-preserving engineering of one-dimensional (1D) band structures and topological phases, with potential applications in qubits, artificial quantum spin chains, topological quantum dots and other quantum devices.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究发现，在N_w=3p+2家族的扶手椅型石墨烯纳米带中，其体能隙可以完全通过边缘处的跳跃来控制，这与传统预期截然不同。这种完全的边缘控制源于体区域中沿纳米带和跨纳米带的长程跳跃贡献的精确抵消，并且在存在哈伯德相互作用时以及与纳米带宽度无关的情况下都成立。研究结果表明，边界动力学是操纵体电子性质的强大手段，有望实现一维能带结构和拓扑相的工程设计。
authors: Lin Wang, Thomas Luu, Ulf-G. Meißner

articles.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
articles.title_zh: PbTe-Pb纳米线中栅极可调超导体-半导体耦合及其对零能模式的影响
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究展示了PbTe-Pb纳米线中可调谐的超导体-半导体耦合及其对诱导能隙和零偏压峰（ZBPs）的影响。在强耦合状态下，器件呈现出清晰的超导能隙，并观察到在不同磁场范围内的鲁棒和非鲁棒ZBPs。随着栅极电压增加，系统进入弱耦合状态，能隙变窄且变软，鲁棒ZBPs消失而非鲁棒ZBPs依然存在。研究结果建立了可调谐耦合与鲁棒ZBPs之间的直接联系，为马约拉纳零模和拓扑量子比特的工程设计提供了指导。
authors: Ruidong Li, Shuai Yang, Wenyu Song, Zeyu Yan, Yuhao Wang, Zehao Yu, Li Chen, Zixun Xia, Zonglin Li, Shan Zhang, Jiaye Xu, Lining Yang, Weizhao Wang, Xiao Feng, Tiantian Wang, Yunyi Zang, Lin Li, Runan Shang, Dong E. Liu, Qi-Kun Xue, Ke He, Hao Zhang

articles.title: Cluster Condensation and Symmetry-Protected Thermal Rigidity of Bose gases on the Haldane Sphere
articles.title_zh: Haldane球上玻色气体的团簇凝聚与对称性保护的热刚性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a spinless Bose gas on a Haldane sphere with a small monopole charge (q) realizes, in the lowest Landau level (LLL), an exactly solvable SU(2)-protected cluster condensate: a Hafnian condensate of two-boson singlets for (q=1), analogous to resonating-valence-bond singlet coverings, and a four-boson singlet condensate for (q=3/2). Unlike topologically protected quantum Hall states, the exactness of these states relies only on SU(2) symmetry and repulsiveness, with no pseudopotential fine-tuning. Their SU(2)-protected degeneracy renders the single-particle correlations exactly temperature-independent even as the clusters dissociate, a thermal rigidity absent in conventional Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs). Increasing the interaction drives a transition to a vortex BEC with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究表明，在具有小单极荷（q）的Haldane球上，无自旋玻色气体在最低朗道能级中实现了SU(2)保护的精确可解团簇凝聚态。这些态的精确性仅依赖于SU(2)对称性和排斥性，而非赝势微调。其SU(2)保护的简并性使得单粒子关联即使在团簇解离时也与温度无关，展现出传统玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体所不具备的热刚性。增加相互作用会驱动系统向具有自发破缺旋转对称性的涡旋玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体转变。
authors: Meng-Jie Wang, Jun-Hui Zheng

articles.title: Zero-field plasmon splitter: Controlled interaction between quantum anomalous Hall edge states
articles.title_zh: 零场等离激元分束器：量子反常霍尔边缘态之间的受控相互作用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect provides chiral edge states without the need for an external magnetic field, but unlike in conventional quantum Hall systems, their trajectories cannot be readily controlled electrostatically. Here, we engineer Coulomb interactions between two spatially separated, counter-propagating QAH edge channels using a floating metallic island. Microwave measurements reveal frequency-dependent redistribution of injected edge plasmons between two output channels, demonstrating interaction-induced hybridization of the collective modes. A long-range interaction model quantitatively reproduces the response and reveals a very low plasmon velocity in the coupling region, strongly reduced by electrostatic screening. Our results establish engineered Coulomb coupling as a route to control collective excitations in QAH edge states and provide a building block for chiral plasmonic circuits and electron quantum optics in magnetic topological insulators.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究通过浮动金属岛，在空间分离的两个反向传播量子反常霍尔（QAH）边缘通道之间设计库仑相互作用，从而实现了零场等离激元分束器。微波测量揭示了注入边缘等离激元频率依赖的再分配，证明了集体模式的相互作用诱导杂化。长程相互作用模型定量再现了响应，并显示耦合区域中等离激元速度因静电屏蔽而显著降低。这项工作确立了工程化库仑耦合作为控制QAH边缘态集体激发的途径，为手性等离激元电路和电子量子光学提供了基本构建块。
authors: Dominik Hoborka, Torsten Röper, Fabian Hassler, Alexey A. Taskin, Yoichi Ando, Erwann Bocquillon

articles.title: Hidden variable Z₂ topological order in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet
articles.title_zh: 双层kagomé反铁磁体中的隐藏变量Z₂拓扑序
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03073v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological orders in realistic systems are quite rare, raising one fundamental question of whether they might be harbored with hidden degrees of freedom rather than directly exposed in conventional spins or electrons. We here propose a set of hidden variables and their effective interactions in a bilayer kagomé antiferromagnet. By properly organizing four local states of the spin dimer into two pseudospin-1/2 variables (boldsymbolτ and boldsymbolμ), we identify a regime where an effective Balents-Fisher-Girvin model emerges, realizing a Z₂ topological order in the hidden boldsymbolτ sector while the auxiliary boldsymbolμ sector remains a trivial paramagnet. This hidden nature drastically alters the experimental manifestations. Physical spins map to composite objects, typically convolving fractionalized anyon continua with non-topological magnon excitations. Nevertheless, specific symmetry-selected channels, such as the longitudinal intralayer response, exclusively reveal the bare two-vison continuum without collective-mode dressing. Our findings demonstrate that the topological order could be buried in certain hidden and emergent degrees of freedom, pointing to a promising pathway for seeking elusive topological states disguised within hidden internal degrees of freedom.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究提出了一种双层kagomé反铁磁体中的隐藏变量及其有效相互作用。通过将自旋二聚体的四个局域态组织成两个赝自旋-1/2变量，研究发现一个有效的Balents-Fisher-Girvin模型得以出现，在隐藏的τ扇区实现了Z₂拓扑序，而辅助的μ扇区则保持为平凡顺磁体。这种隐藏性质显著改变了实验表现，其中物理自旋映射到复合对象。然而，特定的对称性选择通道，如纵向层内响应，可以专门揭示裸露的双vison连续谱。研究结果表明拓扑序可能隐藏在某些隐藏和涌现的自由度中。
authors: Hao Tian, Pengwei Zhao, Gang v. Chen

articles.title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
articles.title_zh: 通过结合非反常对称性强制实现无能隙
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and U(1)² in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究表明，即使两个较大的对称性都是可逆且非反常的（即每个对称性单独都允许一个平凡的带隙相），对称性跨度也能强制系统处于无能隙状态。这是因为嵌入方式因与对称性保护拓扑相相关的扭曲而不同，从而阻止了具有有限个基态的带隙相的出现。作者提出了1+1维的有限群和U(1)²对称性示例，包括一个在参数空间任何区域都无能隙的晶格哈密顿量。
authors: Takamasa Ando, Kantaro Ohmori

articles.title: Pressure-correlation phase diagram unraveling quantum phase transitions in altermagnetic ϵ-FeOOH and realization of piezo-anomalous Hall effect
articles.title_zh: 压力-关联相图揭示交错磁性ϵ-FeOOH中的量子相变及压电反常霍尔效应的实现
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a pressure-correlation phase diagram that yields multiple pressure-tunable quantum phase transitions in iron oxyhydroxide (ϵ-FeOOH) across three critical pressures, Pc₁>Pc₂>Pc₃. The transitions arise from the competition among electron-correlation, crystal-field, and Hund's coupling. First-principles calculations reveal that the earlier reported high-spin (HS) to low-spin (LS) crossover at correlation-sensitive Pc₁ is accompanied by a transition from charge-transfer to Mott insulating (CTI-MI) phase, and a change in the spin-quantization axis (SQA) from haty to hatx. The HS-LS crossover and CTI-MI transition is driven by the simultaneous increase in crystal-field splitting and decrease in Hund's coupling. The critical pressure Pc₂ governing the structural transition from centrosymmetric Pnnm phase to noncentrosymmetric P2₁ₙₘ phase is found to be independent of electron-correlation. When correlation is strong, a third critical pressure (Pc₃) emerges in the lower-pressure regime of the phase diagram. Validating the recent experimental observation, Pc₃ is responsible for changing the SQA from hatz to haty. By exhibiting altermagnetism in both P2₁ₙₘ and Pnnm phases and possessing finite anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) only for SQA along hatx and haty, ϵ-FeOOH enables a unique piezo-anomalous Hall effect where one can switch on the AHC at a lower pressure and change its direction at a higher pressure.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究建立了交错磁性ϵ-FeOOH的压力-关联相图，揭示了在三个临界压力下可调谐的量子相变。这些相变源于电子关联、晶体场和洪特耦合之间的竞争。第一性原理计算表明，在Pc₁处的高自旋到低自旋转变伴随着电荷转移到莫特绝缘相变以及自旋量子化轴的变化。Pc₂控制着与电子关联无关的结构相变。在强关联条件下，出现了第三个临界压力Pc₃，负责改变自旋量子化轴。
authors: Arijit Mandal, Nayana Devaraj, Birabar Ranjit Kumar Nanda

articles.title: Polariton tweezers
articles.title_zh: 极化激元镊子
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究展示了动态极化激元镊子的概念，能够对二维电子系统中的电荷载流子进行非侵入式、确定性操控。通过特定设计的非共线三束光泵浦驱动半导体微腔，合成了一个具有六方对称性的宏观极化激元晶格。该d-极化激元凝聚体的空间周期场作为电子的可重构捕获景观。引入目标频率失谐打破了时空对称性，将静止的干涉图样转化为动态移动的传送带，从而能够将整个晶格及其静电捕获的电子刚性地驱动到任意面内方向。
authors: Nika Gribova, Evgeny Sedov, Alexey Kavokin

articles.title: An Intrinsically Gapless Topological Phase with Dipole Symmetry
articles.title_zh: 具有偶极对称性的本征无能隙拓扑相
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the boundary fractionalization familiar from gapped topological insulators can enforce bulk gaplessness in a dipole-conserving system. In a one-dimensional fermion model with charge conservation, dipole conservation, and particle-hole symmetry, we realize an intrinsically gapless symmetry-protected topological (igSPT) phase combining a dipolar Luttinger liquid with half-quantized boundary charges. This boundary structure obstructs a unique gapped bulk preserving these symmetries and lattice translation. Remarkably, the two charge-neutral edge configurations remain exactly degenerate even at finite size due to dipole conservation and particle-hole symmetry. The boundary fractionalization also manifests as shifted conformal towers in the dipole-resolved entanglement spectrum, reflecting distinct conformal boundary conditions of the Luttinger liquid. We support our analysis of the igSPT by studying exactly-solvable limits and performing DMRG computations, establishing its stability for a wide range of tuning parameters.
articles.abstract_zh: 该研究表明，在偶极子守恒系统中，源自带隙拓扑绝缘体的边界分数量子化可以强制实现体态的无能隙。在一个具有电荷、偶极子和粒子-空穴对称性的一维费米子模型中，实现了本征无能隙对称性保护拓扑（igSPT）相，它结合了偶极子Luttinger液体和半量子化的边界电荷。这种边界结构阻碍了唯一带隙体态的形成。偶极子守恒和粒子-空穴对称性使得两个电荷中性边缘构型即使在有限尺寸下也保持精确简并。
authors: Amogh Anakru, Linhao Li, Zhen Bi

articles.title: Polarons in atomic gases and two-dimensional semiconductors
articles.title_zh: 原子气体和二维半导体中的极化子
articles.abstract: arXiv:2501.09618v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we provide a comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental studies of the properties of polarons formed by mobile impurities strongly interacting with quantum many-body systems. We present a unified perspective on the universal concepts and theoretical techniques used to characterize polarons in two distinct platforms, ultracold atomic gases and atomically-thin transition metal dichalcogenides, which are linked by many deep parallels. We review polarons in both fermionic and bosonic environments, highlighting their similarities and differences including the intricate interplay between few- and many-body physics. Various kinds of polarons with long-range interactions or in magnetic backgrounds are discussed, and the theoretical and experimental progress towards understanding interactions between polarons is described. We outline how polaron physics, regarded as the low density limit of quantum mixtures, provides fundamental insights regarding the phase diagram of complex condensed matter systems. Furthermore, we describe how polarons may serve as quantum sensors of many-body physics in complex environments. Our work highlights the open problems, identifies new research directions and provides a comprehensive framework for this rapidly evolving research field.
articles.abstract_zh: 该工作全面综述了移动杂质与量子多体系统相互作用形成的极化子的理论和实验研究。它为超冷原子气体和原子级薄过渡金属二硫化物中的极化子提供了统一的视角，强调了其普遍概念和技术，并突出了少体与多体物理之间复杂的相互作用。文章讨论了各种具有长程相互作用或处于磁场背景下的极化子，以及极化子之间的相互作用。该综述还阐述了极化子物理如何为复杂凝聚态系统的相图提供基本见解，并可作为多体物理的量子传感器。
authors: Pietro Massignan, Richard Schmidt, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Ataç İmamoglu, Martin Zwierlein, Jan J. Arlt, Georg M. Bruun

articles.title: Multipolar exchange in a many-body homonuclear mixture of atoms in different internal states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.22375v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a general method for constructing the many-body Hamiltonian of pairwise interactions describing homonuclear mixtures of atoms occupying states with different total angular momenta or other quantum numbers. This Hamiltonian explicitly accounts for isotropic interactions governed by low-energy s-wave scattering. The advantage of the irreducible spherical tensor operator formalism is demonstrated: these operators give the Hamiltonian an explicit physical structure, account for all scattering channels, and include multipolar exchange interactions. The latter correspond to the exchange of both angular-momentum projections and the total angular momentum. Particular realizations of the general Hamiltonian, widely used in the physics of ultracold gases, are also analyzed. The resulting Hamiltonian provides a universal framework for investigating a broad range of quantum many-body phenomena in bosonic and fermionic atomic gases.
authors: M. Bulakhov, A. S. Peletminskii, Yu. V. Slyusarenko

articles.title: Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the symmetric Werner state
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper determines exactly the Rényi-2 entanglement of purification of the normalized symmetric Werner state in every local dimension dge2 beginequation* EoP₂₍W₊,d)=łog₂frac4d(d+1)d²⁺³d+4. endequation* We establish additivity for tensor power and, more generally, additivity for finite products of symmetric Werner states with different local dimensions. A canonical purification and its products achieve these values globally, even when arbitrary joint purifications with unrestricted finite dimensional auxiliary systems are allowed. We further examine perturbations away from the symmetric endpoint, and prove the continuity of the optimal value at this endpoint; moreover, we show a sharp square root order of variation in the optimal purity, while the canonical purification remains asymptotically optimal in the achieved entropy as this weight goes to zero.
authors: Shokoufe Faraji

articles.title: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks and their classical surrogates on long-range strongly correlated models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We benchmark quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) and their classical surrogates for phase differentiation in one-dimensional strongly correlated systems with beyond-nearest-neighbour terms. Using an anisotropic Heisenberg spin chain and an extended t-t' Fermi-Hubbard model as representative spin and fermionic testbeds, we train QCNN classifiers on labelled ground-state datasets and map out finite-size phase diagrams. In hybrid setups, we employ Pauli backpropagation to express the QCNN measurement as a weighted sum of Pauli-string expectation values to be evaluated directly on input states, and study how truncation parameters control the trade-off between approximation accuracy and the size of the resulting Pauli expansion. Robust convergence is achieved for the Heisenberg model under aggressive truncation, whereas the Fermi-Hubbard model requires substantially looser thresholds, resulting in a sharp growth in retained Pauli strings and evaluation cost. Our results contribute to charting where hybrid quantum-classical training is viable for learning strongly correlated quantum states, and provide practical guidance for choosing truncation regimes in Pauli backpropagation-based surrogates.
authors: Tatiana A. Bespalova, Réka Schwengelbeck, Laura Mismetti, Johannes Schachenmayer, Ivano Tavernelli, Francesco Tacchino

articles.title: Triple descent in quantum linear regression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum linear regression models, such as quantum extreme learning machines and quantum fidelity kernels, are trained on features that can only be estimated from finitely many measurement shots. Sampling noise is usually treated as a nuisance that more shots suppress; we show instead that it can fundamentally reshape the instabilities of the learning problem. As the number of measurement outcomes grows, the prediction error displays a triple-descent profile, with two peaks of fundamentally different origins. The first, classical, peak occurs when the measurement first becomes informationally complete, is a direct analogue of double descent in classical linear regression, and is caused by ill-conditioning of the measurement itself. This peak affects predictions only through their variance, and is thus suppressed by increasing the number of shots at inference. The second, quantum, peak occurs beyond informational completeness when the number of outcomes matches the number of training states: shot noise populates unphysical outcome combinations and the regression fits these pure-noise features with large weights, corrupting the learned model itself. More training or test shots cannot remove this quantum peak, which disappears only in the ideal limit of exact training features. Using random-matrix theory, we derive the shape of both peaks analytically, accounting also for ridge regularization. Our results show that treating quantum features as exactly known overestimates classical instabilities while missing genuinely quantum ones.
authors: Gabriele Lo Monaco, Salvatore Lorenzo, Alessandro Ferraro, Mauro Paternostro, G. Massimo Palma, Luca Innocenti

articles.title: Application a quantum machine learning algorithm to the applied problem of modeling the thermal regime of a servers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly developed field of science. In the NISC era, quantum machine learning stands out, potentially outperforming classical machine learning. In this paper, we explore the applicability of quantum machine learning to a real-world application. We solved the problem of prediction of the temperature of GPUs in a high-performance computing cluster. We trained a quantum circuit to predict the temperature of each of the eight GPU of each cluster node based on 16 physical parameters. We demonstrated that quantum machine learning performs on this task just as well as classical machine learning. Furthermore, using model problems, we demonstrated that quantum machine learning can potentially outperform classical machine learning.
authors: P. V. Buzin, M. A. Remnev

articles.title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.
authors: Eduardo Martín-Martínez, Ireneo James Membrere, Adam Teixidó-Bonfill

articles.title: Early Fault-Tolerant Magic State Synthesis and Spacetime Efficient Analog Rotations with Color Code on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With recent improvements to syndrome extraction scheduling and decoding, and the availability of complete transversal Clifford operations and lattice surgery, color code is an especially promising platform for quantum processors with local connectivity. The key ingredient for universal computation is thus generating useful magic states with limited resources. Space-Time Efficient Analog Rotations (STAR) and Fault-tolerant magic state synthesis (MSS) are two such methods for magic state generation, targeted for near-term and long-term quantum computing, respectively. In this work, we perform the first implementations of both magic state paradigms on a superconducting quantum processor. We present a STAR-type injection protocol on the color code, with favorable error rate and spacetime costs versus prior protocols on both the color and surface codes. We then implement a MSS factory by performing multi-patch magic state cultivations, interleaved with transversal Clifford operations, and lattice-surgery magic state teleportation. Under post-selection, we achieve a kickback tomography correct sign probability of 99.9859% on cultivated T_L states, 96% tomographic fidelity on logical analog rotation states, and 91% fidelity on synthesized logical magic states consuming 3 cultivated T_L states, 3 transversal Hadamard operations, and real-time feed-forward S_L corrections during magic state teleportation. We compare the efficacy of post-selection, Most-Likely-Error (MLE) decoding, and concatenated-matching decoding throughout, highlighting the potential of end-to-end color code computation.
authors: Sean Garner, Aaron Hoyt, Shuwen Kan, Samuel Stein, Chenxu Liu, Ang Li

articles.title: Measurement-angle control of a continuously monitored quantum oscillator: purification limits and optimal protocols
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dynamic purification of a continuously monitored quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a thermal bath, where the control is the quadrature measurement angle of up to two detectors with prescribed strengths and efficiencies. Within the Gaussian regime, the conditional state covariance obeys a deterministic Riccati equation, and we ask what purity can be reached and sustained by manipulating the angle in time, in analogy with rapid-purification protocols for qubits. We propose, analyze, and compare constant-rate, greedy, vibrational, and variational monitoring strategies on the basis of sustained purity starting from the thermal bath state, and quantify to what extent they are able to maintain higher purity levels compared to lab-fixed or phase-locked detectors. We highlight structural features, operational limits, and optimal protocols from each strategy and study how model parameters shape control performance. We observe that in the absence of measurement-frame anisotropy, the time-dependent strategies achieve higher but similar performance. Once this symmetry is broken, their performances diverge, either improving or worsening depending on the relative timescales of oscillator dynamics, thermalization, and measurement.
authors: Ralph Sabbagh, Olga Movilla Miangolarra, Andrew N. Jordan, Tryphon T. Georgiou

articles.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 textmum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 textmum is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 textmum has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 textmum. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 textmum relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.
authors: Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi

articles.title: Scaling Laws for Parameter Setting in Digitized Counterdiabatic QAOA
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing parameters separately for each problem instance limits the reuse of variational quantum algorithms. We develop empirical scaling laws for parameter setting in the digitized counterdiabatic quantum approximate optimization algorithm (DC-QAOA) for weighted MaxCut. The prescription combines exact covariance under uniform edge-weight rescaling with power laws in mean degree fitted separately to offline-optimized cost and counterdiabatic angles. After the weight and degree scales are removed, the optimized angles of different training graphs cluster around common amplitudes, so a small coefficient table suffices. Frozen coefficients assign angles from a target graph's mean degree and root-mean-square edge weight without target-instance variational optimization. In ideal-circuit simulations across 1050 test graphs spanning ten graph families and five positive edge-weight distributions, mean optimal-solution probability is higher than that of the fixed-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) at each depth from one to four layers, reaching 19.36% versus 13.11% at four layers. A six-layer extension on 600 graphs also shows a mean probability advantage. Hardware execution on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_fez for 21 unit-weight 3-regular graphs shows a mean probability advantage at one layer, while the ordering reverses at two layers. In separate energy-based experiments, direct assignment gives a higher mean approximation ratio than random-start optimization reaches within 500 evaluations, and refinement started from the formula angles improves it further. These results show how a scaling-based representation of optimized angles can guide parameter reuse across graph instances, enabling direct parameter assignment without target-instance variational optimization and providing initial angles for local refinement.
authors: Yaocheng Chen, Jiapei Zhuang

articles.title: Enhanced shortcuts to adiabaticity in an interacting giant-atom-atomic-waveguide system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In realistic quantum systems, isolated few-level models usually provide only an approximate description, since the controlled subsystem is generally coupled to additional degrees of freedom. As a result, a quantum control scheme designed for an isolated system may lose its original performance in a more complex coupled setting. Here, we consider a giant atom coupled to an interacting atomic waveguide and investigate enhanced shortcuts to adiabaticity (eSTA) in such a structured system. As a first step, a weak-coupling perturbative analysis identifies how changes in the initial and target states, together with dynamical transitions, contribute to the fidelity loss. Starting from a shortcut to adiabaticity control scheme for the uncoupled system, the enhanced STA correction improves the final fidelity by modifying only the giant-atom control fields. This improvement is found for both periodic and open boundary conditions of the atomic waveguide. The results demonstrate a way to design an eSTA protocol for an interacting composite system.
authors: Ruijin Sun, Zhihai Wang, Andreas Ruschhaupt

articles.title: Implications of the PXP ground-state sign structure for neural-network variational Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positive-definite neural-network quantum states cannot directly represent the ground state of the PXP Hamiltonian, since the ground-state wavefunction carries a nontrivial relative-sign structure. Building on the chiral symmetry of the PXP Hamiltonian, we show that this sign structure is fixed exactly by the parity of the total up-spin number: a diagonal unitary transformation that assigns a sign to each spin configuration according to this parity maps the PXP Hamiltonian to its negative, rendering the transformed Hamiltonian stoquastic on the Rydberg-blockaded Hilbert space. Since the configuration graph of allowed configurations is connected, the Perron-Frobenius theorem guarantees a unique, strictly positive ground state of the transformed Hamiltonian, yielding an exact sign rule for the ground state of the original Hamiltonian in terms of the parity of the up-spin number. Variational Monte Carlo performed directly on the transformed Hamiltonian with a positive-definite ansatz therefore requires no architecture-specific modification to represent the true ground state. We evaluate the performance of this formulation using five representative neural-network quantum state architectures, SineKAN, reflection-symmetrized SineKAN, RBM, MLP, and LSTM, for different chain lengths.
authors: Jun Sur Richard Park, Kwangmin Yu

articles.title: Compressed Oracle Duality: A simple framework for knowing what quantum adversaries know
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a quantum adversary that queries a random oracle, how do we characterize the information that they "know"? The Compressed Oracle method of Zhandry (CRYPTO 2019) is one method that records the queries that the adversary makes; this recording serves as a representation of the information that is learned. However, a significant limitation of the Compressed Oracle method is that it may continue to store information that the adversary has "forgotten." This issue is especially pertinent in the space-bounded setting, where the adversary may uncompute information to free up space, while the information may still reside in the compressed oracle. In this work, we present a simple and interpretable framework called "Compressed Oracle Duality," which extends the Compressed Oracle method for space-bounded algorithms. By applying an isometry to the memory of a quantum adversary, we obtain a pair of compressed oracles with identical marginal distributions and classical correlations which correspond to the knowledge the adversary retains. In fact, we show that the outcome of measuring the new compressed oracle database corresponds exactly to applying the pretty-good measurement on the adversary's memory. As an application of our framework for collision search, we give a simplified proof of the recent T²S = Ømega(Nłog N) quantum time-space tradeoff for label-symmetric algorithms due to Magniez-Zur (arXiv:2609.10808); we also prove a stronger classical tradeoff of TS=Ømega(Nłog N) assuming label symmetry. The proofs under our framework do not require representation theory and instead bound the mutual information between the compressed oracle pairs. This highlights both how the label symmetry assumption bypasses known proof barriers as well as the challenges that remain in achieving unconditional quantum time-space tradeoffs.
authors: Matthew Ding, Mark Zhandry

articles.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Here we introduce an artificial intelligence-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent, equipped with tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. We apply the workflow to three previously published experimental cavity-QED datasets collected from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. Across the experiments, the agent successfully identifies physical models for the system and characterizes the disorder. In assessing reproducibility, we find that run-to-run variability is concentrated primarily in the research plan generation step, while the computational analysis itself is substantially more consistent. Our results suggest that structured LLM agent workflows can support model discovery from quantum optical experimental data while simultaneously allowing for human expert supervision and collaboration.
authors: Hannah C. Kleidermacher, Bennet Windt, Miguel Bello, James Zou, Jelena Vučković

articles.title: Coherence controls the visibility of frozen disorder in an open quantum chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Gaussian position distribution need not imply that frozen disorder is irrelevant. We study a resonant quantum chain where neighboring sites couple with opposite signs to auxiliary states that decay with frozen, random return probabilities. Lowering dephasing spreads the effect of each local return bias over more sites. We take dephasing to zero at a fixed, sufficiently weak disorder amplitude. On the scale of a coherent wave packet, the position distribution approaches the same Gaussian for almost every frozen sample. At larger distances and later times, it remains sample dependent and is described by diffusion in a random potential with Brownian spatial statistics. The covariance of bounded, direction-sensitive position readouts from independent trials in the same field distinguishes these regimes. Simulations resolve their separation at finite dephasing. Taking weak disorder before vanishing dephasing also reveals a different packet-scale response from a memoryless random-force model matched in clean diffusion and leading potential strength. The coherent response develops an integrable logarithmic peak near the initial site, where the reference response stays finite. It reflects the correlated duration and displacement of motion between jumps, together with the unfinished packet at measurement.
authors: S. Y. Li, M. H. Yu, X. Z. Zhang

articles.title: Multicopy teleportation and quantum program retrieval on superconducting quantum hardware
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Correction-free teleportation protocols offer a probabilistic route around the limits imposed by the quantum no-programming theorem, but have remained largely theoretical. Here, we experimentally implement and benchmark correction-free multicopy teleportation on noisy superconducting quantum hardware. Key to this is an efficient circuit implementation: by suitably decomposing the unitary that maps the multicopy measurement basis onto the computational basis, we substantially reduce circuit depth and gate count. For one- and two-qubit input states, using k=2 and 3 copies, we observe success probabilities substantially exceeding the single-copy bound with fidelities above 0.85. We further explore applications to probabilistic programmable quantum processors, in particular the storage and retrieval of unitary operations encoded in quantum program states. Our results establish the practical feasibility of multicopy teleportation and highlight its potential for near-term quantum processors and distributed quantum computing.
authors: Yousef Mafi, Ali G. Moghaddam

articles.title: Experimental Realization of a Nonreciprocal Quantum Battery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum batteries promise faster and more efficient energy storage and extraction by harnessing quantum mechanics, serving as essential building blocks for future quantum devices. A key practical requirement-unidirectional energy flow during charging-is straightforward in classical batteries via potential difference, yet remains a major challenge in the quantum regime due to the inherent reciprocity of coherent coupling. Here, we realize the first backflow-free, nonreciprocal quantum battery in the few-quantum regime, implemented in a highly controlled trapped-ion system via a qubit-reservoir engineering technique. By subtly tailoring quantum interference between coherent and dissipative couplings of two laser-cooled motional modes, we achieve strictly unidirectional energy flow from the charger to the battery. We observe maximum charging power at an exceptional point and demonstrate a complete charge-discharge cycle with unitary work extraction. This work establishes the foundation for directional energy transfer and storage in micro- and nanoscale quantum devices, with broad implications for nonreciprocal energy harvesting, precision metrology, information processing, and quantum thermodynamics.
authors: Jie Zhang, Xin-Sheng Chen, Ruo Kun Cai, Gang Xia, Jia-Yang Song, Fu-Wen Zhao, Ting Chen, Wei Wu, Yi Xie, Zhi Jiao Deng, Chun-Wang Wu, Ping-Xing Chen

articles.title: Quantum Mpemba effect of Z2 symmetry restoration in the Dicke model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a symmetry-restoration quantum Mpemba effect in the dissipative Dicke model as an example of a weakly mathbb Z₂₋ₛymmetric open quantum system, where the full Liouvillian is parity covariant although individual quantum jumps connect the two Hilbert-space parity sectors. Using the entanglement-asymmetry (EA) diagnostic to monitor parity restoration, we compare coherent-product and cat-product initial states. Coherent-product states show conventional relaxation, with larger initial asymmetry decaying more slowly and no Mpemba crossing observed. Cat-product states, by contrast, can reverse this hierarchy over a finite region of initial-state space. This reversal is enabled by initial-state mode filtering: the cat-product superposition suppresses the contributions of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, allowing a more asymmetric state to restore parity through faster decay channels. Our results reveal that symmetry-restoration QME can arise even when parity is preserved only as a weak Liouvillian symmetry, with quantum jumps mixing the Hilbert-space parity sectors. The anomalous relaxation is governed by initial-state-dependent filtering of the leading slow Liouvillian modes, providing a mechanism for symmetry-restoration QME beyond strongly conserved symmetry sectors.
authors: Dongni Chen, Wei Xiong, Peng-Cheng Li, Yee Sin Ang, Ching Hua Lee, Yi Qin

articles.title: Binary Quantum Hypothesis Testing with a Rejection Option: The Exact Error-Exponent Trade-off
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the exact error-exponent trade-off in binary quantum hypothesis testing with a rejection option for faithful states on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. The probabilities of rejection under the two hypotheses are required to vanish exponentially, with exponents at least K and L. We show that a quadruple (a,b,K,L) of positive error and rejection exponents is achievable if and only if it satisfies three single-letter conditions: two conditions involve Petz--Rényi quantities and coincide with the converse bound conjectured to be tight by Ji and Regula; the third involves the α--z Rényi quantities on the triangle maxα,1-αłe złe1. The proof combines a sector decomposition inside Schur--Weyl blocks, an explicit one-shot measurement construction, and an exact minimax argument.
authors: Yonglong Li

articles.title: Single-Mode Squeezing Using Degenerate Four-Wave Mixing in a Dual-Pump TWPA
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-mode squeezing of the electromagnetic vacuum is a key resource for mode-selective noise reduction in quantum measurements. At microwave frequencies, single-mode squeezing is typically obtained by using Josephson and Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers designed for three-wave mixing operation. In single-pump degenerate four-wave mixing, the coincidence of pump, signal, and idler frequencies complicates separation of the squeezed field from the strong pump. A dual-pump configuration enables degenerate operation while keeping both pumps spectrally separated from the squeezed mode. Here, we demonstrate single-mode squeezing in a flux-tunable, dual-pump Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier, employing reversed-Kerr phase matching. By independently calibrating the single-pump gains, we find that the strongest squeezing occurs along approximately balanced-gain trajectories, while the optimal squeezing does not necessarily correspond to the highest dual-pump gain. At flux biases Φₑₓₜ/Φ₀ = 0.0 and 0.5, the minimum quadrature noise levels reach -2.48 ± 0.18~dB and -1.62 ± 0.20~dB relative to vacuum, respectively. These results establish the proposed architecture as a platform for single-mode squeezing in microwave continuous-variable quantum technologies.
authors: Anna Levochkina, Kirill Petrovnin, Iiro Harju, Jiaming Wang, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu

articles.title: Normal Factor Graph Representations of Stabilizer Quantum Codes with Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop normal factor graph (NFG) representations of stabilizer quantum error-correcting codes and entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes. We introduce two complementary representations. Quantum-code NFGs describe stabilizer and normalizer label codes and provide a graphical framework for establishing self-orthogonality, constructing codes from component codes, and identifying encoding and decoding circuits. Quantum-probability NFGs represent the quantum-mechanical probabilities associated with encoding, noise, and measurement. We also introduce a doubleedge formulation that makes the relationship between these two representations explicit. We apply the framework to convolutional and tail-biting convolutional stabilizer codes, as well as to two classes of low-density parity-check stabilizer codes. Finally, we extend the quantum-probability representation to entanglementassisted codes.
authors: July X. Li, Pascal O. Vontobel

articles.title: On Estimating Quantum Divergences with p-Power Means
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the problem of estimating the quantum divergence with p-power means, Φₚ₍ₕ̊o,|,σ). This quantity was investigated by Lam and Le (Linear Algebra Appl. 2021). For any constant p in (0, 1), we present sample-efficient and query-efficient quantum algorithms for estimating Φₚ₍ₕ̊o,|,σ) and further show that estimating Φₚ₍ₕ̊o,|,σ) is mathsfBQP-complete in the low-rank case.
authors: Jinge Bao, Minbo Gao, Qisheng Wang

articles.title: All-to-All Connectivity in Superconducting Qubits via Metamaterial-Mediated Interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling lengthens every gate. The encoding suppresses this coupling at the hardware level, from second to fourth order in the inverse qubit--mode detuning. A two-tone cross-resonance drive then generates a Mølmer-Sørensen interaction between encoded qubits, which we use for an entangling gate and a joint parity measurement, both selective and parallelizable through different modes. Simulating two dual-rail transmons sharing three resonators with a mode lifetime of 30,μs, we find that heralding transmon relaxation as erasure leaves a gate infidelity of 1.4×10⁻³ at 152~ns, dominated by photon loss. Photon loss and mode crowding together bound the array size. The gate duration must exceed the inverse mode spacing, which shrinks as the array lengthens, while photon loss grows with gate duration. This bound grows linearly with the mode lifetime and with the inter-resonator coupling; at a lifetime of 150,μs, five times the simulated value, and a coupling of 80~MHz, a 10⁻³ error budget admits 13 qubits on 25 resonators.
authors: Or Golan, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Andreas Butler, Gihwan Kim, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Oskar Painter, Alex Retzker

articles.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for N identical d-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of Łambda and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where g⁽²⁾(0) is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.
authors: Stephan Hartmann

articles.title: Persistence of Fractal Structures in Iterated Quantum Protocols: Robustness to Preparation and Gate Errors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeatedly combining entangling gates on an ensemble of qubits with measurement and postselection on a part of them induces a nonlinear evolution of the unmeasured qubits' state, whose fractal convergence boundaries make the outcome sensitive to the initial state. We study a family of iterated protocols in which n identical qubits are coupled by CNOT gates, n-1 of them are postselected, and a parametrized single-qubit unitary acts on the survivor. For orders n=2 to 5, we map the box-counting dimension of the pure-state Julia sets over the complex parameter plane and identify the symmetries that constrain it. Allowing mixed initial states, we find that moderate preparation noise preserves the main parameter-dependent trends of the boundary dimension over much of the studied range, and that the three-dimensional quasi-Julia boundary in the Bloch ball has a dimension that is approximately equal to the dimension of the pure-state Julia set plus one. We further model gate imperfections by an effective depolarizing channel and by fixed coherent interactions. Weak errors leave the estimated dimensions consistent with their ideal values even where the convergence regions visibly deform, and ZZ errors are shown to be exactly conjugate to the ideal protocol at a rotated parameter. Finally, we analyze the postselection and storage cost of an implementation and propose a diagnostic test combining conditional fidelity with acceptance statistics, which we demonstrate on IQM Emerald and Rigetti Cepheus-1-108Q.
authors: Attila Portik, Orsolya Kálmán, Tamás Kiss

articles.title: Chaos, Fractals, and Ergodicity in Nonlinear Quantum Protocols
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iterated nonlinear quantum protocols provide a straightforward way of realizing nonlinear dynamics in quantum systems through measurement and postselection. We investigate a family of protocols in which the order of the induced nonlinearity is controlled by the number of qubits involved in a single step. By examining the resulting rational maps and applying a set of numerical diagnostics, we identify extended parameter regions that exhibit ergodic-like dynamics for protocol orders n=3,4, and 5. We further characterize the associated chaotic behavior through the distribution of Lyapunov exponents. Our results show that ergodic-like dynamics persists beyond the quadratic case, while the geometry of the corresponding parameter regions and the typical degree of chaoticity depend strongly on the order of the nonlinear transformation.
authors: Attila Portik, Orsolya Kálmán, Tamás Kiss

articles.title: Model-Based Fast Calibration for a Nitrogen Vacancy Center QPU
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a simulation-informed calibration workflow for NV quantum processing units that combines a digital twin, optimal control pulses, and a Fisher-information-guided experiment design into an iterative parameter estimation feedback loop. We find that using this framework, we obtain the same calibration precision as standard techniques with up to 4x reduction in measurement time.
authors: Tobias F. Sjolander, Marco Rossignolo, Lorena C. Bianchet, Swathi Hegde, Anurag Saha Roy, Thomas Lippert, Manpreet Singh Jattana

articles.title: Hidden selection rules and amplitude ceilings in quantum Fourier models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum models with Pauli data encodings compute trigonometric polynomials whatever channels, ancillas and outcome-averaged measurements follow, so their expressivity depends on the Fourier coefficients a circuit can reach. We identify two kinds of structure that settle this before training. An antiunitary time-reversal rule and a unitary reflection rule remove frequencies. For gate-level circuits, deciding whether such a rule exists reduces to a linear system over GF(2), solvable in polynomial time, and the time-reversal rule holds in 17.6% of 6,120 configurations of standard templates. Single-upload encodings cap the top coefficient at 2⁻m for every channel, and we compute the tight ceiling for every frequency and a depth-independent re-uploading bound. Frozen before training, these bounds were never violated on a non-linearity benchmark, and they predicted trained performance on real data. On IBM processors the rule held on a 65-qubit chain, and we switched rule-breaking relaxation noise on and off by design.
authors: Pavel Sulimov, Claude Lehmann

articles.title: Floquet engineering of quantum relaxation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamical decoupling suppresses decoherence by averaging selected interactions between a quantum system and its environment. Here, we extend this notion through a general Floquet formalism that maps periodic control onto relaxation and dephasing channels. Environmental fluctuations are decomposed into Floquet components that sample the noise spectrum at distinct frequencies, with coupling strengths determined by control-induced Floquet coefficients. We experimentally investigate this approach using a single nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond under multi-pulse control. By tuning the drive and detuning, we reshape the coupling to environmental fluctuations and create isolated operating points where the dominant decoherence channel vanishes, strongly suppressing Floquet dephasing. The resulting coherence enhancement follows the predicted Floquet coupling coefficients and can be shifted by modifying the control sequence. These results establish Floquet driving as a general framework for engineering transverse and longitudinal relaxation through the design of quantum control protocols.
authors: Kang Xu, Dionisio Cendoya, Nazar Delegan, Daniela Pagliero, Lisandro Buljubasich, Carlos A. Meriles

articles.title: Logical-Class Diagnostic Layer for Stabilizer Codes and Decoders via Supercharge Structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a decoder-agnostic logical-class diagnostic layer for abelian Pauli stabilizer codes, motivated by fault-tolerant quantum computing. An ancilla fermionic register defines a nilpotent supercharge whose clean degree-zero harmonic sector is the code space. Projected-return blocks derived from graded commutators organize the recovery test of whether a decoder-selected correction preserves every encoded input for every error in a declared same-syndrome family; the passing syndromes form the certified faithful window. Demoting the supercharge to an exact binary diagnostic formulation classifies residuals modulo stabilizers, separating a check violation, a harmless stabilizer residual, and a syndrome-silent nontrivial logical action, with a two-sector form for CSS codes. Because the unknown fault cancels, the relative logical class of two record-compatible candidates is computable online. We verify the diagnostic formalisms on the Steane code and specify a static--circuit bridge audit protocol for the Gross bivariate-bicycle quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code. The method supplements existing decoders without additional physical qubits for software use.
authors: Hai Lin

articles.title: A GPU-Accelerated and Geometry-Aware Quantum-Classical Framework for Optimized PES Scans with CUDA-Q
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workloads, particularly Potential Energy Surface (PES) scans in quantum chemistry using batched VQE and QAOA, involve many structurally similar Hamiltonians differing only in coefficients. Existing warm-start and meta-optimization strategies reuse parameters between instances but still consume fixed quantum-classical resources, ignoring cross-instance structural similarities. We present OptiPESS, a GPU-accelerated runtime system for adaptive resource allocation in hybrid quantum-classical execution. OptiPESS introduces the Locality-Occupancy-Variance (LOV) metric, a lightweight, geometry-aware measure of Hamiltonian similarity, coupled with efficient alignment and Pauli-classification passes. Using LOV, OptiPESS performs distance-aware scheduling of iteration and shot budgets, predicting which instances can be skipped, quick-solved, or fully optimized. Implemented atop CUDA-Q with persistent multi-GPU execution and near-linear scaling, OptiPESS reduces classical and quantum evaluations by up to 78.3% and wall-time by up to 74.8% while maintaining baseline accuracy. This demonstrates how lightweight static analysis and adaptive scheduling can transform quantum-classical co-execution from fixed-budget loops into a predictive, resource-aware runtime.
authors: Panayiotis Christou, Shuwen Kan, Ying Mao

articles.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.
authors: Youngrong Lim

articles.title: Bounds and sufficient conditions in quantum Zeno effect
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a quantum system undergoes a series of repeated measurements during its time evolution to check whether it remains in the initial state, the resulting state lifetime can decrease (the quantum Zeno effect) or increase (the quantum inverse Zeno effect) as the inter-measurement period increases. Several transitions between these two regimes may occur within the same system. A carefully chosen measurement period τₐₛₜ (or rate rₐₛₜ in the case of a stochastic measurement protocol) brings the state lifetime to its global minimum. Here, we describe the upper and lower bounds on the optimized state lifetime, which are expressed in terms of characteristic time scales encoded in the state survival probability P(T), which is assumed to decrease monotonically to zero at large T. In addition, we analyze the bounds on the optimal measurement periods/rates and formulate sufficient conditions for observing the inverse Zeno effect. The analysis is also extended to states with non-monotonic survival functions. The results are illustrated numerically with an example of a system of optically trapped ultra-cold atoms.
authors: Vladimir Parfenyev, Sergey Belan

articles.title: An Observable-Algebra Approach to Quantum Coherence in Anyonic Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical restrictions on operations can make quantum coherence inaccessible. Quantifying off-diagonal density matrix elements in a chosen basis alone does not reveal which information is hidden by each restriction. To distinguish their effects, we describe physical restrictions through subalgebras of accessible observables. The associated trace-preserving conditional expectations unify two reconstruction principles: each gives both the maximum-entropy state compatible with the accessible data and the closest state in the corresponding subalgebra in relative entropy. We apply this framework to anyonic systems to separate the contributions from local-charge superselection and non-Abelian fusion rules. We prove that the charge-line severing map is the conditional expectation onto the local-product subalgebra. It is completely positive and quantum-trace-preserving, and uniquely reconstructs a state in this space from all local-product expectation values. The hierarchy of measurement restrictions then separates total bipartite coherence into three nonnegative contributions: coherence between local charges, inaccessible fusion information, and conventional coherence. The first two decompose the anyonic charge entanglement and distinguish the effects of local-charge superselection from the remaining fusion information. Finally, we relate basis-independent measures of anyonic coherence to entanglement. For pure anyonic states with vacuum total charge, the optimized total and correlated coherence equal the total and conventional relative-entropy entanglement, respectively.
authors: Cheng-Qian Xu, D. L. Zhou

articles.title: Quantum Lower Bounds for Collision Problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish tight lower bounds on the adaptive and non-adaptive quantum query complexities of Promised k-to-one Finding on an exactly k-to-one input string xinmathbb Z_qⁿ, for every fixed kge2 and every feasible alphabet size qge n/k. The lower bounds are Ømegaₖ₍ₙ¹/²⁻¹/⁽²⁽²^k⁻¹⁾⁾) for unrestricted adaptive algorithms and Ømegaₖ₍ₙ¹⁻¹/k) for one-round non-adaptive algorithms. The former matches the adaptive quantum algorithm of Liu and Zhandry [LZ19], whereas the latter matches classical birthday sampling even when the parallel queries are arbitrarily entangled. We also establish the non-adaptive lower bound Ømegaₖ₍sqrtn/k) for k-to-one Testing when qge n, resolving an open question posed by Koiran, Landes, Portier, and Yao [KLPY10]. Our proofs generate the balanced input from a uniformly random permutation and use compressed permutation oracles to describe the information learned by the algorithm. The adaptive proof bounds the growth of partial collisions through successive queries. The one-round proof instead analyzes the state after the parallel queries directly, bounding the probability that the compressed database contains a full collision. In both proofs, a short verification step accounts for correct outputs that include unrecorded positions. For the decision problem, we also compare one-round states with independent and distinct output labels.
authors: Pan Peng, Jingyu Wu

articles.title: Quantum Recovery from Black-Hole Radiation Beyond the Emission Yield
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A proposed resolution of the black-hole information paradox must explain which information an outside observer can recover from escaping radiationi̧teHawking,Page,Hayden,Almheiri. Environmental memory can return correlations to the source without delivering them to that observeri̧teChenQi,ChenMemory. Here we establish a sharp recovery frontier at fixed mean radiation yield for single-excitation channels and realize its qubit limit with an autonomous quantum-memory emitter. Unequal transmissions balance retained coherence against information in failed collection events. A reference--radiation correlation test distinguishes this gain even when the mean collected energy is unchanged. Identical transmission channels instead give the same recovery at matched collection, regardless of their emission timescales. For a broader class of interacting sources, an ordering of collected and inaccessible coupling spectra forbids unassisted quantum transmission irrespective of internal memory. A separate coding example supports a positive rate where uniform transmission at matched actual yield has zero capacity. Together, these results identify what openness must change to assist recovery: the accessible transmission structure. They supply a physically constrained comparison of evaporation mechanisms, separating information delivered to radiation from coherence retained elsewhere or an increase in the collected output.
authors: Kashif Ammar Yasir

articles.title: Long-term yields of short-rate models as Feynman-Kac ground states: a variational quantum eigensolver with single-setting energy estimation on two NISQ platforms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the long-term yield of a short-rate model is the ground-state energy of a Schrodinger operator obtained from the Feynman-Kac bond-pricing equation, so that it can be computed by a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). We treat the Vasicek, Cox-Ingersoll-Ross and Black-Karasinski models; the last has no closed form. Calibrated monthly to the U.S. Treasury curve from 1985 to 2026, the long-term yield follows the 30-year yield with an in-sample correlation of 0.98. The Hamiltonian is stoquastic, so its ground state is positive and the energy can be estimated from computational-basis samples with a single measurement setting. On ibm_cleveland, gate noise appears mainly as bit flips of the high-order qubits. A bit-flip deconvolution with a tail set fixed by a WKB criterion, combined with readout mitigation and zero-noise extrapolation, gives four-qubit estimates within 33-125 bp of the grid ground-state energies for all three models, and within 23-67 bp for Treasury-calibrated parameters. On IonQ Forte Enterprise the same analysis reduces the error in the same proportions. On the same circuits, a Pauli-measurement VQE deviates by 791-1,129 bp, so the single-setting estimator gives about ten times smaller errors with one setting instead of nine. An on-device VQE converges from 4,939 bp to 130 bp.
authors: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Department of Electrical,Computer Engineering, University of Seoul, Seoul 02504, Republic of Korea,,Singularity Quantum Inc., Newport Beach, CA 92660, USA)

articles.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, the decomposition needs no approximation: each class's probability above its no-information share splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM) over the picture and measurable on the hardware that classifies. For the quadratic form behind each class probability it equals Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline, in closed form. Deleting the 5 % of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73 % to 9 %, as occlusion does with 1,024 extra runs per picture, whereas gradient saliency removes much less. One architecture serves both: a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at a single wavelength reach 72.3 % on Caltech-10 colour photographs (96.8 % on MNIST, 86.7 % on Fashion-MNIST, 47.9 % on colour CIFAR-10). On IBM's ibmₖᵢₙgston, with the mask applied before approximate loading, 300 Caltech-10 test pictures were classified at 37.7 % against 10 % by chance (56.3 % in exact simulation), and 2x2 maps of ten correctly and confidently classified pictures, estimated on the chip, agreed with the exact ones (r = 0.77). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data.
authors: Teerawat Tongloy, Rangsan Jomtarak

articles.title: Rule-based hardware-configurable static analysis for quantum programs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid evolution of quantum hardware necessitates an adaptable static analysis framework for validating quantum programs. In this work, we introduce SHARP, a rule-based static analysis framework designed for OpenQASM that decouples hardware-specific constraints from the validation engine. By employing a rule-based approach, SHARP allows quantum computing services to validate programs against evolving instruction set architectures (ISAs) without having to modify the core analysis engine. SHARP achieves this by ingesting ISA descriptions as standalone data, making the validation engine resilient to hardware updates. Furthermore, the framework employs an analysis-driven validation mechanism that enables multi-stage validation, simplifying rule construction and enhancing extensibility. We demonstrate how SHARP supports hardware-specific validation tasks and discuss its impact on quantum software development, including language decoupling, program-level constraint validation, and feature access control. Our findings suggest that SHARP provides a path toward a scalable and maintainable programming interface for quantum computing.
authors: Yi-Ting Chen, Lauren Capelluto, Ryan Shaffer, Jeffrey Heckey

articles.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
authors: Mladen Pavicic

articles.title: Interaction order sets the onset cost of steady-state quantum magic
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maintaining quantum magic under continuous noise requires coherent control and a supply of purity. We determine the cost of local stabilizer replacement resets sustaining any positive stationary magic in autonomous qubit networks with depolarization rate γ, interactions on at most k sites, and Hamiltonian strength J per site. An exact global stabilizer decomposition and a matching finite construction give the optimal onset scaling γ(γ/J)¹/⁽k⁻¹⁾, uniformly over network size and noisy ancillas. For two-body interactions, the leading maximal-reset-rate coefficient is 1/(2sqrt2) for every fixed finite size Nge2, allowing mixed reset targets and heterogeneous rates. The same coefficient holds uniformly over growing networks with pure Pauli targets and equal reset rates. The converse combines hafnian stabilizer geometry with a positive random-order forest expansion.
authors: Mingdi Xu

articles.title: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detection times are routinely recorded in quantum experiments. We show that, under natural covariance and consistency requirements, the observables describing these times cannot be algebraically localized in any bounded spacetime region, even when the records themselves are localized. This challenges the identification of algebraic localization with the physical localization of measurements and shows why microcausality alone does not establish non-signalling for measurements in quantum field theory.
authors: Charis Anastopoulos, Ntina Savvidou

articles.title: Sound-wave interference reveals the symmetry of a quantum transition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A single sound quantum emitted from two places interferes with itself, like a particle passing through two slits. The fringe position reveals whether the sources emit with the same sign (symmetric) or opposite signs (antisymmetric). Knowing this symmetry is important because qubits in solids lose energy by emitting such sound quanta, phonons. For a qubit shared between two sites, antisymmetric emission cancels at long wavelengths, suppressing energy loss, whereas symmetric emission does not. Lifetime measurements give only the total loss and cannot distinguish them. Such fringes appear in double quantum dots, but their position has not been analysed. Here we measure it for single phonons emitted as one hole tunnels between two gallium arsenide quantum dots. Using a quantitative model of sound focusing in the crystal, we find that the two dots emit antisymmetrically, as expected for a moving charge, with only a small symmetric part. Spin-flip transitions in a magnetic field weaken the fringes without shifting them. For double-dot charge qubits, antisymmetric emission is predicted to reduce phonon losses strongly at the frequencies where qubits operate, and phonon interferometry gives a direct way to measure how qubits release energy and to design longer-lived qubits.
authors: Sergei Studenikin, Yousef Karimi Yonjali, Alex Bogan, Andy Sachrajda, Shabir Barzanjeh

articles.title: From Fabrication Disorder to Quantum-Protocol Yield in Inverse-Designed Silicon Photonic Beam Splitters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Telecom-band silicon spin-photon qubits offer a promising platform for scalable quantum networks and distributed information processing, but their fixed emission wavelengths require compact, low-loss beam splitters with precise splitting and fabrication robustness. Conventional designs can face trade-offs between footprint, optical performance, and wavelength-specific operation. Here, we employ adjoint-based inverse design to optimize photonic geometries beyond conventional layouts, developing 1*2 Y-splitters and 2*2 directional couplers for the silicon T (1326 nm) and Al1 (1482.44 nm) spin-photon qubits. The devices achieve footprints of 2.9 and 26 um², respectively, with excess losses of 0.14-0.44 dB and back-reflection below 5*10⁻⁴. We assess fabrication tolerance using 100-realization Monte Carlo simulations incorporating etch bias, line-edge roughness, thickness, and refractive-index variations. Mirror symmetry reduces the splitting-ratio spread of the Y-splitter by a factor of seven to nine relative to the directional coupler. We translate these variations into dual-rail fidelity, ideal splitting-ratio-limited Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility, and random-number min-entropy. All realizations satisfy a protocol-performance threshold of 0.95. At 0.99, the tolerated splitting-ratio deviation shrinks from 0.035 for visibility to 0.0035 for min-entropy, and the simulated yields are 68% (T) and 91% (Al1) for coupler visibility and 90% (T) and 66% (Al1) for Y-splitter min-entropy. The tolerance of the target protocol, rather than the device alone, therefore sets the fabrication requirement for silicon spin-photon beam splitters.
authors: Nail Letty, Tahmeed Ul Islam, Wayesh Qarony

articles.title: What is the connection between quantum relationality and symmetry-based relationality?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although it has often been noted that both quantum mechanics and relativistic physics involve significant forms of relationality, the nature of the connection remains unclear. In addressing such a question it makes sense to start from the simplest possibility, so in this article I set out to consider the viability of the hypothesis that the two types of relationality are ultimately the same: that is, quantum states always characterize degrees of freedom which can be changed by a symmetry transformation, so they are relativized for exactly the same reason as partial observables in general relativity. I use the idea that we only measure partial observables to argue that this suggestion is compatible with all existing empirical evidence for quantum mechanics, and then I consider the consequences for ongoing debates about the nature of measurement in quantum mechanics.
authors: Emily Adlam

articles.title: Quantum Temporal Marginal Problem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experiments on a multi-time quantum process may reveal its responses only on selected, possibly overlapping, sets of times. We ask whether these partial descriptions admit a common underlying process, and formulate this process tensor marginal problem as a semidefinite feasibility test. Agreement on overlaps is necessary but insufficient: three locally consistent qubit marginals can have no common extension. Another family is incompatible as a time-ordered process even though a single quantum channel satisfies both its channel and temporal marginal constraints. This isolates temporal causality as the obstruction. We quantify incompatibility by the mixing needed to restore compatibility and derive finite tests using separate interventions at each time and final measurements. We further show that incompatibility is equivalent to an advantage over every compatible family in a multi-time process-discrimination task. Together, these results test whether process descriptions obtained in different experiments can arise from one causally ordered quantum process.
authors: Dingqian Wang, Jiayi Zhao, Ge Bai

articles.title: Qubrio: High-Performance Quantum Compilation via Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
