articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer an adaptable alternative to traditional quantum compilation heuristics, which bottleneck progress by demanding costly manual redesigns whenever hardware evolves. However, naive single-pass LLM approaches fail under the unique challenges introduced by quantum compilation. We introduce Qubrio, a practical agentic framework that significantly reduces heuristic redesigns through a three-level decomposition. By (1) partitioning programs into sequential operation stages, (2) deploying specialized agents for placement, routing and optimization, and (3) using disaggregated feedback for precise error correction, our system reliably navigates complex physical constraints. Beyond serving as a direct compiler, our LLM framework also uncovers novel strategies that facilitate convoy-style shuttling, substantially enhancing hardware concurrency without sacrificing fidelity. We further integrate these strategies into the previous state-of-the-art (SOTA) compiler, recovering a significant fraction of the LLM's performance advantages. On realistic workloads, our compiler achieves significant improvements in hardware runtime and program fidelity over the SOTA baseline PowerMove, seamlessly adapting to new hardware capabilities. Qubrio features an open user interface for practical use, and its code is publicly available at https://github.com/crosaa/Qubrio.
authors: Jixuan Ruan, Zhuo Cui, Zhengding Hu, Zhongkai Yu, Xiang Fang, Yue Guan, Jason Ludmir, Phillip E. Weinberg, Xiuzhe Luo, Shengtao Wang, Sonia Lopez Alarcon, Hezi Zhang, Yufei Ding

articles.title: The Reference System Loophole
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I argue that the Extended Wigner's Friend theorems have a `loophole' that has previously not been appreciated, coming from the fact that we typically need a reference system to give meaning to a measurement outcome. I show how this loophole can be used in the context of the Local Friendliness theorem to preserve the predictions of quantum mechanics without denying Local Friendliness, and I respond to some objections. I explain how the loophole arises naturally from consideration of relevant symmetry transformations, and then I appeal to the partial/complete observables formalism to argue that the same loophole will work for any type of Wigner's Friend experiment, even if it is performed with a variable that does not obviously look like it requires relativization to a reference system. Finally I compare the loophole to other possible responses to the Local Friendliness theorem, and I show that the same loophole will work for other Extended Wigner's Friend theorems too.
authors: Emily Adlam

articles.title: Probing non-adiabaticity in a quantum Otto cycle through quantum texture and imaginarity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-time driving in quantum thermodynamic cycles inevitably generates coherences in the instantaneous energy basis, leading to quantum friction and degrading the operational performance. In this work, we demonstrate that the non-adiabatic inner friction produced during unitary driving of a two-level system can be faithfully quantified by combining two distinct resource-theoretic notions: quantum texture (rugosity) and imaginarity. We show that neither rugosity nor imaginarity alone is sufficient to track the total non-adiabaticity, and we introduce a combined witness, which is strictly non-negative and vanishes if and only if the driving is quasi-static. Applying this framework to a finite-time quantum Otto refrigerator, we establish an exact closed-form relation connecting the coefficient of performance directly to the quantum texture and imaginarity, evaluated at the end of the unitary compression and expansion strokes. Furthermore, we show that local minima of the non-adiabatic witness accurately identify the operating regimes that maximize cooling performance. Our findings provide a geometric and resource-theoretic foundation for inner friction, offering practical diagnostic tools for optimizing finite-time quantum thermal machines.
authors: Jonas F. G. Santos

articles.title: Shallow data-loading circuits for multivariable functions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct shallow QROM, diagonal block-encoding, and quantum state preparation oracles for analytic functions on the D-dimensional hypercube [0, 1]^D. On n qubits and with 2⁻ Ømega ⁽ⁿ/D⁾ error, these circuits have depths of O łeft( sqrtfracn łog₂ (n)D i̊ght) in the Clifford + T gate set, albeit using 2O⁽sqrtⁿD łog₂ ⁽ⁿ⁾⁾ ancilla qubits. This is a near-quadratic depth reduction compared to known linear-depth methods.
authors: Arjun Dixit, Ákos Nagy

articles.title: State Synthesis with an NP oracle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, I describe a quantum algorithm that prepares an arbitrary state |ψångle to inverse exponential precision in polynomial time by making queries to an mathsfNP oracle, assuming one can directly query entries of the state vector corresponding to |ψångle. The previous best upper bound on the complexity class required by an oracle for this task was mathsfPP. I provide evidence that mathsfNP is the best possible upper bound by showing that any quantum algorithm using a mathsfP oracle, or even a mathsfP/poly oracle, requires exponentially many queries. I also discuss some implications of this result for the mathsfQMA search-to-decision problem and unitary synthesis.
authors: Aniruddha Sen

articles.title: Finite attainment and efficient computation of regularized quantum channel relative entropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum channel relative entropy can be nonadditive, making its regularization essential for asymptotic analysis. We study when the regularized value is attained at finite blocklength and how efficiently it can be approximated. For the first question, we establish a sharp dichotomy: the regularized value is either attained already at the single-copy level, implying additivity at every blocklength, or is never attained at any finite blocklength. Notably, a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes between these alternatives for qubit channels and for channel pairs in arbitrary dimensions admitting an interior optimizer. We further show that both the interiority condition and finite nonattainment are generic, holding for almost every channel pair. For the second question, we establish explicit convergence rates for approximating the regularized channel relative entropy. For fixed channel dimensions, widetilde O(ǎrepsilon⁻³/²) channel copies suffice to approximate the regularized value to additive accuracy ǎrepsilon. Alternatively, a semidefinite hierarchy achieves the same accuracy at level widetilde O(ǎrepsilon⁻²), yielding a certified polynomial-time approximation. Together, these results reveal the intriguing structure and generic behavior of regularized channel relative entropy, sharpening our understanding of both its analytical and computational aspects.
authors: Yiwei Xu, Kun Fang

articles.title: Barycentric programming: Classical realization of programs for universal quantum processors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A programmable quantum processor implements a target unitary using information stored in a classical or quantum program register. For arbitrary unitaries in SU(d), quantum programs attain the optimal leading-order memory cost, whereas deterministic classical rounding requires twice as much memory for the same diamond-distance error. We show that this gap disappears when classical randomization is allowed. We introduce barycentric programming, which stores the label of a unitary randomly selected from a finite set, with probabilities chosen so that first-order approximation errors cancel in the averaged unitary channel. Consequently, the diamond-distance error scales quadratically with the discretization spacing. For any ν-parameter family of unitaries forming a compact, smooth manifold without boundary, this method achieves error ǎrepsilon using only (ν/2)łog₂₍₁/ǎrepsilon)+O(1) classical bits. We also prove a matching lower bound for arbitrary quantum programs, determining the optimal leading-order program size for general unitary families. Thus, classical randomization achieves the optimal scaling (ν/2+o(1))łog₂₍₁/ǎrepsilon) without requiring coherent quantum memory.
authors: Yutaka Hashimoto, Satoshi Yoshida, Mio Murao

articles.title: Logarithmic Bias of Zero-Noise Extrapolation under 1/f Noise
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-noise extrapolation estimates ideal quantum observables by amplifying noise and extrapolating the measured response. Its accuracy depends on whether the extrapolation model captures the physical effect of amplification, including correlations between repeated operations. Here we derive the response of complete multiqubit gate folding in the simultaneous presence of time-local Markovian noise and stationary finite-band 1/f noise. An ordered circuit kernel couples the observable to noise memory; exact block counting shows how folding samples correlations at increasing time separations. The resulting response contains an r² ln r coordinate, with a coefficient fixed by the noise spectrum and the integrated forward-inverse control response. Ordinary polynomial Richardson extrapolation leaves a calculable contribution from this coordinate; the three-node rule (1,3,5) retains 2.73 theta. We construct response-matched extrapolation, including a log-domain implementation, that cancels this contribution at the retained order. Explicit bounds separate the remaining control-shape, finite-band, higher-order, and native-offset errors. The theory applies to arbitrary finite multiqubit circuits within the stated control and noise model, and distinguishes removal of memory-induced bias from an unconditional guarantee of the ideal intercept. Single- and ten-qubit numerical examples illustrate the predicted correction and its response dependence.
authors: Chenhui Wang, Weilong Wang, Haoran He, Ping Lv, Zheng Shan

articles.title: Entanglement inference from quantum erasure and path discrimination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fringes recovered by conditioning on quantum-eraser outcomes do not, by themselves, establish entanglement. We determine the minimum entanglement compatible with recorded eraser data when the preparation may be mixed, distinguishing these data from independently determined optimal which-path distinguishabilities and additional joint measurement outcomes. For noisy Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) preparations, explicit compatible states establish sharp entanglement-depth thresholds and show how parity information strengthens certification. A matching converse establishes the exact threshold for two complete Pauli-outcome distributions. For an ideal three-qubit eraser, we classify the additional marker measurement directions that certify genuine multipartite entanglement within a fixed eraser configuration and determine the separate minima of compatible concurrence and squared GHZ fidelity for specified tilted axes. For noisy three-qubit data, an exact semidefinite characterization and constructive converse determine biseparable compatibility at arbitrary fixed local measurement axes, with rational certificates bounding one example. These results establish what entanglement is required by the measurement record, rather than inferred from assumptions about the source.
authors: Mohd Asad Siddiqui

articles.title: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unitary synthesis complexity studies the computational cost of applying a target unitary to an unknown quantum state, extending complexity theory beyond its traditional focus on problems with classical inputs and outputs. Rosenthal and Yuen (ITCS 2022) introduced two complexity classes for unitary synthesis: mathsfunitaryQIP and mathsfunitaryPSPACE for the unitary families implementable via interactive proofs and in polynomial space, respectively. In this work, we prove the equality mathsfunitaryQIP=mathsfunitaryPSPACE and thereby establish a unitary-complexity analogue of mathsfQIP = mathsfPSPACE (Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous, J. ACM 2011) and mathsfstateQIP=mathsfstatePSPACE (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022; Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023). To prove mathsfunitaryQIP subseteq mathsfunitaryPSPACE, we use an acceptance rigidity lemma derived from the soundness condition to show that the polynomial-space prover constructed for a fixed input in state synthesis (Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023) implements the target unitary on every input, leading to a polynomial-space simulation of the protocol. For the reverse inclusion, we build on OpenAI's recently announced solution to the unitary synthesis problem (Aaronson and Kuperberg, Theory Comput. 2007), and show that mathsfunitaryPSPACE families can be synthesized in polynomial time with a mathsfPSPACE oracle. We then implement the oracle queries using auxiliary states prepared via the mathsfstatePSPACE subseteq mathsfstateQIP protocol (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022). Beyond the equality, we show that our protocol for mathsfunitaryPSPACE can be parallelized to constant rounds when the verifier receives polynomially many copies of the input, and we also obtain a complexity-theoretic barrier to proving the existence of mathsfEFI pairs.
authors: Entong He, Fengning Ou, Mingnan Zhao

articles.title: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI scientists are expanding automated research across scientific domains, yet their ability to turn the scientific record into a foundation for autonomous discovery remains elusive. Here we uncover a fundamental barrier to this transition and demonstrate a route to overcome it in computational quantum science, where advances shape both what we can learn from complex quantum systems and what quantum computing can ultimately deliver. To identify this barrier, we introduce OmniQ, an expert-audited virtual research environment that converts published studies into executable reproduction tasks. Across 59 papers spanning classical simulation, quantum algorithms and quantum-property characterization, we systematically evaluate five agentic systems powered by large language models and six third-party agent harnesses. Our findings reveal that current AI scientists often fail to reproduce published results, exposing a fundamental mismatch between what scientific papers communicate and what autonomous agents require. By contrast, human expert intervention can turn these failures into successful reproductions, showing that the missing information can be identified and converted into reusable research experience. Guided by this observation, we develop Residual Agents (RA), a quantum-tailored self-improving AI scientist that distils externally verified workflow repairs into such experience. RA substantially improves research performance under fixed base models and limited adaptation budgets. For example, RA raises DeepSeek V4.1 Flash performance from 68% to 85%, matching Claude Code with Opus 5 at a third of its cost despite using a weaker base model. We integrate all reproduced results into an extensible platform built on the model context protocol, making verified research workflows directly accessible to AI scientists and allowing new scientific papers to be continuously incorporated.
authors: Yuxuan Du, Hanqing Zhao, Xinbiao Wang, Yiming Lu, Kaining Zhang, Dacheng Tao

articles.title: Quantum-Nondemolition Probing of Multiphoton Transitions between Dressed States in a Strongly Driven Jaynes--Cummings System
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The response of the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) model to strong driving has been examined previously, but the origin of intriguing features near emitter--cavity resonance remains poorly understood because of the large background in conventional transmission spectroscopy. Here we introduce a spectroscopic approach for circuit quantum electrodynamics that combines strong cavity driving with quantum-nondemolition qubit readout. Separating the drive and readout substantially enhances the measurement sensitivity as compared with conventional cavity-transmission spectroscopy. With this technique, we identify the near-resonant features as multiphoton transitions between emitter--photon dressed states of the same parity, and resolve transitions between dressed states of opposite parity. Away from resonance, we also observe selective enhancement and suppression of multiphoton transitions, together with transitions involving the second excited state of the anharmonic qubit. Our approach opens a route to resolving the rich transition structure of the JC ladder and probing strongly driven light--matter interactions.
authors: Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Wen-Qi Fu, Zhuo Chen, Wen-Hua Qin, Tao Rong, Bo-Yang An, ZhiAng Qin, Li-Wei Liu, Rami Mrad, Ming Gong, Yingqiu Mao, Yuan Zhang, Johannes Majer

articles.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is exp(Ømega(N)) at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.
authors: Yali Aharon-Holzman, Michael Ilan, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma

articles.title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.
authors: Laia Domingo, Daniil Tarpanov, Arsenii Senokosov, Asel Sagingalieva

articles.title: Needle-beam generation from SPDC photons using inverse-designed flat optics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02993v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the generation of needle-like beams from spontaneous parametric downconversion (SPDC) light using a compact inverse-designed multilevel diffractive lens (MDL). The nonclassical nature of the SPDC source is independently verified through a three-detector heralded Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurement performed before the MDL, yielding a zero-delay second-order correlation value of approximately 0.14. Spatial measurements using an intensified charge-coupled device reveal that the MDL maintains a tightly confined focal distribution over an axial distance of approximately 11 mm under collinear SPDC illumination, substantially reducing diffraction-induced broadening compared with a conventional plano-convex lens of the same nominal focal length. Under non-collinear SPDC illumination, two distinct regions of extended axial confinement are observed, demonstrating the dependence of the engineered focal distribution on the incident spatial field. These results establish a compact flat-optical approach for engineering extended-focus SPDC photon fields, with potential applications in structured quantum photonics.
authors: Sunny, Jyotshna Bora, Ayush Tiwari, C. S. Yadav, Rajesh Menon, Amit D. Lad, Vishwa Pal

articles.title: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directionally generating and controlling quantum states is critical in chiral quantum technologies. Here, we propose a scheme for the nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system, consisting of a superconducting transmon qubit and a yttrium iron garnet sphere subject to a bias magnetic field. The cooperative dissipation between them is induced by coupling both to a common transmission-line waveguide. Due to this cooperative dissipation, the system possesses a dark eigenstate within the single-excitation subspace. Under appropriate parameter conditions, the dark eigenstate reduces to a specific Bell state. With the assistance of a drive pulse, the system can be prepared in this Bell state (i.e., the dark eigenstate). In particular, we find that the dark eigenstate corresponds to different Bell states under positive (+B₀₎ and negative (-B₀₎ bias fields. Consequently, nonreciprocal Bell-state generation is achieved: +B₀ yields one Bell state, while -B₀ yields the other. Moreover, we define a fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate to quantify this nonreciprocity. Our work establishes cooperative dissipation as a versatile resource for nonreciprocal entangled-state generation, opening a promising route toward chiral quantum technologies.
authors: Fei Gao, Xiang-Jing Geng, Wei Feng, Lijiong Shen, Guo-Qiang Zhang

articles.title: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: No consensus has been reached on the appropriate operators for the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons. But there is a tendency to believe the existence of a spin-orbit coupling through the Berry connection. Here we show that this is not the case. Because the positive-energy solution of the Dirac equation is associated with the state of the electron, it is reasonable to postulate that only when projected onto the positive-energy subspace can observable operators on the Hilbert space of the Dirac equation represent physical quantities of the electron. On this basis, we find, after mapping the projected operators onto an irreducible representation, that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point with respect to the laboratory reference frame, relative to which the position of the electron is canonical. The orbital angular momentum of the quantum reference point about the origin of the laboratory reference frame is expressed in terms of the Berry connection. It combines with the canonical orbital angular momentum of the electron about the quantum reference point to give the orbital angular momentum of the electron about the origin of the laboratory reference frame.
authors: Chun-Fang Li

articles.title: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement distillation converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. The distillable entanglement E_D determines the maximum asymptotic rate at which this process can be performed reliably. For several classes of quantum states, distillation above this rate obeys a strong converse: the fidelity with the target state vanishes asymptotically. Here we show that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. Specifically, at any target rate R>E_D, the optimal asymptotic fidelity is given by E_D/R. Thus, although catalysis does not increase the maximum reliable distillation rate, it allows nonvanishing fidelity at every finite rate. Remarkably, this advantage persists even when the catalyst is returned exactly at every finite blocklength and the correlations between the output and catalyst vanish asymptotically. We further characterize the catalyst size required to sustain nonvanishing fidelity above the reliable distillation rate.
authors: Piotr Masajada, Aby Philip, Alexander Streltsov

articles.title: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03220v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum state of a traveling light pulse can qualitatively change the excitation dynamics of a two-level atom. We investigate this dependence for coherent and Fock input states using a virtual-cavity formulation with matched input and output temporal profiles. Analytical treatment of the master equation and numerical simulations show that coherent pulses produce damped Rabi oscillations, whereas Fock pulses can exhibit a partial recovery of the oscillation amplitude in the trailing part of the pulse. We examine how coupling to an auxiliary temporal mode and radiative loss shape this recovery. We also establish a connection with stimulated Raman adiabatic passage through an exact many-photon dark state and derive the associated adiabaticity condition. The observed recovery occurs away from ideal dark-state following. These results distinguish transient recovery in traveling-pulse scattering from conventional cavity collapse and revival, and clarify the scope of an adiabatic-transfer interpretation.
authors: Vasil Z. Vasilev, Benedetto Militello, Anna Napoli, Nikolay V. Vitanov

articles.title: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most quantum circuit platforms focus on idealized circuit assembly and simulation, hiding hardware compilation, error identification, and variational model training behind black-box operations. QYANTRAM addresses this gap through an open platform comprising four subsystems, built around evidence-backed results and independent verification. Its staged compilation pipeline makes every transformation traceable, while the router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores for transparent decision-making. Verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k for k active qubits. This mathematically exact reduction enables full pre-compilation verification on 127- and 156-qubit layouts, achieving approximately 10,000x speed-ups with execution times below one millisecond. The error identification engine exhaustively evaluates all Pauli error patterns without sampling, matching closed-form predictions within 2.8e-17. Its machine-learning engine achieves numerical agreement within 2.0e-15 of qiskit.quantumᵢₙfo while training 25-50 times faster. The router introduces approximately 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE due to its omission of optimization, trading routing efficiency for complete decision transparency and traceability.
authors: Sharyu Kekane, Sadique Khatib, Abhushan Bokade, Uday Wad, S. M. Kamalapur, Y. D. Bhise

articles.title: Stabilizer Learning under Global Depolarizing Noise with Polynomial Copies and 2^t Time
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study learning the stabilizer structure of an unknown pure n-qubit state observed through global depolarizing noise of unknown strength, with a fixed promised upper bound below one, using destructive two-copy Bell measurements. Let 0łe tłe n bound the stabilizer nullity, let ǎrepsilon>0 be the accuracy, and let 0<δ<1 be the failure tolerance. With probability at least 1-δ, a learner must return a commuting unsigned Pauli group containing every stabilizer of the pure state; averaging conjugation by that group must decrease the purity of the observed noisy state by at most ǎrepsilon. Tang and Steckmann gave such a learner with polynomially many copies and 2^t times polynomial time when the noise strength is below a threshold of at most about 0.16, which tends to zero as t/n→1. They asked whether other algorithms with these resources can exceed this threshold. We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed bound on global depolarizing noise below one and every 0łe tłe n, including states with only one promised independent stabilizer. Our learner uses polynomially many copies and 2^t times polynomial classical running time. All resource bounds hold on every execution. Their polynomial factors depend on n,1/ǎrepsilon,łog(1/δ), with degrees and constants depending on the fixed noise promise.
authors: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

articles.title: Efficient thermalization of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians via system-bath interactions with Θ(n) ancilla qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove rapid convergence of a system-bath interaction algorithm for preparing Gibbs states of one-dimensional noncommuting Hamiltonians at every fixed positive temperature. For a chain of n qudits of local dimension 2^q with bounded nearest-neighbor interactions, the algorithm prepares the Gibbs state from any initial state to trace-norm error 0<ǎrepsilonłe1/2 in expected total Hamiltonian evolution time widetildeO(n/ǎrepsilon). This improves the previously proved widetildeO(n⁶/ǎrepsilon) bound for single-ancilla system-bath Gibbs samplers, up to logarithmic factors. The proposed algorithm couples 4^q-1 resettable bath qubits to each site in parallel and randomizes the interaction time. Our analysis bounds both the one-round approximation error and the stationarity defect of an approximate stationary state in Gibbs-weighted L² norms, with only linear dependence on the system size. It also uses the dephasing induced by randomized evolution to control the extensive Lamb shift without treating it as a small perturbation of the dissipative dynamics.
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Bowen Li, Ruizhe Zhang

articles.title: Surface charges and quantum reflection of hydrogen-isotope beams at grazing incidence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experiments with cryogenic beams of hydrogen isotopes (hydrogen (H), deuterium (D), and tritium (T)) can be used to study quantum reflection from solid dielectric mirrors. Most dielectric surfaces carry trapped electric charges whose field polarizes the incident atom. We study theoretically how such charges, distributed randomly, in clusters, with compensation over a finite length, or in order, change specular reflection and diffuse scattering of H, D, and T at grazing incidence on typical dielectric mirrors (SiO₂/Si and MgF₂₎, for longitudinal velocities of 100--300~m/s and normal velocities of 3--100~cm/s which might become available soon in grazing incidence experiments. Starting from the exact coupled-channel equations, we show that the specular wave feels only the laterally averaged polarization potential, which is fixed by the structure factor of the charges and, for uncorrelated charges, is an inverse-square tail -C₂/z². The exact solution replaces the linear threshold law 1-Rrproptop̌erp by the fractional power p̌erp²ν, ν=(1/4-ζ)¹/², with the coupling ζpropto C₂; for weak coupling, this appears as a logarithmic velocity dependence, and for ζ>1/4, the reflection coefficient oscillates log-periodically. At the surface charge density of 10¹² cm⁻², absorption increases by up to 26% for SiO₂/Si and by a factor of two to three for MgF₂; the effect increases with atomic mass, saturates for compensated charges, and is accompanied by diffuse scattering below 10⁻³ of charge-induced loss. We also formulate the condition of complete absorption at the solid surface.
authors: A. Yu. Voronin, V. V. Nesvizhevsky

articles.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical π rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.
authors: Yves Rottstaedt, Andrei I. Pavlovm Alexander Shnirman, Yuval Gefen, Bernd Rosenow

articles.title: Quantum tomography on Schwartz space
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we show that standard results in quantum tomography, which are typically proven in the context of Hilbert spaces, can analogously be established in the theory of Schwartz spaces. In particular, we will see that quantum states are equivalently characterized by their Wigner function, the characteristic of their Wigner function, and the probability distributions for a family of linear combinations of position and momentum. Physically, the latter can be understood as the evolution of its probability distribution in position over time under, for example, free or harmonic evolution. The result is obtained with techniques that are more accessible to a physicist audience, and shows that, at least for tomography results, the full structure of Hilbert spaces is not necessary.
authors: Tobias Thrien, Gabriele Carcassi, David Carfì, Christine A. Aidala

articles.title: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond the binding energy over temperature expansion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the pNRQCD open-quantum-system description of bottomonium in a quark-gluon plasma, writing the full master equation in a spherical basis and establishing a framework for its numerical treatment. The equation does not rely on an expansion in the ratio of the binding energy over the temperature, while retaining the Born, Markov, and dilute approximations. It depends on suitable convolutions of Coulombic Green's functions with real-time chromoelectric correlators, rather than a finite set of transport coefficients. It contains jump-operator contributions that enter with both positive and negative signs, so it is not of a Lindblad type. We utilize optimal operator rotations to minimize the negative sector and define a positive-sector approximation that retains only the optimized positive terms, obtaining in this way a Lindblad equation that can be simulated efficiently with the open-source code QTraj for arbitrary chromoelectric spectral functions. We treat the discarded sector as a systematic uncertainty associated with positivity-breaking effects of the pseudo-Lindblad generator. Positivity breaking effects can be attributed to the approximations made in the derivation of the quarkonium master equation, such as the Born--Markov approximations. Using a spectral model constrained by known infrared and ultraviolet limits, we compute the in-medium width and Bjorken-evolved survival probabilities of the Upsilon(1S,2S,3S). The computations show the convergence of the binding-energy-over-temperature expansion at high temperatures and provide the first large-scale quantum-trajectory simulation results for bottomonium in the low temperature regime. We can thus follow the bottomonium evolution over the full temperature range relevant in heavy-ion collisions.
authors: Nora Brambilla, Arthur Yi-Ting Lin, Tom Magorsch, Antonio Vairo

articles.title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. In cavities supporting multiple wavelengths, a central question is whether degradation at one wavelength compromises performance at another. Understanding this interplay is essential for those cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments that need diverse optical fields for cavity stabilization, trapping, and light--matter coupling. Here, we investigate wavelength-dependent degradation and recovery of a bichromatic cavity with high-reflectivity coating at 455 nm and 671 nm in vacuum. Cavity ring-down measurements reveal a decrease in the 455 nm finesse from 7.7*10³ to 1.9*10³ after 11 hours of continuous exposure to high circulating power. Simultaneous measurements show no measurable degradation at 671 nm. Continuous operation at 671 nm, instead, produces no measurable degradation at either wavelength under the tested conditions. Comparison of oxygen depletion and Avrami-type loss models indicates kinetics compatible with nucleation and growth, without uniquely identifying the microscopic mechanism. We demonstrate partial recovery of the finesse with illumination at 455 nm in air. Our results indicate a wavelength dependence of laser-induced optical damage in bichromatic cavities and provide an estimate of the blue light intensity that can be safely used in such cavities.
authors: M. S. Caracas Nuñez, A. Kadakkavattathu, G. Gatta, L. Duca, N. Mizukami, C. Sias

articles.title: ⁸⁵Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear 5S₁/₂i̊ghtarrow5P₁/₂i̊ghtarrow5D₃/₂i̊ghtarrow 25F₅/₂ three-photon cascade schemes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor. Using the cascade system 5S₁/₂i̊ghtarrow5P₁/₂i̊ghtarrow5D₃/₂i̊ghtarrow 25F₅/₂ in ⁸⁵Rb, we explore two collinear laser-beam configurations. The detunings of the upper two lasers of the cascade system are varied. In both configurations, the probe transmission maps contain rich sets of EIT/EIA features and substructures. To explain these, we utilize a dressed-atom and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. The latter includes 108 relevant fine- and hyperfine-structure levels and their magnetic substates, accounting for coherent optical drives, optical pumping, atom recycling, electromagnetic decays via the 5PJ levels, and velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions. We find quantum-trajectory solutions of the Lindblad master equation, which show good agreement with experimental data and aid in finding physical explanations for the observed spectra. To further explore collision-induced spectral features, collisional loss of EIT/EIA visibility, velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions, we acquire spectra in Rb cells with 50 and 500~mTorr of Ar gas. Our work is of interest to studies of multi-level EIT systems that underpin emerging quantum technologies, where accurate accounting of internal atomic structure, laser beam geometry, optical pumping, transit time, and collisional effects is critical.
authors: Shuaijie Li, Alisher Duspayev, Georg Raithel

articles.title: Validation of the five-electron pO qubit in Si using full configuration interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The pO qubit is a recently proposed charge qubit consisting of five electrons confined in a gate-defined Si quantum dot. Because its two qubit states have no dipole moment, it couples to electric fields only through the quadrupole moment, suppressing the dominant decoherence channel of conventional charge qubits while retaining all-electrical control. The original proposal was formulated in a shell-filling picture without Coulomb interactions. In this work we perform full configuration interaction (FCI) calculations to assess the impact of the Coulomb interaction on the viability of the pO qubit. We find that the interacting eigenstates occupy orbital shells beyond the shell-filling picture, with the degree of excitation governed by the competition between valley splitting, orbital energy, and Coulomb energy scales. Additionally, we find that the ground states form degenerate doublets, but of two distinct kinds. Above a crossover near a valley splitting of Eₘ̊VSapprox50~μeV the doublet is a pair of orbital angular momentum excitations with |łangle L_zångle|=1 in the lower valley, while below the crossover the doublet is a pair of single valley excitations with łangle L_zångle=0. Despite this substantial departure from the shell-filling picture, for Eₘ̊VS > 50~μeV the essential features, vanishing dipole moments and nonzero quadrupole tensor between qubit states are preserved. We show that the vanishing dipole is in fact guaranteed by the symmetry properties of the five-electron Hamiltonian. The same energy scales that govern the orbital occupation also set the quadrupole tensor elements and the first excited state energy gap, both of which are in principle tunable through device engineering.
authors: David W. Kanaar, John H. Caporaletti, J. P. Kestner, Christopher R. Anderson, Mark F. Gyure

articles.title: Polyteam logics for quantum contextuality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce logics of dependence and independence over polyteams (that is, databases with multiple relation schemes), in a similar way as in arXiv:1704.02158v3 [cs.LO]. On this basis, we develop a logical framework in which we can express (in formulas) relevant properties about the statistics of a repeated quantum experiment. In this framework, we formalize Bell's theorem, and the Kochen-Specker theorem as failure of logical entailments, as it was suggested in arXiv:2107.10817v3 [math.LO]. The key feature of polyteam logics in action here is their power to express both local and global properties, with respect to the set of possible measurements. The point of this is at least twofold. Firstly, as in arXiv:1102.0264v7 [quant-ph], it gives a high-level (information-theoretic) understanding of these physical phenomena, that is not intrinsic to the physical objects involved. Secondly, since logical entailment is often (partially) axiomatizable, this framework incites us to tackle the question of contextuality computationally. We also define semiring-weighted polyteams along with logics on them, and use them to recover the probabilistic versions of the contextuality theorems mentioned above.
authors: Loan Le Maguet

articles.title: Benchmark Study for Quantum Statevector Simulators for Scientific Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum circuit simulators are essential for quantum algorithm development, yet systematic runtime benchmarks comparing major frameworks across CPU and GPU backends are limited. We benchmark three open-source frameworks - Cirq (qsim), CUDA-Q, and Qiskit (Aer) - on statevector simulation of the 2D quantum acoustic wave equation, evolved via Trotterized Hamiltonian dynamics, for problem sizes from 7 to 29 qubits on a single Azure virtual machine. The evaluation spans four categories: CPU runtime versus qubit count, strong scalability on multi-core CPUs at 27 qubits, GPU runtime versus qubit count, and GPU-over-CPU speedup. Relative rankings shift from one category to the next. On CPU, Cirq is fastest up to 23 qubits (2.4x faster than Qiskit at 21 qubits), but Qiskit overtakes it at larger sizes and higher thread counts, sustaining 80% parallel efficiency at 16 threads. On GPU, CUDA-Q leads between 13 and 21 qubits, while Cirq becomes the fastest GPU backend at large problem sizes, achieving 1.5x and 2.3x speedups over CUDA-Q and Qiskit at 29 qubits. GPU-over-CPU speedup ratios should be interpreted alongside absolute GPU runtimes; CUDA-Q's 1500x at 21 qubits is largely driven by the limited scaling of its CPU backend (qpp), and the absolute GPU runtimes show that the three frameworks' GPU backends differ by less than these ratios alone suggest. These results indicate that no single framework dominates across configurations, and that backend selection for statevector simulation should be guided by both target hardware and problem size.
authors: Timothy M. Yeo, Rodney W. Lessard

articles.title: Density functionals for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a density-functional theory for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian of nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the spirit of the convex-analytic formulation of Lieb. We consider finitely many electrons, subject to external scalar and vector potentials, coupled to the full continuum of massless transverse photons with an ultraviolet cutoff. The natural basic variables are the standard electron density and a combined current density, the sum of the paramagnetic current density and a field-induced current density generated by the quantized vector potential. We prove representability results for these density-current pairs and show that the mixed-state constrained-search functional attains its infimum and coincides with the Lieb functional obtained by convex conjugation. Since arbitrarily soft photons purify mixed states at a negligible energy cost without changing their density and combined current density, the pure-state Levy-Lieb functional equals the Lieb functional and is therefore convex, even though its infimum need not be attained. In addition, we establish the zero-coupling limit, which recovers the mixed-state Vignale-Rasolt functional of current-density-functional theory. Finally, we consider the long-wavelength (dipole) limit and show that the limiting functional can be written as a constrained search for the well-known length-gauge dipole Hamiltonian.
authors: Mihály A. Csirik, Andre Laestadius, Markus Penz, Erik I. Tellgren

articles.title: Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator L_ϵ=D[a²⁻α²]+ϵ D[a], describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large α and sufficiently small ϵ>0, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with α², uniformly in ϵ. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.
authors: Ruikang Liang, Rémi Robin

articles.title: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid moiré excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. With the strong dipole-dipole interaction, they also realize Bose-Hubbard quantum simulators of emergent correlated matter such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC). Here we reveal the characteristic cooperative radiation from condensates of hybrid moiré excitons in twisted MoTe₂ bilayers. In each individual moiré trap, the layer hybridization selection rule dictates that the ground-state exciton is a quantum emitter of orbital-angular-momentum photons, with an exceptionally long radiative lifetime. Ground-state emission becomes pronounced only upon forming condensates, where inter-sublattice dipole attraction and intra-sublattice repulsion together lead to the coexistence of exciton and biexciton BEC with comparable weights. The biexciton (molecular-type) BEC decays through superradiance of path-entangled biphotons, whereas the exciton (atomic-type) BEC is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent. Our findings not only uncover a novel source of entangled light but also establish unique fingerprints for exploring the cold chemistry of atomic-molecular condensates with moiré excitons.
authors: Haochen Wang, Shengxian Li, Hongyu Lu, Mingxing Chen, Wang Yao

articles.title: Experimental demonstration of phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km with injection locking assisted phase stabilization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recovering complex optical signals with high sensitivity is central to coherent communication and sensing. Beyond conventional homodyne and heterodyne reception, phase-conjugate twin-wave encoding and phase-sensitive joint detection offer an alternative strategy with enhanced sensitivity. Extending this approach to long-distance transmission of high-order-modulated signals is challenging because optical phase coherence must be maintained at the receiver. Here we experimentally demonstrate injection-locking-assisted phase-conjugated twin-wave reception of 200-MBaud signals with modulation formats up to 256-QAM over 100 km of optical fiber. Optical injection locking regenerates the local oscillator (LO) from a reference transmitted through the 16 dB-loss link, while pilot-assisted optical feedback stabilizes the relative signal-LO phase, enabling coherent combining of the phase-conjugated twin waves at a single balanced photodetector. At equal received signal-photon number per quadrature in each data-carrying optical mode, the measured PCTW signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exceeds the ideal single-mode homodyne standard quantum limit (SQL) benchmark. The SNR gains over the measured homodyne and conventional heterodyne results are about 3 dB and 6 dB, respectively. Constellation and bit-error-rate measurements show that this gain improves high-order data recovery relative to heterodyne reception. An ideal Gaussian-noise model predicts a photon information efficiency of 1.54 bits per received signal photon for uniform 16-QAM. These results establish an injection-locking-assisted coherent receiver architecture that implements joint detection of phase-conjugated twin waves over 100 km of fiber with enhanced sensitivity, providing a practical route for photon-efficient coherent communication.
authors: Zhenlin Zhao, Xingwen Yi, Dawei Wang

articles.title: MBUndo: Sound, Automatic, and Efficient Measurement-Based Uncomputation for Quantum Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum programs that use temporary values, known as emphancilla qubits, must explicitly emphuncompute each ancilla back to zero to ensure that the program produces correct outputs. Conventional uncomputation uses unitary quantum gates, whereas leading quantum algorithms now leverage emphmeasurement-based uncomputation (MBU), which replaces costly unitary T gates with cheaper measurements and phase corrections. Current quantum programming frameworks can use measurement to uncompute specific gates such as Toffoli. No automatic transformation, however, accepts an arbitrary circuit whose ancillas are computed and uncomputed via the standard approach and converts the circuit to use MBU@. Researchers instead apply MBU to individual circuit designs by hand, which limits algorithm development and compiler optimization. Such a transformation has not existed due to two fundamental unknowns: where MBU applies and which gates realize MBU for an arbitrary computation. To solve these, we first present a static analysis that identifies, for each ancilla qubit, each circuit position where measurement is sound --- subsuming basic assumptions that MBU only applies at the end of a circuit. Next, we present circuit transformations that soundly turn unitary uncomputation gates into efficient phase corrections after measurement --- generalizing rewrite rules from prior literature that are either limited to a single gate or not applicable to a general circuit. We present textsfMBUndo, an integrated compiler pass that automatically converts circuits to measurement-based uncomputation. It requires no user annotations other than which qubits are ancillas, the same as needed by existing uncomputation synthesizers, and can enhance their output circuits. We evaluate textsfMBUndo on 22 benchmarks to reveal emphT gate reductions of >36.5% over uncomputation synthesizers.
authors: Shengyuan Yang, Charles Yuan

articles.title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries. The twist is the temporal analogue of Laughlin's flux insertion in the quantum Hall effect. For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator. For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist. We derive this relation for matrix product unitaries and test it numerically in random unitary circuits. Applied to the matrix product operators of non-invertible symmetries, the same twisted rank returns the quantum dimension of the symmetry operator in addition to its flow index.
authors: Ryota Nakai, Taozhi Guo, Shinsei Ryu

articles.title: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02798v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We measure current across a voltage-biased, long array of Josephson junctions. Current-voltage characteristics do not reveal any critical current and instead display the presence of threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with the Coulomb blockade. However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, E_Jgg E_C, where E_C is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter E_J/E_C) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-e solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.
authors: Bayan Karimi, Ze-Yan Chen, Jukka P. Pekola, T. Yamamoto, M. Houzet, L. I. Glazman

articles.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of frac3N. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of G=3K₂, which is equal to 4/6. G=3K₂ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to 4/6 and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.
authors: Mohamed Nomeir, Sennur Ulukus

articles.title: Amortized Stabilizer Rényi Entropy of Quantum Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2409.06659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magic states are essential resources for fault-tolerant quantum computation. We introduce the amortized stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), which quantifies the largest SRE increase generated by a unitary, including arbitrary pure inputs and reference systems. Initial nonstabilizerness can enhance this increase, whereas analogous amortized logarithmic robustness and extent collapse to stabilizer-input optimizations. We establish structural properties and exact amortized 2-SRE values for the T and CCZ gates. We then derive explicit lower bounds on approximate T-state cost, with diamond-distance error, allowing stabilizer ancillary states, Pauli measurements, and classical feedforward. A Choi-state witness gives computable bounds for quantum Fourier transforms, controlled rotations, fractional controlled-SWAP gates, and finite Heisenberg-chain evolutions. We distinguish the unrestricted optimization from its Choi witness and specify the access and precision requirements for estimating Pauli moments. An odd-moment variant yields a confidence-qualified cost witness from ordinary copies.
authors: Chengkai Zhu, Yu-Ao Chen, Zhiping Liu, Zhan Yu, Zanqiu Shen, Xin Wang

articles.title: Quantum Feature Space of a Qubit Coupled to a Classical Stochastic Environment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2505.03397v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Qubit control protocols traditionally characterise qubit-environment coupling using resource-intensive pulse sweeps on quantum hardware. Although previous work attempted to reduce this quantum runtime by inferring noise operators, it relied on a complex grey-box approach combining deep neural networks with physics-encoded layers, posing challenges in training and scaling. Here, we introduce a quantum feature space (QFS, denoted F) constructed from a single pulse sequence. By engineering F to encode qubit-environment dynamics, we eliminate the need for expensive neural networks to learn these physical interactions. This allows us to offload extraction of spectral features to efficient classical machine learning algorithms. Bypassing both the extensive pulse sweeps of traditional quantum noise spectroscopy and the costly neural networks of prior methods, we demonstrate that a simple random forest algorithm on F classifies broad noise classes with sim 90% accuracy under simulated realistic hardware constraints, including pulse jitter and readout errors. Furthermore, Euclidean distance searches over F can determine spectral resonances. Focusing on noise classification and identification rather than continuous power spectral density reconstruction makes F an efficient diagnostic tool for quantum hardware.
authors: Chris Wise, Akram Youssry, Alberto Peruzzo, Jo Plested, Matt Woolley

articles.title: Chirally frustrated superradiant phases in a Jaynes-Cummings trimer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.13800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the emergence of frustrated quantum phases in a Jaynes-Cummings (JC) trimer with complex hopping amplitudes between the cavities, which represents the smallest frustrated unit in light-matter systems. The complex hopping amplitudes that can be engineered via synthetic gauge fields introduce chiral effects and geometric frustration to the system. We obtain analytic solutions in the semiclassical limit and map out the phase diagram of this model, featuring one normal and three distinct superradiant phases. Among these phases, a chirally frustrated superradiant phase emerges, characterized by broken chiral and translational symmetries and unidirectional photon flow. These results reveal how frustration and symmetry breaking can arise in JC systems with synthetic gauge fields and strong light-matter coupling.
authors: Lin-Lin Jiang, Ya-Ping Ni, Xuan Xie, Lin Tian, Jin-Feng Huang

articles.title: Work extraction from long-lived quantum coherence of a three-level system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.02614v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze work-extraction protocols using the long-lived quantum coherence of a three-level quantum system coupled to a thermal bath. We identify conditions under which persistent quantum coherence can arise, i.e., for systems with degenerate excited states and aligned transition dipoles, or for nearly degenerate systems with small energy splittings. By proposing two thermodynamic protocols that employ energy-preserving unitary operations, we show that quantum coherence can be converted into population asymmetry, thereby serving as a quantum resource for work extraction. Specifically, we propose an optimized protocol to extract the maximum extractable work (MEW), measured by the free energy difference (FED), from quantum coherence in a single-shot thermodynamic cycle. Our results highlight the thermodynamic advantages of long-lived coherence in a three-level quantum system and could influence future designs of coherence-driven quantum thermal machines.
authors: Wenjing Chen, Si-Wei Han, Ziye Wang, Xiaoshan Feng, Jun Feng

articles.title: Low Overhead Universal Quantum Computation with Triorthogonal Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.05708v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the use of triorthogonal codes for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation and propose two methods to circumvent the Eastin-Knill theorem, which prohibits any single quantum error-correcting code from supporting both universality and a transversal gate set. We show that our methods reduce the resource overhead compared with existing fault-tolerant protocols. We develop a simple fault-tolerant implementation of the logical Hadamard gate for triorthogonal codes by exploiting the fact that they have transversal controlled-Z (CZ) gates, resulting in a circuit with reduced overhead. We also introduce a procedure for generating a symmetric Calderbank-Shor-Steane code paired with a triorthogonal code, which allows CNOT and CZ gate transversality across the pair of codes. In addition, we present logical state teleportation circuits that transfer encoded states between the two codes, allowing all logical operations to be performed transversally. Our methods can be integrated into the Steane error correction framework without incurring additional resource cost. Finally, using the 15-qubit code as an example, we demonstrate that our protocols significantly reduce the gate overhead compared with other existing methods. These results highlight the potential of combining distinct code structures to achieve low-overhead, universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.
authors: Dawei Jiao, Mahdi Bayanifar, Alexei Ashikhmin, Olav Tirkkonen

articles.title: Sequential realization of Quantum Instruments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.14588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In adaptive quantum circuits classical results of mid-circuit measurements determine the upcoming gates. This allows POVMs, quantum channels or more generally quantum instruments to be implemented sequentially, so that fewer qubits need to be used at each of the N measurement steps. In this paper, we mathematically describe these problems via adaptive sequence of instruments (ASI) and show how any instrument can be decomposed into it. Number of steps N and number of ancillary qubits n_A needed for actual implementation are crucial parameters of any such ASI. We show an achievable lower bound on the product N.n_A and we determine in which situations this tradeoff is likely to be optimal. Contrary to common intuition we show that for quantum instruments which transform n to m(>n) qubits, there exist N-step ASI implementing them just with (m-n) ancillary qubits, which are remeasured (N-1) times and finally used as output qubits.
authors: Soham Sau, Michal Sedlák

articles.title: Magnetic levitation and spatial superposition of a nanodiamond with a current-carrying chip
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.06608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a current-carrying-chip scheme for generating spatial quantum superpositions using a levitating nanodiamond with a built-in nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre defect. Our setup is versatile, for a mass range of 10⁻¹⁹~m̊ kgłeq młeq 10⁻¹⁷~m̊ kg a superposition size of range a̧l O(100)m̊ nm < Δ x < a̧l O(10) m̊ μ m is achievable in tłeq 0.1s, depending on the position we launch from the centre of the diamagnetic trap. Using numerical simulations, we provide an in-depth analysis of the chip that can support stable trapping of the particle in all three dimensions as well as create a spatial superposition along the x-axis, while producing a very tight trap in the transverse directions. This setup enables the creation of a Schrödinger cat state with a diamagnetically levitated nanoparticle in a table-top experiment. Although the mass and superposition size considered here remain below those required for a QGEM test, the proposed device provides a building block toward future QGEM experiments.
authors: Qian Xiang, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Andrew Geraci, Sougato Bose, Anupam Mazumdar

articles.title: A Stochastic Reconstruction of Entangled States: from Quantum Foundations to Machine Learning and Decision Making
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.17070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article presents a concrete mathematical framework for the generation of entangled quantum states from classical stochastic processes. We demonstrate that any density operator h̊oAB of a composite system can be derived from the correlations between two underlying stochastic processes, X(t) and Y(t), representing the random fluctuations of its subsystems. This construction utilizes a two-scale temporal scheme - micro and macro time - where quantum correlations emerge as macro-correlations derived from underlying micro-correlations. We propose the Double Covariance Model (DCM), which reproduces the some properties of quantum theory by treating quantum states as the fourth-order moment structure of an underlying classical probability space. DCM may also have potential implications for applications, particularly in quantum-inspired simulation and technology, and quantum-like modeling of cognition and decision making, as a tool for generation of density matrices with classical stochastic processes.
authors: Andrei Khrennikov, Irina Basieva

articles.title: High-fidelity non-adiabatic dark state gates for neutral atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.13885v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rydberg blockade gates are the most experimentally mature entangling operations in neutral-atom quantum processors, combining fast gate times with simple control, but their performance degrades at larger interatomic separations and remains sensitive to motional and technical noise. Non-blockade gate schemes, such as dark state and geometric protocols, offer complementary robustness but typically rely on complex and experimentally demanding control. Here we show that quantum optimal control enables non-blockade gate schemes to be implemented using the experimentally established pulse-shaping techniques developed for blockade-based gates. Focusing on the dark state gate, we construct non-adiabatic implementations that preserve the intrinsic robustness of adiabatic dark state protocols while achieving gate times comparable to time-optimal blockade gates using only smooth, experimentally feasible pulses. The resulting gates exhibit enhanced resilience to motional coupling, laser noise, and interaction inhomogeneity, particularly near and beyond the blockade radius. This work establishes a practical route to fast, robust non-blockade-based two-qubit gates without increased experimental complexity.
authors: Nader Mostaan, Kapil Goswami, Peter Schmelcher, Rick Mukherjee

articles.title: Quantum algorithm for solving high-dimensional linear stochastic differential equations via amplitude encoding of the noise term
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.24133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work studies quantum algorithms to solve high-dimensional stochastic differential equations (SDEs) d Xₜ = A(t) Xₜ d t + B(t) d Wₜ. Aiming for a speed-up in the dimension N of Xₜ, we generate quantum states that encode Xₜ in the amplitudes, while most of the existing quantum methods for SDEs employ binary encoding. A key challenge is the amplitude encoding of the noise term, and we address this by utilizing the quantum circuit implementation of a pseudorandom number generator (PRNG). We propose two methods: the Dyson series-based method and the Euler-Maruyama (EM)-based method. In the former, we express the noise term via the Dyson series approximation of the time evolution operator, while in the latter, it is approximated using the EM time discretization. Both methods use the quantum linear systems solver to generate the amplitude-encoding state of Xₜ, making only m̊ polylog(N) queries to the PRNG circuit and the block-encodings of A and B. Additionally, going beyond state preparation, we present methods to estimate expectations of functions of Xₜ using the state.
authors: Koichi Miyamoto

articles.title: Quantum Proper Scoring Rules: Convex Duality, Bregman Risk, and the Coherence Gap
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.05268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We generalize proper scoring rules to the quantum domain, replacing probability distributions with density operators. We define Quantum Value Functionals via convex generators and establish a duality theory yielding proper quantum scoring rules using McCarthy's tangent-plane construction. We derive local minimax optimal bounds for quantum state tomography under these incentives, proving a Local Holevo-McCarthy Bound that explicitly links asymptotic risk to the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori metric and the Holevo bound. Furthermore, we establish an exact coherence floor that quantifies the irreducible excess score of fixed-basis forecasting strategies when phases are unknown (minimax over the phase orbit), proving a worst-case minimax floor of łog d over the full state space. Our results contextualize fundamental sample complexity separations compared to optimal quantum estimation strategies and guide the design of incentive-compatible quantum data markets and robust quantum machine learning protocols.
authors: M. W. AlMasri

articles.title: How to make quantum cheese: efficient geometry oracles for exponentially many pseudorandom microstructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.00222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum algorithms for partial differential equations often assume oracle access to the geometry of the material being simulated. As explicitly specifying a geometry pixel by pixel on an exponentially large grid automatically yields an exponential cost, a central question is when such oracles can effectively be implemented by polynomially sized quantum circuits. We give explicit polynomial-size circuits for a family of geometries with exponentially many pseudorandom microscopic features. The geometry is generated by a pseudorandom procedure and a convolution with a local kernel to shape the texture. This proves to be a versatile framework, that includes materials with fixed-shape holes, spatially correlated textures, and activation--inhibition patterns. For a fixed kernel with bounded integer coefficients, the oracle cost is polynomial in the number of qubits, even when the number of microfeatures is exponential. We implement the circuit constructions in PsiQuantum Construct and verify their behaviour through numerical simulation. We also discuss why efficient access does not follow from an arbitrary description of the material, by proving worst-case query lower bounds for amplitude-encoded formation fields and databases of holes.
authors: Alice Barthe

articles.title: The use of Peres lattices in periodically driven systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.20009v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate the strength of the method of Peres lattices in periodically driven quantum systems. The method, which has previously been used mostly in stationary systems, enables us to efficiently detect resonances in the driven system, to monitor the onset of chaos, and to recognize critical properties of the Floquet modes. It also allows quick comparisons of the spectra of Floquet modes for various driving Hamiltonians and transparent tests of the iterative approximation techniques based on effective stationary Hamiltonians.
authors: Lukáš Honsa, Jan Střeleček, Jakub Novotný, Pavel Cejnar

articles.title: The Halperin (111) state as a paired composite-fermion wave function: Two exact finite-size identities on the sphere
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two wavefunctions have previously been proposed to describe the ν=1/2+1/2 quantum Hall bilayer: p-wave pairing of composite fermions and s-wave pairing of composite fermions with anti-composite fermions. We show analytically in the spherical geometry and within the Jain-Kamilla lowest Landau level projection scheme that both of these paired composite fermion wavefunctions exactly reproduce the Halperin (111) state for a specific form of the pairing that we derive. We also find a second wavefunction that is common between both classes of wavefunctions. However, we provide evidence the two variational families generate overlapping but not identical sets of electronic states, ruling out a universal reparametrization that identifies their wavefunctions.
authors: Glenn Wagner

articles.title: Quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions in atomic-defect landscapes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~μeV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.
authors: Samir Lounis

articles.title: Quantum Dipolar Magnon Drag in Conducting Magnetic Bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We predict electrical drag between two electrically isolated metallic ferromagnets mediated by quantum dipolar magnon coupling. A charge current in one layer generates a nonequilibrium magnon current whose momentum is transferred across an insulating spacer through interlayer dipolar interactions. The resulting magnon current in the passive layer produces a measurable voltage through electron-magnon scattering. We show the combination of resonant quantum momentum transfer and magnetic tunability through the control of magnetization configurations distinguish quantum dipolar drag from conventional drag mechanism.
authors: Ling Gan, Shufeng Zhang

articles.title: Effect of Rapid Thermal Annealing on the Superconductivity of ALD-Grown TiN thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing.
