articles.title: A quantum oscillator interacting with a classical oscillator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2403.07479v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a quantum oscillator interacting with, and back-reacting on, a classical oscillator. This can be done consistently provided the quantum system decoheres, while the backreaction has a stochastic component which causes the classical system to undergo diffusion. Nonetheless, the state of the quantum oscillator can remain pure conditioned on the trajectory of the classical oscillator. We solve the system using the classical-quantum path integral formulation, and compute the free and bridge correlators of the theory, which we use to find the heating rate. In addition, we explicitly compute the conditioned, and unconditional purity of the system. This serves as a toy model for a number of other systems in which one subsystem can be treated as effectively classical, such as a scalar quantum field interacting with another field undergoing decoherence, or a system emitting radiation, one of which is treated classically.
authors: Muhammad Sajjad, Andrea Russo, Maite Arcos, Andrzej Grudka, Jonathan Oppenheim

articles.title: Classical simulation of universal measurement-based quantum computation using multipartite Bell scenarios
articles.abstract: arXiv:2410.23734v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a novel classical simulation algorithm based on non-signaling polytopes of multipartite Bell scenarios, capable of simulating universal measurement-based quantum computation with single-qubit Pauli measurements. In our model, the simultaneous presence of non-stabilizer states and entanglement is necessary for quantum speedup. The region of quantum states that can be efficiently simulated includes the Bell polytope and extends beyond the reach of current sampling algorithms based on phase-space methods.
authors: Cihan Okay, Atak Talay Yucel, Selman Ipek

articles.title: A Linearly Convergent Algorithm for Petz-Augustin Means with Applications to Computing Petz-Augustin Capacity and Equilibrium Prices in Fisher Markets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2502.06399v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the computation of the Petz-Augustin mean of order α in (0,1) u̧p (1,infty), defined as the minimizer of a weighted sum of n Petz-Rényi divergences of order α over the set of d-by-d quantum states, where the Petz-Rényi divergence is a quantum generalization of the classical Rényi divergence. We propose the first algorithm with a non-asymptotic convergence guarantee for solving this optimization problem. The iterates are guaranteed to converge to the Petz-Augustin mean at a linear rate of Ołeft( łvert 1 - 1/α v̊ert^T i̊ght) with respect to the Thompson metric for αin(1/2,1)u̧p(1,infty), where T denotes the number of iterations. The algorithm has an initialization time complexity of Ołeft(nd³ⁱ̊ght) and a per-iteration time complexity of Ołeft(nd² + d³ⁱ̊ght). Two applications follow. The first application concerns the Petz-Augustin capacity of order αin(1/2,1), which generalizes the quantum channel capacity and characterizes the optimal error exponent in classical-quantum channel coding. To compute this quantity, we propose the first iterative method with a non-asymptotic convergence guarantee, which uses our algorithm for computing the Petz-Augustin mean as a subroutine. The second application concerns the equilibrium prices in Fisher markets with constant elasticity of substitution (CES) utilities. We establish that when all buyers have CES utilities of common elasticity, the equilibrium prices are equivalent to the Petz-Augustin mean when all quantum states commute. In this case, our proposed algorithm is a tâtonnement process à la Walras. We further extend the algorithm to inhomogeneous Fisher markets, where buyers have CES utilities with different elasticities, and prove a faster convergence rate than existing tâtonnement-type algorithms.
authors: Chun-Neng Chu, Wei-Fu Tseng, Yen-Huan Li

articles.title: Multiband dispersion and warped vortices of strongly-interacting photons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2502.11553v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a theoretical study of quantum correlations between interacting photons realized through co-propagating Rydberg polaritons. We show that the spatial evolution of the n-photon wavefunction is governed by a multiband dispersion featuring one massive mode and multiple massless modes with degenerate Dirac points and n-fold rotational symmetry. The resulting band structure is warped, departing from the single-band, parabolic approximation commonly assumed for interacting polaritons. Our analytical results are supported by rigorous numerical modeling that fully accounts for photon propagation inside the finite atomic medium. These findings advance the understanding of multi-photon interactions and support the development of future multi-photon control tools.
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, Ofer Firstenberg

articles.title: Qudit-based scalable quantum algorithm for solving the integer programming problem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.13906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integer programming (IP) is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem that is widely used to represent a diverse set of real-world problems spanning multiple fields, such as finance, engineering, logistics, and operations research. It is a hard problem to solve using classical algorithms, as its complexity increases with problem size. Most quantum algorithms for solving IP are highly resource-inefficient because they encode integers into qubits. In [1], the issue of resource inefficiency was addressed by mapping integer variables to qudits. However, [1] has limited practical value due to a lack of scalability to multiple qudits to encode larger problems. In this work, by extending upon the ideas of [1], a circuit-based scalable quantum algorithm is presented using multiple interacting qudits for which we show a quantum speed-up for solving the integer programming problem. The quantum algorithm consists of a distillation function that efficiently separates the feasible from the infeasible regions, a phase-amplitude encoding for the cost function, and a quantum phase estimation coupled with a multi-controlled single-qubit rotation for optimization. We prove that our algorithm yields the optimal solution with the maximum measurement probability. The time complexity for the quantum algorithm is shown to be O(r_P(mn²log d + dⁿ/²/Ny_ₛ¹/² + n ϵQPE⁻¹)) for a problem with the number of variables n taking d integer values, satisfying m constraints with a precision of ϵQPE and r_P repetitions required for reaching a success probability P. Compared to the classical time complexity of brute force O(dⁿ⁾ and the classical exact algorithm O((łogn)O⁽ⁿ⁾), it incurs a reduction of sim dⁿ/² in the time complexity (for a polynomial number of repetitions and precision requirements) for solving a general polynomial IP problem.
authors: Kapil Goswami, Peter Schmelcher, Rick Mukherjee

articles.title: Comparing Quantum Annealing and BF-DCQO
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.14358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work [1] has claimed that a gate-model quantum-classical hybrid algorithm called bias-field digitized counterdiabatic quantum optimization (BF-DCQO) [2] outperforms D-Wave's annealing quantum computers in optimization tasks. We find the opposite to be true, and demonstrate that D-Wave's quantum annealers find solutions of far greater quality than claimed in Ref. [1], while using far less computation time. We also present evidence that suggests the quantum component of the hybrid approach makes minimal contributions to solution quality.
authors: Pau Farré, Erika Ordog, Kevin Chern, Catherine C. McGeoch

articles.title: Incoherent Imaging with Spatially Structured Quantum Probes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.09521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Incoherent imaging, including fluorescence and absorption microscopy, is often limited by weak signals and resolution constraints -- notoriously, Rayleigh's curse. We investigate how spatially structured quantum probes, combined with quantum detection strategies like spatial mode demultiplexing and photon counting, overcome these limitations. We propose a novel imaging protocol based on twin-beam echoes that maps the generalized incoherent-imaging model -- comprising both absorption and fluorescence -- onto distinct passive imaging channels that separately encode the absorption and fluorescence signatures. This enables (i) simultaneous absorption and fluorescence imaging and (ii) direct application of well-known results from passive imaging, all featuring quantum-enhanced measurement sensitivity. Remarkably, the same protocol supports displacement-field reconstruction of multiple quadratures (e.g., oscillators' positions) and works for both conventional and subdiffraction imaging, thereby functioning as a universal quantum imaging module. We also examine the utility of Fock states in a structured spatial mode basis, which offer comparable performance in principle. Though developed for optical imaging, our framework applies broadly to quantum-optical microscopy, phononic or acoustic imaging, and mapping stochastic forces, fields, or charge distributions using an array of mechanical oscillators.
authors: Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Saikat Guha

articles.title: Symmetry-Adapted Eigensolver from Real-Space Sampling of Tensor-Network-Bridged Quantum Circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.19219v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a symmetry-adapted eigensolver for strongly correlated systems that separates where the wave function is emphsampled from where it is emphdefined. The lattice is divided into equal blocks: parallel quantum circuits absorb the entanglement within each block, while a matrix product state (MPS) backbone bridges the blocks and restores global correlations. The resulting real-space amplitude φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ) acts only as a sample generator---configurations are drawn from |φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ)|² directly, block by block, without any Markov chain. The variational state itself is defined in a symmetry-adapted basis by two separate rules: the modulus of ψ(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ) is the square root of the total weight accumulated over the entire equivalence class, widetildep(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ)=sumₐₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗᵢₙg ₐₘ̊ ᵣₑₚᵣ|φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ)|², whereas its phase is inherited from the single representative amplitude φ(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₚᵣ). The modulus rule is what makes the scheme both exact and cheap: the distributionwidetildep(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ) sampled in the symmetric basis is exactly the one induced by the mapping from the real-space distribution p(aₘ̊ ᵣₑₐₗ), so every generated configuration is an unbiased sample of |ψ(aₘ̊ ₛyₘₘ)|²; the phase rule then fixes the only freedom that remains. Because amplitudes within a class are combined in probability rather than summed with symmetry characters, ψ is emphnot a group projection of the circuit-MPS state; the class-wide aggregation instead supplies long-range, symmetry-enforced entanglement that the MPS never has to carry itself.
authors: Lei Xu, Ling Wang

articles.title: The relativistic reason for quantum probability amplitudes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.10497v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the quantum-mechanical probability distribution involving complex probability amplitudes can be derived from three natural conditions imposed on a relativistically invariant probability function describing the motion of a particle that can take multiple paths simultaneously. The conditions are: (i) pairwise Kolmogorov additivity, (ii) time symmetry, and (iii) Bayes' rule. The resulting solution, parameterized by a single constant, is the squared modulus of a sum of complex exponentials of the relativistic action, thereby recovering the Feynman path-integral formulation of quantum mechanics.
authors: Karol Sajnok, Kacper Dkebski, Andrzej Dragan

articles.title: Madelung hydrodynamics of spin-orbit coupling: action principles, currents, and correlations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.10698v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We exploit the variational and Hamiltonian structures of quantum hydrodynamics with spin to unfold the correlation and torque mechanisms accompanying spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in electronic motion. Using Hamilton's action principle for the Pauli equation, we isolate SOC-induced quantum forces that act on the orbital Madelung--Bohm trajectories and complement the usual force terms known to appear in quantum hydrodynamics with spin. While the latter spin-hydrodynamic forces relate to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), SOC-induced orbital forces originate from a particular current operator that contributes prominently to the spin current. This distinction between force terms reveals two fundamentally different mechanisms generating quantum spin-orbit correlations. Leveraging the Hamiltonian structure of the hydrodynamic system, we also elucidate spin transport features such as the correlation-induced quantum torques and the current shift in the spin Hall effect. This Hall shift leads to a new definition of the transport spin current thereby addressing an open question in spintronics. Finally, we illustrate the framework via the Madelung--Rashba equations for planar SOC configurations and propose a particle-based scheme for numerical implementation.
authors: Cesare Tronci

articles.title: Type-I and Type-II Fusion Protocols for Weighted Graph States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.13381v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weighted graph states extend standard graph states by associating phases with entangling edges, and may serve as resources for measurement-based quantum computation. We analyze how the two main fusion operations, Type-I and type-II, act on weighted graph states. Type-I fusion operates identically to the unweighted case, merging two one-dimensional weighted graphs, while preserving edge weights and success probabilities. In addition, the pool of two-qubit weighted graph states can be generated easily from Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states or Bell pairs. In contrast, type-II fusion requires a logical qubit, which can be formed only for specific weight configurations, and with a success probability below one-half. When successful, it fuses the states correctly, but its failure outcomes destroy the structure of the graphs, removing the good-failure feature known from ordinary graph states. These two obstacles can be overcome by using extra qubits and π weights in the one-dimensional weighted graph states that are being fused, which enables scalability. We compute the change in the entanglement entropy of the resulting link due to the fused states being weighted graph states (for generalized fusion), and classify the resulting states of a general non-Bell projection. These results define the practical limits of the fusion-based construction of weighted graph states. To our knowledge, this is the first time that fusion processes have been used to construct weighted graph states.
authors: N. Rimock, Y. Oz

articles.title: Thermodynamics Beyond Equilibrium in Coherent Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.09074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central open question in quantum thermodynamics is the identification of thermodynamic entropy away from equilibrium. Although thermodynamic entropy coincides with the von Neumann entropy for a Gibbs state at equilibrium, the thermodynamic role of quantum coherence generated during nonequilibrium evolution remains unclear. Here, we show that von Neumann entropy does not, in general, represent the thermodynamic entropy governing heat exchange in coherent nonequilibrium quantum systems. By integrating the resource theory of quantum coherence with thermodynamic principles, we develop a general framework for nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics. We identify thermodynamic entropy with the energy entropy derived from energy-measurement statistics and introduce a dynamical temperature extending the equilibrium concept to nonequilibrium states. Consequently, we obtain an exact entropy-balance relation separating the entropy flux associated with heat exchange from the coherence-loss contribution to entropy production, establishing an operational connection between quantum coherence, heat flow, and total entropy change. Unlike approaches relying on equilibrium reference states or stationary Gibbs ensembles, our framework uses instantaneous dynamical quantities and remains valid throughout transient nonequilibrium evolution. It provides consistent dynamical definitions of temperature, work, heat, and free energy. Applying the formalism to an exactly solvable open quantum system, we show that the first and second laws hold throughout transient evolution and that equilibrium thermodynamics emerges dynamically in the weak-coupling long-time limit. Our results establish a unified framework for coherent nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics and suggest opportunities for controlling heat dissipation through coherence engineering in quantum thermal technologies.
authors: Md Manirul Ali, Po-Wen Chen

articles.title: Preparing pre-established quantum correlations with pulse-level control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.20275v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present a technique for quantum state preparation in transmon qubit system that employs optimized electromagnetic pulse sequences rather than discrete quantum gates. By focusing directly on quantum correlations rather than specific target states, we optimize the pulse parameters to generate the desired entanglement structures in two and three qubits systems. The resulting protocols reproduce the characteristic entanglement properties associated with the Bell, GHZ, and W classes, reaching values of the corresponding entanglement measures consistent with these entanglement structures. The approach uses a reduced set of parameters to characterize the control pulses, thereby restricting the space explored during optimization while retaining the entanglement properties of interest.
authors: K. De La Ossa Doria, T. Merlo Vergara, D. Goyeneche

articles.title: On the emergence of quantum mechanics from stochastic processes
articles.title_zh: 量子力学从随机过程中的涌现
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.22095v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stochastic--quantum correspondence reinterprets quantum dynamics in terms of an underlying stochastic process on a configuration space. We generalize its lifting prescription, overcoming restrictions on the reachable density matrices without enlarging the configuration space or its associated Hilbert space. A compatibility relation and Kraus dictionary connect stochastic kernels to completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) maps: every finite-dimensional kernel admits a compatible lift, and these lifts collectively encompass all quantum channels as the kernels vary. We describe sufficiently regular composable CPTP dynamics through time-local Lindblad generators. We establish that every rooted quantum dynamical family admits a stochastic realizer on the same configuration space, and that a revival of configuration-space distinguishability rules out every Markovian realizer on that space. We show how the predictive information carried by off-diagonal degrees of freedom in a compatible composable lift is encoded in the continuation probabilities of a family of context-dependent stochastic processes. We also analyze physical measurement by separating active basis rotations from configuration recording. The rooted quantum probabilities alone do not enforce faithfulness in idealized recording interactions; nevertheless, we show that a faithful stochastic realizer always exists.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文通过配置空间上的底层随机过程重新解释了量子动力学，并推广了其提升方案，克服了可达密度矩阵的限制。研究建立了随机核与完全正、迹保持（CPTP）映射之间的兼容性关系和Kraus字典，表明所有量子通道都可由随机核的提升实现。工作还证明了每个量子动力学族都存在一个随机实现，并分析了对角外自由度所携带的预测信息如何编码在上下文相关随机过程的延续概率中。
authors: Jason Doukas

articles.title: Qudit Implementation of the Rodeo Algorithm for Quantum Spectral Filtering
articles.title_zh: 用于量子谱滤波的Rodeo算法的Qudit实现
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.16049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Qudits, the multi-level generalization of qubits, provide a natural extension of the binary paradigm in quantum computation and offer new opportunities to enhance algorithmic performance. Beyond their direct applicability to the simulation of multi-level quantum systems, higher-dimensional ancillae can improve sampling efficiency in quantum algorithms by enabling the simultaneous implementation of multiple control operations, thereby reducing circuit complexity. In this work, we pursue three main objectives. First, we present a formulation of the Rodeo algorithm employing a general d-level ancilla qudit. Second, we introduce the concept of the emphRodeo kernel, defined as a two-frequency interferometer, which acts as a spectral filter in the energy domain. Finally, we propose a microcanonical protocol for the Rodeo algorithm. This protocol enables the estimation of entropic quantities through a single energy sweep and admits a natural interpretation as a Gaussian convolution of the density of states. To support the theoretical analysis, we perform numerical evaluations of the corresponding quantum circuit using ancilla qudits of dimensions three, four, and five. The simulations are performed for the one-dimensional Ising model, considering both spin-sfrac12 and spin-1 particles. The ancilla qutrit implementation exhibits an 18% reduction in fluctuations compared to the qubit implementation. Our results show that qudits provide a framework for spectral analysis and thermodynamic characterization of multi-level quantum systems.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了使用d级辅助量子比特（qudit）实现Rodeo算法的方案，以增强量子算法性能。研究引入了“Rodeo核”概念，将其定义为在能量域中充当谱滤波器的双频干涉仪。此外，还提出了Rodeo算法的微正则协议，该协议通过单次能量扫描实现熵量估计，并可解释为态密度的 Gaussian 卷积。
authors: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha, Rodrigo Alves Dias

articles.title: Gradient-Based Optimization Enables Scalable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Gate Synthesis
articles.title_zh: 基于梯度的优化实现可扩展的容错量子门合成
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.25101v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a numerical approach to optimizing a quantum circuit over a discrete gate set by using gradient descent to tune R_Z angles to a solution where many R_Z gates can be rounded to a Clifford or T gate without introducing further synthesis error. Through benchmarking, we show that our approach is able to match state-of-the-art techniques for multi-qubit Clifford + T circuit synthesis, and is able to find circuits for unitaries that previous approaches fail to find solutions for. Our approach can adapt to any discrete gate set, which we demonstrate using the Clifford + T + sqrt T gate set.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种数值方法，通过梯度下降优化量子电路，调整R_Z角，使许多R_Z门可以四舍五入为Clifford或T门而不会引入额外的合成误差。基准测试表明，该方法在多量子比特Clifford + T电路合成方面与最先进技术相当，并能为先前方法无法找到解决方案的酉算子找到电路。该方法适用于任何离散门集，并在Clifford + T + sqrt T门集上进行了演示。
authors: Marc Grau Davis, Ed Younis, Mathias Weiden, Hyeongrak Choi, Dirk Englund

articles.title: Continuous-time evolution via probabilistic angle interpolation and its applications
articles.title_zh: 基于概率角度插值的连续时间演化及其应用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.02854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the applicability of a stochastic time-evolution algorithm based on probabilistic angle interpolation. To simplify the pre-processing of the algorithm, we take the continuous-time limit, thereby explicitly eliminating Trotter errors and streamlining the resource analysis. We also introduce a noise-mitigation method tailored to it. As demonstrations, we apply the algorithm to two representative problems: estimating the ground-state energy of the H₃⁺ molecular Hamiltonian and computing out-of-time-ordered correlators in the sparse Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model. We evaluate the protocol's performance through numerical simulations and experiments on a trapped-ion quantum computer, Quantinuum Reimei.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文探讨了基于概率角度插值的随机时间演化算法的适用性。通过取连续时间极限，该算法消除了Trotter误差并简化了资源分析，同时引入了定制的噪声缓解方法。研究将该算法应用于H₃⁺分子哈密顿量的基态能量估计和稀疏Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev模型中的时序关联器计算，并通过数值模拟和离子阱量子计算机实验验证了其性能。
authors: Tomoya Hayata, Yuta Kikuchi

articles.title: Tight Quantum Lower Bound for k-Distinctness
articles.title_zh: k-Distinctness问题的紧致量子下界
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.05133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new quantum query lower bound framework. It is inspired by Zhandry's compressed oracle technique, but it also subsumes the polynomial method as a special case. Compared to Zhandry's technique, our approach has two key differences. First, we do not use any oracles (except for the standard input oracle), and define ``knowledge'' directly through the expansion of the state of the algorithm in the Fourier basis. Second, we allow arbitrary probability distributions of inputs. We show how this framework behaves on the problem of finding equal elements in the input string. In particular, we demonstrate its power by proving a first tight quantum query lower bound for the k-Distinctness problem.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文引入了一个新的量子查询下界框架，该框架受Zhandry压缩预言机技术的启发，并包含多项式方法作为特例。与Zhandry技术不同，该方法不使用任何预言机（标准输入预言机除外），并通过算法状态在傅里叶基中的展开直接定义“知识”，并允许任意输入概率分布。研究展示了该框架在k-Distinctness问题上的应用，并首次证明了其紧致量子查询下界。
authors: Aleksandrs Belovs

articles.title: A Logarithmic-Depth Quantum Multiplier
articles.title_zh: 一种对数深度量子乘法器
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.09847v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for multiplying two n-bit integers with overall circuit depth and T-depth both bounded by O(łog n), while using O(n²⁾ gates and ancillary qubits. Our construction generates partial products via indicator-controlled copying and adds them using a tree of reversible 3-to-2 adders followed by one quantum carry-lookahead adder. Building on the carry-save adders of Kim et al., we combine full input fanout, workspace reuse, and phase-corrected gate implementations to reduce T-depth. We provide explicit circuit constructions, proofs of correctness, and concrete closed-form resource bounds.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种量子算法，用于乘法两个n比特整数，其总电路深度和T-深度均为O(log n)，同时使用O(n²)门和辅助量子比特。该构造通过指示器控制的复制生成部分积，并使用可逆3-to-2加法器树和量子超前进位加法器进行求和。研究提供了明确的电路构造、正确性证明和具体的封闭形式资源界限。
authors: Fred Sun, Anton Borissov

articles.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
articles.title_zh: 开放量子系统中的半经典Ehrenfest路径
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.27328v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. We first give a self-contained derivation of the Fokker--Planck equation that governs the time evolution of the mixing measure for a Gaussian mixture. Then, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture to study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究了开放量子系统中的半经典Ehrenfest轨迹。研究首先推导了高斯混合物混合测度时间演化的Fokker--Planck方程，并将开放量子系统的广义Ehrenfest定理嵌入到相空间图像中。工作展示了在无摩擦谐波区域中相干和不可逆贡献如何分离，为开放量子动力学中经典轨迹的出现提供了清晰的相空间解释。
authors: Xiao-Kan Guo

articles.title: Physics inspired quantum algorithm for QCD splitting functions
articles.title_zh: 基于物理启发的QCD分裂函数量子算法
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.06789v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a modular quantum circuit primitive to model entanglement dynamics in QCD parton splitting and use it as a composable building block for data-driven, physics-consistent modelling of parton-shower kinematics. For the pure-gluon channel, we derive an analytic expression for the helicity entanglement generated at the splitting vertex, quantified via the concurrence, and construct a two-qubit circuit whose σ₃ expectation values encode the momentum shared between outgoing gluons. The circuit reproduces the QCD-predicted concurrence by construction, which fixes a two-qubit correlator that the momentum fractions alone do not determine. Iterating the primitive, the concurrence obeys a product rule across successive splittings. Calibrating the circuit parameters to LHC jet substructure data relates the reconstructed momentum-sharing fractions directly to circuit rotation angles. Composing multiple splitting primitives yields multi-prong momentum-fraction distributions; we compare the three- and four-prong cases against experimental data, reproducing the core of the distributions. For the three-prong configuration, we execute the circuit on superconducting quantum hardware, recover the momentum-fraction distributions after a device-bias correction calibrated on a held-out subset, and study how noise alters the entanglement-dependent observable. This work provides a concrete framework for quantum-native parton-shower modules that encode quantum correlations at the level of splitting dynamics, and offers physics-informed ansätze for future quantum algorithms for QCD.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文引入了一种模块化量子电路原语，用于模拟QCD部分子分裂中的纠缠动力学，并将其作为可组合的构建块，用于数据驱动、物理一致的部分子簇射运动学建模。研究推导了纯胶子通道中螺旋度纠缠的解析表达式，并构建了一个双量子比特电路，其σ₃期望值编码了出射胶子之间的动量共享。该电路通过与LHC喷注子结构数据校准，成功再现了三叉和四叉动量分数分布的核心特征。
authors: Gabriel Rouxinol, Yacine Haddad, Cenk Tüysüz, Sofia Vallecorsa, Michele Grossi

articles.title: Degree-Guided Adiabatic Quantum Algorithm for MIS with Neutral Atoms
articles.title_zh: 基于度引导的绝热量子算法在MIS问题中的中性原子应用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.16944v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum adiabatic algorithm for solving MIS with Rydberg atoms, which uses graph degrees to engineer the Hamiltonian for adiabatic evolution. Our approach extends the algorithm of Pichler et al. for MIS state preparation, which uses time-dependent global controls to excite atoms while the Rydberg blockade mechanism suppresses adjacent excitations. To accelerate adiabatic evolution, we introduce local light shifts that favor excitation of low-degree nodes and constrain the final Hamiltonian so that energy scales inversely with the number of Rydberg excitations, preventing convergence to non-MIS states. Benchmarking our degree-dependent MIS algorithm with the traditional adiabatic algorithm on a set of 1000 MIS instances, we demonstrate numerically that our algorithm inflates the minimal spectral gap and, consequently, accelerates the convergence. By fitting power-law relations for both the time-to-solution and success probability metrics as a function of the hardness parameter, we demonstrate a superior scaling exponent for our algorithm over the traditional global protocol. Furthermore, the classical Hamiltonian engineering step required to construct degree-dependent controls introduces only polynomial overhead. These results indicate that our algorithm can be used to extend the size of graphs for which MIS can be found on physical hardware. Moreover, our approach extends beyond MIS to additional graph problems such as MAX-CUT.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一种利用Rydberg原子解决最大独立集（MIS）问题的量子绝热算法，该算法通过图的度数来设计绝热演化的哈密顿量。研究引入了局部光移，以加速绝热演化并防止收敛到非MIS状态。数值基准测试表明，该算法能增大最小谱隙并加速收敛，在时间-解和成功概率指标上均表现出优于传统全局协议的标度指数。
authors: Guy Karni, Noam Cohen, Adi Pick

articles.title: Sideband fingerprints of antibunched light in cascaded quantum wave mixing
articles.title_zh: 级联量子混频中反聚束光的边带指纹
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.25828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum wave mixing on a single superconducting qubit produces a hierarchy of coherent side peaks associated with elastic multiphoton scattering pathways. In a cascaded source--probe geometry these pathways become sensitive to the photon statistics of the radiation emitted by the source qubit. We develop an analytical theory of this effect starting from the cascaded master equation in the weak-driving regime. In the coherent-filtering limit when the decay rate of the probe qubit is less than that of the source, the standard coherent--coherent wave-mixing hierarchy is recovered. In the opposite limit, side peaks associated with multiphoton absorption from the antibunched source field are parametrically suppressed. Numerical solutions confirm the analytical scaling laws. The resulting sideband hierarchy provides a frequency-domain fingerprint of antibunched itinerant microwave light.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究了级联源-探测几何中量子混频产生的相干边峰，这些边峰对源量子比特辐射的光子统计敏感。研究从弱驱动状态下的级联主方程出发，发展了该效应的分析理论。结果表明，当探测量子比特的衰减率小于源量子比特时，恢复了标准的相干-相干混频层次结构；而在相反的极限下，与反聚束源场多光子吸收相关的边峰被参数抑制。
authors: R. D. Ivanovskikh, W. V. Pogosov, A. A. Elistratov, A. Yu. Dmitriev, T. R. Sabirov, A. V. Vasenin, S. A. Gunin, O. V. Astafiev

articles.title: Quantum geometry of connected state manifolds: When diabolic points act as bridges between eigenstate manifolds
articles.title_zh: 连通态流形的量子几何：当魔点充当本征态流形之间的桥梁时
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.28351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric Hamiltonians often exhibit point-like spectral degeneracies, called diabolic points (DPs) or conical intersections, which can lead to singularities in the Provost-Vallee metric of eigenstate manifolds. We regularise the metric by a transformation to polar coordinates and develop a formalism in which DPs act as bridges between adjacent eigenstate manifolds, glueing them into a single connected state manifold (CSM). We characterise the topology of this structure and extend the local rules for nodal lines governing the Berry phase to global ones. On the CSM, the class of geodesics can be enlarged by those passing through the DPs. They can be stable with respect to their initial direction, and can be shorter than those constrained to a single eigenstate manifold, providing new geodesic shortcuts. Further, the CSM provides a new mechanism for Berry phase computation along paths traversing the DPs.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究了参数哈密顿量中的魔点（DPs），它们可能导致本征态流形度量的奇异性。研究通过坐标变换对度量进行正则化，并发展了一种形式主义，其中DPs充当相邻本征态流形之间的桥梁，将它们连接成一个单一的连通态流形（CSM）。工作表征了这种结构的拓扑，并扩展了控制Berry相位的节点线局部规则到全局规则，揭示了CSM为Berry相计算提供了新机制。
authors: Jan Střeleček, Jakub Novotný, Pavel Cejnar

articles.title: Counterdiabatic Raman Atom Optics for Compact High-Sensitivity Gravimetry
articles.title_zh: 用于紧凑型高灵敏度重力测量的反绝热拉曼原子光学
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.16945v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large-momentum-transfer (LMT) atom interferometry provides a route toward enhanced inertial sensitivity in compact quantum sensors, but its scalability is limited by the accumulation of pulse-transfer errors across long Raman pulse sequences. We investigate theoretically the use of stimulated Raman shortcut-to-adiabatic passage (STIRSAP) for high-fidelity LMT atom optics in a Mach--Zehnder interferometer geometry. The counterdiabatic correction is encoded directly into the Raman pulse envelopes, eliminating the need for auxiliary microwave or radio-frequency control fields. Numerical simulations based on an effective Raman model show that 1~μs STIRSAP pulses achieve single-pulse transfer fidelities of F_π = 0.99902 while maintaining negligible pulse-time overhead even at high momentum order. We analyze the resulting tradeoff between interferometric phase enhancement and compound contrast decay and identify an unconstrained shot-noise optimum near napprox270. The analysis further shows that practical operation at extreme LMT order is constrained by wave-packet separation, vibration noise, Doppler detuning, and accumulated systematic effects rather than by pulse duration itself. These results establish superadiabatic Raman control as a promising approach for scalable high-fidelity atom optics and clarify the physical limitations governing compact high-order atom interferometers.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文理论研究了在马赫-曾德尔干涉仪几何中，利用受激拉曼绝热捷径（STIRSAP）实现高保真大动量转移（LMT）原子光学。反绝热校正直接编码在拉曼脉冲包络中，无需辅助微波或射频控制场。数值模拟表明，1微秒的STIRSAP脉冲实现了高单脉冲转移保真度，同时在高动量阶下保持可忽略的脉冲时间开销。研究分析了干涉相位增强与复合对比度衰减之间的权衡，并指出了实际操作在高LMT阶下受到的限制。
authors: Asad Ali, Hamid Arian Zad, Saif Al-Kuwari, Muhammad Irtiza Hussain, Muhammad Talha Rahim, Hashir Kuniyil, Tim Byrnes, James Q. Quach, Saeed Haddadi

articles.title: Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Herbertsmithite (ZnCu₃₍OH)₆Cl₂₎ is one of the most extensively studied quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidates, yet the precise nature of its ground state remains unresolved. Here, we compare the results of high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of herbertsmithite (ZnₓCu₄₋ₓ₍OD)₆Cl₂, xsimeq 0.85) with large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and dynamical DMRG simulations to benchmark the spin Hamiltonian and uncover fundamental properties of the ground state. The measured spin correlations determine an energy density for the Heisenberg model that closely matches simulations, an essential verification of the Hamiltonian. In parallel, DMRG simulations reveal two nearly degenerate QSL states. Both preserve translational symmetry, but one retains the lattice point-group symmetries whereas the other develops anisotropic spin correlations that break point-group symmetry. These two QSLs have distinct spin structure factors, and, remarkably, close agreement with the neutron spectra is achieved with an admixture of the two states. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between neutron scattering and simulations, and suggest that herbertsmithite realizes a regime in which two proximate gapped QSL states coexist.
authors: Arthur C. Campello, Shengtao Jiang, Wei He, Jiajia Wen, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Steven A. Kivelson, Hong-Chen Jiang, Young S. Lee

articles.title: Charge disproportionation and spin ordering in LiV₂O₅ and NaV₂O₅: a distributed moment point of view
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effects of charge disproportionation between V⁴⁺ and V⁵⁺ on the exchange interactions and related magnetic, electronic and optical properties are studied in LiV₂O₅ and NaV₂O₅. The magnetic exchange interactions between local moments on atomic sites are calculated using a linear response approach based on the QSGW band structure. While the induced magnetic moments are small on the vanadyl Oᵥ and bridge O_b, their exchange interactions with the V are found to be larger than between V atoms. The Néel temperature T_N are calculated within the mean-field (MFA) and random phase (RPA) approximations for two different crystal structures with P2₁ₘₙ and Pmmn spacegroups. The critical temperatures are are corrected by a quantum statistical factor of (S+1)/S to obtain reasonable agreement with experiment. Band structures, optical dielectric functions calculated using the Bethe Salpeter Equation method and spin waves are also calculated and presented for both crystal structures and both compounds. The spin wave dispersions are calculated from the classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian including magnetic moments on both V and O atoms. Besides the lowest energy weakly interacting spin waves of the two chains of spins in the unit cell, the model predicts additional high energy optical spin waves, which correspond to more complex spin excitations in which the spins on the two V across a bridge, vanadyl O and bridge O precess independently from each other instead of staying locked together according to their collinear alignment in the ground state. These show only weak dispersion and extend up to about 1 eV but we argue that these are an artefact of using the Heisenberg model beyond its validity range and would be suppressed in a more complete theory that allows for coupling of the transverse spin with longitudinal spin and charge excitations.
authors: Claudio Garcia, Ilteris K. Turan, Jerome Jackson, Swagata Acharya, Mark van Schilfgaarde, Walter R. L. Lambrecht

articles.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for a Nanothermometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The steady-state temperature predicted for an ideal point heat source diverges in conventional heat-conduction theory, but no physical thermometer measures a point value. We derive a sharp, shape-independent upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor with thermometric volume Vₛ, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound requires only the total heat power generated in the region dotQ, a lower bound on its thermal conductivity κₘ, and the value of Vₛ. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source--sensor distance. For dotQ=50~pW, κₘ = 0.1~mathrmW,m⁻¹K⁻¹, and Vₛ₌₁₀⁻²²,m³, approximately the volume of a 60~nm-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately 2~mK above the reference level. The result applies directly to nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer particles, and core-shell quantum dots. It shows that neither source localization nor uncertain source-sensor separation can account for kelvin-scale readings under steady-state heat conduction.
authors: Taras Plakhotnik

articles.title: Spontaneous particle-hole symmetry breaking in a disordered two-site quantum breakdown model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spontaneous particle-hole symmetry breaking in a disordered two-site quantum breakdown model. The model is solvable in the limit of a large number of fermionic modes on each site. For a small ratio of the numbers of modes on the two sites, we derive the free energy analytically and find a finite-temperature symmetry-breaking transition. This transition changes from continuous to first order as the number of fermions produced in each conversion increases. Numerical results show that both types of transition persist beyond this regime, with an order-parameter exponent close to 1/2 for continuous transitions.
authors: Kinya Guan

articles.title: Scaling Dimensions and Two-Point Amplitudes from Operator Covariance Matrices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The long distance behavior of two-point functions of critical lattice statistical mechanics models depend on detailed information of the underlying quantum field theory. Yet these universal properties can be difficult to extract because generic lattice operators couple to the infinite hierarchy of continuum scaling operators with unknown coefficients. Recently in Physical Review E 114, 024146 (2026), one approach to disentangle some of this information was proposed using the eigen-decomposition of the operator covariance matrix constructed from cross correlations of a finite set of Nₑₗₗ lattice operators. In this work we analyze this method in detail. We provide an explicit proof that under the assumption of scale invariance the leading decay of the eigenvalues are controlled by the smallest Nₑₗₗ scaling dimensions, even after taking irrelevant perturbations into account. Based on this understanding, we propose a new method by which the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix can be used to construct the amplitudes of the continuum two-point correlation functions. This allows for a complete determination of the structure of the continuum two-point functions from the lattice covariance matrix. We demonstrate our ideas both on synthetic data sets (drawn from the scaling hypothesis) and numerically exact data for the two dimensional Ising model.
authors: You-Chiuan Chen, Ribhu K. Kaul

articles.title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting (SC₁₎, and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
authors: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

articles.title: Self-Trapping and Liouvillian Spectral Transitions in a Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Dimer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.25222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the self-trapping transition in dissipative double wells using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization. We find that, similar to the conventional interaction-driven transition from oscillatory dynamics to self-trapping, dissipation alone can also induce self-trapping-like localization in one well. The resulting state, although transient and decaying, persists for a substantial time. At the mean-field level, the interaction- and dissipation-driven transitions are discontinuous and continuous, respectively. When interaction and dissipation both are present, their interplay produces three dynamical regimes: (i) at weak interaction, increasing dissipation drives a transition from oscillations to self-trapping; (ii) at moderate interaction, self-trapping at weak dissipation, oscillatory dynamics at intermediate dissipation, and re-entrant self-trapping at strong dissipation; and (iii) at strong interaction, self-trapping persists but is weakened by dissipation. We connect the transition with the Liouvillian spectrum. It is observed that purely dissipation-driven transition coincides with an exceptional point in the spectra, and a peak in the Liouvillian gap, marking the onset of the quantum-Zeno regime. In the presence of interactions, however, the onset of the Zeno regime is shifted to dissipation strengths larger than that required for the self-trapping transition.
authors: Subhendu Saha, Raka Dasgupta

articles.title: Phase engineering of odd parity state in a quantum dot Josephson junction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Controlling fermion parity in quantum-dot Josephson junctions (QDJJs) enables access to novel superconducting physics. While parity transitions are usually tuned electrically, we study phase-induced transitions in a strongly coupled QDJJ using the superconducting phase difference across the dot terminals, denoted by φ. We find that this phase allows control over the ground state parity, with parity transitions observed as the Andreev bound states (ABSs) energies crossing zero. These crossings occur near φ = π, and their behavior is in good correspondence to a simple model considering a single-level quantum dot proximitized by a superconductor. These results place phase-controlled QDJJ arrays as a promising platform for exploring exotic phenomena such as Majorana zero modes.
authors: Shohei Kobayashi, Tyler Lindemann, Sergei Gronin, Geoffrey Gardner, Peter Stano, Daniel Loss, Michael Manfra, Seigo Tarucha, Sadashige Matsuo

articles.title: Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly believed that a bulk photovoltaic current requires broken spatial inversion symmetry. However, in this work, we demonstrate that dc photocurrents can arise in centrosymmetric solids from the bilinear coupling between the electric and magnetic components of light. This magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect (MBPE) has a quantum-geometric origin in the dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature. We identify four distinct MBPE mechanisms, including time-reversal-even and time-reversal-odd injection-like and shift-like photocurrents driven by linearly or circularly polarized light. Our symmetry analysis shows that the MBPE is allowed in broad classes of two-dimensional centrosymmetric nonmagnetic and magnetic materials under normally incident light. As representative examples, we predict sizable MBPEs in centrosymmetric monolayer Pt₂HgSe₃ and altermagnetic RuF₄, with current densities on the order of 1~mA/m. Notably, the injection-like photocurrent in RuF₄ reverses sign upon switching either the light helicity or the Néel vector. Our results extend the bulk photovoltaic effect to centrosymmetric solids and open new opportunities for electrical readout of altermagnetic order.
authors: Longjun Xiang, Fuming Xu, Lei Zhang, Jian Wang

articles.title: Hidden piezo-Hall effect
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extensive studies of hidden spin polarization have established a broad class of hidden phenomena in quantum materials. Here, we introduce the hidden piezo-Hall effect, in which strain induces finite anomalous Hall conductivities (AHCs) in individual sectors while the global AHC remains zero. At zero strain, neither the full system nor its sectors exhibit an anomalous Hall effect (AHE). Under uniaxial strain, however, opposite sector AHCs emerge while their sum remains canceled. We establish this effect for a d-wave hidden altermagnet using a tight-binding model and first-principles calculations for the experimentally synthesized material RbV₂Te₂O. Rotating the strain direction from the x to the y axis reverses the signs of the sector AHCs without generating a net Hall response. The same symmetry mechanism may also give rise to hidden piezomagneto-optical, piezo-thermal Hall, piezo-Nernst, and piezo-Ettingshausen effects. Our work extends hidden physics to strain-controlled transport and identifies RbV₂Te₂O as a promising candidate for experimental verification.
authors: San-Dong Guo, Shi-Hao Zhang, Bingwen Zhang

articles.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Discovery of Carbon-Related Defect Formation Mechanisms in Diamond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diamond is an important host material for functional defects such as solid-state spin qubits. During the defect creation by irradiation and subsequent thermal annealing, carbon-related defects, including vacancies and interstitials, are generated and can migrate to form new defect complexes. To investigate this kinetically driven process and reveal the formation mechanisms of the di-interstitials and di-vacancies in the neutral charge state, we fine-tuned a universal machine learning interatomic potential using a small dataset generated from density functional theory calculations. We obtained a barrier of 1.84 eV for mono-interstitial migration and found that two initially separated mono-interstitials only need to overcome a lower barrier to form di-interstitial configurations. Beyond the training data, the MLIP also identified the formation pathway for an additional di-interstitial configuration and a stepwise divacancy dissociation mechanism. These results reveal migration-assisted defect complex formation mechanisms and demonstrate how targeted MLIP training can identify reaction pathways.
authors: Grace Huang, Christopher Fivecoat, Xun Xu, Mengen Wang

articles.title: Two-Dimensional Quantum Droplets in a Mixture of Bose-Einstein Condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum droplets represent a striking manifestation of beyond-mean-field physics, with properties that depend sensitively on dimensionality. Although quantum droplets have been experimentally realized in one and three dimensions, their realization in two dimensions has remained elusive. Here, we observe the formation of a two-dimensional (2D) quantum droplet in a quasi-2D geometry by transferring the single-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) into a spin mixture in the Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) regime, where the LHY effect evidently deviates from its three-dimensional form. We find that, in our scheme, 2D quantum droplets are more stable and exhibit longer lifetimes than previously reported quantum droplets. By instead transferring the initial BECs into another single-spin state with a negative scattering length, we generate 2D Townes solitons. A comparison between the two types of self-bound states shows that, whereas 2D Townes solitons are stable only near a critical atom number determined by the scattering length, 2D quantum droplets remain well-defined and self-bound over a much broader parameter range. These realizations of quantum droplets and Townes solitons in two dimensions provide new insights into self-bound states and open new avenues for exploring nonlinear dynamics in quantum liquids.
authors: Yue Zhang, Liangchao Chen, Wei Han, Linshan Gong, Yazhou Wang, Zekui Wang, Xinhao Liang, Wenjie Sui, Pengjun Wang, Lianghui Huang, Zengming Meng, Zhuxiong Ye, Jing Zhang

articles.title: Strain-induced disorder from Schottky gates on high mobility 2DEGs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrostatic gates on two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs) in GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures are essential for numerous studies of correlation driven phenomena, many performed within the fractional quantum Hall effect. However, the most commonly used type of gates, the metallic Schottky gate, has the propensity to adversely impact the electron mobility and suppress the fractional quantum Hall states. Here we demonstrate through commensurability oscillations under specially designed nanostructured superlattice gates, that strain effects are responsible for the mobility reduction. The experimental results agree well with COMSOL Multiphysics simulations. In a regular, unpatterned gate the disordered, granular nature of the metal film fills the same role as the superlattice in creating a strain field penetrating down to the 2DEG, as we show with a simplified model. These results will help in understanding, improving and finding novel methods to reduce strain-induced disorder in gated high-mobility 2DEGs.
authors: Sambit Mohapatra, Lukas Berg, Jean-Baptiste Cuvellier, Yan Sun, Abdelhanin Aassime, Alan Durnez, Antonella Cavanna, Dominique Mailly, Ulf Gennser

articles.title: Variational Block Correlated Coupled Cluster Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.26646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the recent success of quantum neural states, we present a variational implementation of the coupled cluster method suitable for quantum Monte Carlo simulations. We introduce a Young tableaux representation of the wave-function coefficients and their derivatives that substantially reduces the computational complexity of the variational optimization. While the algorithm is generic, we illustrate its implementation with an application to the Heisenberg model in one and two dimensions, using the block correlated coupled cluster ansatz (BCCC) with doubles and triples. Convergence is greatly improved by means of importance sampling based on a fictitious temperature. The resulting approach achieves competitive accuracy while providing a scalable framework for variational coupled-cluster calculations.
authors: Hunter Brodie, Alexander Shilcusky, Adrian E. Feiguin

articles.title: Absorbing state transitions with long-range annihilation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2409.03280v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a family of classical stochastic processes describing diffusive particles undergoing branching and long-range annihilation in the presence of a parity constraint. The probability for a pair-annihilation event decays as a power-law in the distance between particles, with a tunable exponent. Such long-range processes arise naturally in various classical settings, and increasingly play a role in the study of quantum dynamics: for example, quantum state preparation or error correction processes aim to prepare ordered ground states, which requires removing point-like excitations in pairs via non-local feedback operations conditioned on a global set of measurement outcomes. We analytically and numerically describe features of absorbing phases and phase transitions in this family of classical models as pairwise annihilation is performed at larger and larger distances. Notably, we find that the two canonical absorbing-state universality classes -- directed-percolation and parity-conserving -- are endpoints of a new line of universality classes with continuously varying critical exponents. These new classes follow from an interplay of long-range interactions and symmetries: decreasing the long-range exponent effectively weakens the local effects of global symmetry constraints. This competition significantly broadens known non-equilibrium phases and phase transitions.
authors: Nicholas O'Dea, Sayak Bhattacharjee, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Vedika Khemani

articles.title: Quantum Geometric Injection and Shift Optical Forces Drive Coherent Phonons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.17814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a gauge-invariant quantum-geometric theory of light-induced Raman forces driving coherent lattice dynamics in solids. We show that the resonant interband response separates into injection and shift forces, providing the lattice analogue of injection and shift photocurrents. Crucially, the electronic quantum metric and Berry curvature directly govern these forces, weighted by distinct electron--phonon quantities. The injection force is controlled by the quantum geometric tensor and differences between band-diagonal electron--phonon couplings, producing the resonant displacive response. The shift force is a resonant impulsive response governed by quantum geometry and a phononic shift vector arising from interband electron--phonon coherence. We derive polarization selection rules, symmetry constraints, and temporal signatures. Applied to interlayer shear phonons in a bilayer Haldane model, the theory predicts tunability with optical frequency, topology, electronic temperature, and current-induced symmetry breaking. These results establish a quantum-geometric framework for coherent lattice dynamics and identify coherent phonons as experimentally accessible signatures of electronic quantum geometry in quantum materials.
authors: J. Luke Pimlott, Habib Rostami

articles.title: Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points and beyond of far-from-equilibrium dilute system: ultra-cold Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2508.18821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The far-from-equilibrium dynamics driven by the scattering from next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections in the quantum field theory has stationary solutions for the particle distribution characterized as the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points corresponding to scale-invariant particle/energy flux. The dynamics of the spatially homogeneous dilute ultra-cold Fermi gas is investigated, and its kinetic equation confirms the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points in the perturbation theory by the quasi-particle assumption, in contrast to the wave turbulence of the ultra-cold Bose gas. In addition, other stationary states are discussed when the the vertex correction becomes significant in the kinetic equation. It is found that conditions for the scale-invariant flux in this case no longer hold when the quasi-particle assumption is applied.
authors: Chun-Wei Su

articles.title: Linear Ensemble-Constrained Quantum Monte Carlo: From Dilute Fermi Gas to Flat-Band Ferromagnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.08552v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a finite-temperature canonical-ensemble determinant quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that enforces an exact fermion number and enables numerically stable simulations of correlated lattice fermions. We propose a stabilized QR update that reduces the computational complexity from standard cubic scaling O(β N³⁾ to linear scaling O(β N Nₑ²⁾ with respect to the system size N, where Nₑ is the particle number. This yields a dramatic speedup in dilute regimes (Nₑ łl N), opening unbiased access to large-scale simulations of strongly correlated low-density phases. We validate the method on the dilute Fermi gas with onsite Hubbard interactions, observing the suppression of the fermion sign problem in the dilute limit. Furthermore, we apply this approach to a one-dimensional flat-band system, where the canonical ensemble allows for precise control over filling. We reveal a ferromagnetic instability at low temperatures in the half-filling regime. Our linear-scaling approach provides a powerful tool for investigating emergent phenomena in dilute quantum matter.
authors: Tu Hong, Kun Chen, Xiao Yan Xu

articles.title: Scattering Measures and Information Geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.34721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate scattering experiments in terms of parameterized finite measures on outcome spaces and develop the associated information geometry defined by the Fisher metric. The decomposition of a scattering measure into total mass and normalized shape separates Fisher information into contributions from changes in overall scattering strength and redistribution among outcomes. Measurement processes are represented by probability or sub-probability kernels acting on the scattering measure. Such kernels contract Fisher information, placing a broad class of experimental operations within a common information-theoretic framework. This formulation connects scattering experiments to the theory of optimal experimental design through the Fisher geometry of scattering measures. The same finite-measure structure arises naturally in quantum measurements with incomplete detection, clarifying its place in the hierarchy from quantum measurement to classical outcome statistics.
authors: Tatsuro Oda

articles.title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.24025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on A(n,6,w) in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: A(27,6,11)ge 19305, A(27,6,12)ge 24453, A(28,6,10)ge 18642 and A(28,6,9)ge 11154, together with an explicit A(24,6,12) code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: A(29,6,10)ge 27183, A(29,6,11)ge 42042, A(29,6,9)ge 14781, A(28,6,10)ge 19110, A(27,6,12)ge 24804, A(28,6,9)ge 11388 and A(27,6,13)ge 27783, three of which replace first-round values. Every code is a union of orbits of the semilinear affine group AΓ L(1,27), its index-2 subgroup, or AGL(1,23), acting on all but at most two coordinates. The orbits were chosen by maximum-weight independent set search on the orbit conflict graph: branch and bound in the first round, iterated local search in the second. Each code was checked by two separately written programs over all pairs of words and was regenerated from its generators and orbit representatives. We also report two qubit stabilizer codes, [[20,11,4]] and [[43,32,4]], which raise the lower bounds of 3 listed at codetables.de to the listed upper bound 4.
authors: Chris Dzoba

articles.title: Insertion Correcting Capability for Quantum Deletion-Correcting Codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.20635v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is conjectured that a quantum code C corrects t deletion errors if and only if C corrects a total of t insertion and deletion errors. Although this conjecture has been proved only under certain conditions, it has not been proved in general. In this paper, we prove this conjecture for general quantum codes. Specifically, we show that a quantum state after an insertion error is represented as a product state of the original multi-qudit system and the inserted quantum state. Then, we prove this conjecture by combining the previous results and this property. In addition, we define generalized insertion errors by removing the quantum channel requirement from insertion errors and present their properties.

articles.title_zh: 在量子处理器上探索超越朗道理论的量子相变
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文利用超导量子处理器，研究了受挫一维自旋链中朗道理论所禁止的铁磁-价键固体（FM-VBS）相变。研究结合矩阵乘积态辅助电路制备和量子硬件测量，揭示了长程铁磁关联的抑制以及竞争序涨落的重新分布。结果为探测超越传统朗道理论的竞争序、临界关联和多体动力学提供了一个通用的量子硬件框架。
authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee

articles.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
articles.title_zh: 驱动里德堡链中的共振对产生与平带熔化
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning Δ(t) and Rabi frequency Ømega(t) at frequencies ømega₁ and ømega₂₌ν ømega₁ respectively with ν in Z. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for |m̊ vacångle (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), |mathbb Z₂ångle, and |mathbb Z₃ångle (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that |m̊ vacångle shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while |mathbb Z₃ångle exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the |mathbb Z₂ångle initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with |mathbb Z₃ångle state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究了在双音周期驱动下的里德堡链，并利用含时Schrieffer-Wolff变换确定了PXP动力学的有效范围。研究发现，在强但有限的阻塞强度下，平带熔化存在两种机制：一是涉及最近邻里德堡激发对共振产生的多体共振，二是涉及访问中间态的虚过程。分析结果与有限链上的精确对角化结果一致。
authors: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta

articles.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
articles.title_zh: 可编程制备拓扑纠缠态
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文通过逆向工程集成光子晶格的非线性光学泵浦剖面，实现了拓扑纠缠态的可编程制备。该方法能够确定性地控制所生成纠缠态的维度和模态结构，同时保持其拓扑特性。研究在硅光子拓扑超晶格中实验验证了这一方法，展示了通过定制激发实现非线性生成路径的可编程性。
authors: M. Javad Zakeri, Alaric Pan, Darren D Hudson, Andrea Blanco-Redondo

articles.title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
articles.title_zh: 私有同步量子消息中的具体函数：量子优势与结构限制
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on n-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' n-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication (1.633łdots)n qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least 3n qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication 3łog₂ 3. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every k≥ 3, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for k-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most k per player, and hence at most kłog₂ k qubits in total.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文研究了私有同步量子消息（PSQM）中具体函数的通信复杂度，揭示了量子优势和结构限制。对于三方n比特相等性问题，构建了一种纠缠辅助协议，渐近通信量为(1.633...)n量子比特，显著优于无预先纠缠的经典协议。研究还发现，对于某些函数，如三比特AND，在特定条件下无法实现完美正确和完美隐私的协议，但增加局部维度可以克服这一障碍。
authors: Harumichi Nishimura

articles.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in the Extended Agassi Model
articles.title_zh: 扩展Agassi模型中的非平衡动力学量子相变
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in the extended Agassi model following sudden quenches of same level pairing (Σ), monopole-monopole (ḩi) and cross level pairing (Łambda) strengths. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics through the Loschmidt echo and intensive return-rate function. Quenches across equilibrium phase boundaries produce cusp-like structures in the return rate that shows non-analyticities with increasing system size. Equilibrium finite size to large scaling identifies the ḩi-driven transition as a second order phase transition similar to mean-field, Dicke, and Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) models critical behaviour with the exponent of the order parameter β simeq 1/2, while the Σ- and Łambda-driven transitions are first order. We further characterize the associated dynamical singularities through a local scaling exponent α, with α_ḩi simeq 2/3, α_Łambda simeq 1/3, and α_Σ simeq 3/2 of all three parameters. The distinct scaling behaviours across the parameter channels show that dynamical criticality is not determined solely by the equilibrium order of the transition, revealing multiple dynamical scaling regimes. These non-analyticities are associated with the Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude, which cross the real time axis at critical times and the time derivatives of the return-rate function to characterize the order of DQPTs within the extended Agassi model.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文通过精确对角化方法，研究了扩展Agassi模型中在突然淬火后出现的动力学量子相变（DQPTs）。研究发现，跨越平衡相边界的淬火会在返回率函数中产生尖峰结构，并随系统尺寸增加呈现非解析性。结果表明，动力学临界性并非完全由平衡相变的阶数决定，而是与参数通道的独特标度行为相关。
authors: Ritesh Kumar Palai, Rajiv Kumar, Venktesh Singh, Sunil K. Mishra

articles.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
articles.title_zh: 耗散算符非可逆对称性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong Z₂ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global Rényi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文提出了一个通用的Liouville空间对偶框架，将希尔伯特空间中的非可逆对偶性扩展到开放量子系统。该框架在自对偶点处形成精确对称性，并将Liouvillian与对偶哈密顿量和耗散参数联系起来。研究将此框架应用于周期性横场Ising链，揭示了Kramers-Wannier缺陷在自对偶时对Liouvillian Jordan块施加的动量分辨选择规则。
authors: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen

articles.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
articles.title_zh: 囚禁离子玻色子运动模式间的指数SWAP门
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文实验实现了囚禁离子两个玻色子运动模式之间的指数SWAP（eSWAP）门，该门能生成恒等操作和SWAP操作的相干叠加，并具有连续可调的振幅。通过测量不同输入态的联合特征函数切片，验证了该门的性能并展示了对恒等-SWAP叠加的连续控制。这项实现为混合量子比特-玻色子量子信息处理提供了一种可调谐的相互作用。
authors: E. J. W. Koh, Rongjie Zhang, Dzmitry Matsukevich

articles.title: Quantum Sensitivity of N-Component Cat States
articles.title_zh: N分量猫态的量子灵敏度
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend our previous study of squeezed two-component Schrödinger cat states to a phase-referenced single-mode family with an arbitrary number N of coherent components and general relative phases. Within the established circular-state construction, we derive a closed complex overlap kernel for the ordered action of displacement, phase rotation, and squeezing, retaining exact finite-amplitude normalization. We distinguish finite-displacement orthogonality from local phase-estimation sensitivity quantified by quantum Fisher information (QFI). For equal-phase states, we compare N=2,łdots,9 at a common mean photon number and include coherent-state and squeezed-vacuum benchmarks. A bound on the higher photon-number sectors establishes the fixed-energy asymptote FQ,N=4bar n(N-bar n)+o(1). Its leading term agrees with the known QFI of a vacuum--N-photon superposition. The resulting decrease of the ideal local quantum Cramér--Rao bound does not establish unlimited attainable precision: prior phase information, sample size, phase-reference resources, optical loss, state preparation, and measurement choice remain relevant.
articles.abstract_zh: 本文将之前对压缩两分量薛定谔猫态的研究扩展到具有任意N个相干分量和一般相对相位的单模家族。研究推导了一个封闭的复数重叠核，用于位移、相位旋转和压缩的有序作用，并保持精确的有限振幅归一化。通过量子Fisher信息（QFI）量化了局部相位估计灵敏度，并比较了不同N值下的性能。
authors: Ranjit Singh, Alexander E. Teretenkov

articles.title: Quantum Circuits for Variable-Coefficient Vlasov Dynamics via Schrödingerisation
articles.title_zh: 通过薛定谔化实现变系数Vlasov动力学的量子电路
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.23405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional Vlasov equations present promising use cases for quantum simulation, but their transport coefficients must be implemented coherently in order to preserve a compact quantum representation.
